quests/quest:gww:64591/sections/objectiv.text: Defeat your final opponent to claim victory in the Norn fighting tournament.
See Magni the Bison for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:64591/sections/rewards-.text: Note: This reward is actually first mentioned in Round 1: Fight!, the start of this quest chain.

quests/quest:gww:64591/sections/notes-1/.text: Until you win the Norn Fighting Tournament for the first time, you will instead have Final Round: Fight! as your final round instead of this quest.

The opponent for the final round, or round 6, is usually Magni the Bison. Rarely, Palawa Joko with two Minions of Joko may appear instead of Magni. Please refer to the Norn Fighting Tournament article for details on their skill sets.
This quest is automatically accepted upon completing the preceding quest (that is, winning the round 5 of the tournament).

quests/quest:gww:64591/sections/support-.text: Your character must have the quest Round 1: Fight! in order to enter the tournament. Obtain the quest from Magni the Bison if this is the first time your character is entering the tournament or is re-entering the tournament after previously winning the tournament. Losing the tournament will keep that quest in your quest log. Talk to Gellir Frostshield to start the tournament. A fee of 100gold is automatically deducted from your character upon confirmation.
Rules

There are six consecutive rounds that you must win in total to be considered the winner of the tournament. In the first five rounds, an opponent is randomly selected from a subset of those listed below, i.e. each opponent can appear in only a particular round so that each round has a different set of potential foes. In the sixth round, your opponent will be Magni the Bison (although, in extremely rare cases, you might face Palawa Joko during Final Round, Championship Edition: Fight!).

The tournament takes place in a small explorable area designed as an arena. Each of the 6 rounds of battle (5 random opponents and the final round) takes place in a different instance of the area. Your character starts each round in a side room. The door to the battle chamber is locked for 10 seconds; when the timer ends, the door opens and your previously neutral opponent turns hostile. However, you will not aggro your foe until you step out of the side-door, giving you extra time to cast enchantments or preparations. When you leave the side room, the door will close behind you and you must kill or be killed.
Rewards
Upon winning the final round for the first time, you receive:
150 Norn Reputation Points
A Touch of Guile
"Dodge This!"
"Finish Him!"
The Bison Cup
Repeated completions of the tournament reward one Bison Championship Token each.
Winning the first five rounds award Norn reputation points to characters with a Norn rank of less than eight: 5 → 10 → 15 → 20 → 25 (for a total of 75 points).
One-time rewards
Defeating Xandra and Kahmu will unlock them as heroes.
After defeating Zho for the first time, you will receive Zho's Journal, which is required to obtain the Black Moa Chick.
The first time you defeat the Great Zehtuka with Zehtuka's Great Horn in your inventory, he will replace it with Zehtuka's Horn; the new item will be customized to your current character.
Skill recommendations
Guide to the Norn Fighting Tournament
Enchantment removal, to counter the monk opponents.
Condition removal to remove blindness.
Self heal.
A spirit spammer with sufficient damage (e.g. Signet of Spirits) and self-healing (e.g. Vampirism) or protection (e.g. Union).
Counters to Magni:
snares to keep out of melee range, e.g. "You Move Like A Dwarf!".
Skills that cause Blind to nerf his attacks.
Interrupts, to prevent him from using his Bear Form.
The tournament cannot be fought in Hard mode; the game will always switch to Normal mode upon entering.
Opponents do not drop loot; however, their companions can drop seasonal items if they die before you win the round.

Spirits placed in the starting room will not have line of sight to the main battle; spirits placed in the starting room's doorway will. Alternatively, you can move the spirits into the main room just before the gate shuts.
A "You were not worthy." message appears if you die during the tournament.

quests/quest:gww:65471/sections/objectiv.text: Defeat Magni the Bison and claim victory in his tournament.
See Magni the Bison for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:65471/sections/notes-1/.text: This quest is automatically accepted upon completing the preceding quest (that is, winning the round 5 of the tournament).

Unlike the other quests in this quest chain, this one is not repeatable. Once a character wins the Norn Fighting Tournament, the next time this quest chain is started, this quest will be replaced by Final Round, Championship Edition: Fight! instead.

quests/quest:gww:10399/sections/objectiv.text: Speak to Keeper Shafoss to gain entrance to the Heart of Abaddon.
Destroy the binding guardians and free Razah. [3...0] of 3 guardians remain.
See Chaplain Phyratyss for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:10399/sections/walkthro.text: Travel to Abaddon's Gate and speak to Keeper Shafoss who will send you to Heart of Abaddon.

After you enter the Heart of Abaddon, dispose of the patrols around the first Binding Guardian. There are four separate groups, so take care to draw them in one at-a-time. Remain close to the portal until you have dispatched at least two of the groups. There are 3 neutral Binding Guardians in the area protected by hostile foes. They will turn hostile when you reach Razah and first talk to him. If you bring Gaze of Fury or Spirit to Flesh to take them out while neutral on your way to Razah, you won't have to back-track to defeat them and their reinforcements, which will easily cut the quest time by a half.

Once it is safe, follow the quest markers towards Razah, dealing with the all the patrols you see as you head up the hill. Approach each group carefully and pull them to you as there are several popup groups you'd prefer to deal with separately.
Talk to Razah to trigger his dialogue; if you have already removed the guardians, talk to him again to complete the quest.

Otherwise head back down the hill to take care of the guardians one by one. If you get too close to them, you will trigger reinforcements. At the two shrines nearest Razah, they will consist of a Margonite and 4 creatures from the Shadow Army; these are probably easier to deal with than the demonic patrols. The reinforcements at the shrine closest to the portal are more annoying: 4 Titan Abominations; as each dies, it turns into two Madness Titans. Fortunately, you only have to defeat the guardian; once that is done, you can retreat to speak to Razah to finish the quest.

You can avoid triggering the reinforcements by killing the guardians using long-range attacks, e.g. using long- or flatbows or spells. Since these spirits are weak, you can manage this with a single ranger with sufficient fire power or using any nuking build.
Lightbringer skills; all of the foes are demonic servants of Abaddon.
Panic or Psychic Instability to help shutdown foes, especially if dealing with two or more patrols.
Gaze of Fury or Spirit to Flesh will remove the Binding Guardians. The latter only works while they are friendly while the former can also be used to destroy Quickening Zephyrs.

quests/quest:gww:10399/sections/notes-1/.text: Margonite Sorcerers and Rain of Terrors use skills that snare; however, it is possible to complete this quest within minutes by using speed boosts without fighting, in conjunction with Gaze of Fury or Spirit to Flesh to destroy the Binding Guardians along the way.

quests/quest:gww:10399/sections/objectiv.text: Ask Keeper Millzesh about gaining entrance to the Heart of Abaddon.
Explore and investigate the Heart of Abaddon.
Free Razah by destroying the Binding Guardians.
See Chaplain Phyratyss for your reward.
QUEST FAILED: Keeper Mirzesh is missing! Return to Chaplain Phyratyss in the Gate of Anguish for more information.

quests/quest:gww:295341/sections/objecti.text: Defeat the attacking Ministry of Purity forces. Jinnai has placed traps in the area that will aid you.

quests/quest:gww:295341/sections/shared-.text: Talk to Miku in the Shenzun Tunnels Shenzun Tunnels (Winds of Change) (just south of Tahnnakai Temple). This will transport your party to Jinnai's location. After a brief dialogue between Jinnai and Miku, Ministry of Purity will appear all over the map. They will slowly approach your location. Defeat them all to complete the quest. Be aware that neither Jinnai nor Miku can use the teleporters found throughout the area.
There are two basic approaches: find a good place to defend or keep moving around.

Immediately after initiating the opening dialogue, use the teleporter near your starting location and head to the cemetery due south of where you get teleported to; it's one of several decent defensive locations. Regardless of your choice, keep the party spread out to counter the enemy's AoE skills. Defeat the groups as they spawn. Jinnai and Miku will remain at their initial location, diverting the enemy until you are ready to pull them towards you. Or you can wait for the Ministry to find you.

If you use the cemetery, use the stairs as a choke point and block it with a spirit wall, minions, or a tank. You can also walk to your chosen spot, in which case, the NPCs will follow you and aid in the fight.

Alternatively, head north from the first teleporter's exit (instead of south to the cemetery). Defeat the 2-3 ministry groups that spawn at this location and leave any heroes flagged here. Go south to find the next ministry group and draw them back to your heroes. Keep repeating this until there are no more ministry troops. Be careful approaching Miku and Jinnai, since they will also attract foes towards your heroes.

Since Jinnai has spiked the area with traps, you can move between teleporters, drawing the ministry foes to each trap in turn. The traps are not likely to kill all your opponents, but they will weaken them sufficiently to allow your team to mop up the remnants. do the traps do any damage at all? talk page seems to suggest not
Bringing a Minion Bomber or two is useful due to the sheer number of available corpses.
A Soul Twisting hero is recommended for additional protection.
Synergy with MM Protection spells greatly increases survivability if too many enemies are accidentally aggroed.
An effective body block method if using the cemetery defense, such as a Signet of Spirits hero or melee hero capable of AoE damage.
A Vow of Strength Dervish or Hundred Blades Warrior is highly recommended, or:
An Assassin with Death Blossom if protection/healing capability is high.
This quest takes place in an explorable version of Altrumm Ruins.

quests/quest:gww:205449/sections/objecti.text: Help Gadd acquire the Bloodstone from Sparkfly Swamp on the Tarnished Coast.
*BONUS* Complete the mission in Hard Mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:205449/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 30 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the *BONUS* Objective for an additional 75 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:66803/sections/requirem.text: An item related to Gwen's childhood in your inventory

quests/quest:gww:66803/sections/objectiv.text: Gwen must be present to continue.
Travel to Sacnoth Valley to investigate the reports of the new Charr force amassing.
Locate the Charr Shaman's ceremony site.
Destroy the Charr forces to prevent the ritual from being completed. You have [3…0] groups remaining.
See Captain Langmar for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:66803/sections/walkthro.text: To obtain the quest, first get a Red Iris Flower or one of the other suitable items. Then visit Gwen in your Hall of Monuments. Afterwards head out to Longeye's Ledge or Doomlore Shrine and do not forget to wear your Ebon Vanguard rank.

When coming from Grothmar Wardowns into Sacnoth Valley, if Vael has revealed himself to you, he may appear near the resurrection shrine, and help you. Follow towards the marker and you will run into two Charr that are talking to each other, and continue walking. Follow them, and after hearing the needed information, they will become aggressive and you must kill them. A new marker appears in the burning forest.

Entering the burning forest from west or the south is the shortest way. Wipe out patrolling groups first. Be careful not to aggro too much, and pay attention as the nearby boss Borrguus Blisterbark will be running around with a group. Try to spread out your party as many of the enemies have AoE fire skills that can easily wipe out your party. After wiping out surrounding enemies, proceed closer the quest marker.

There are three groups of Charr you have to defeat, and they start off non-aggro and clustered fairly close to one another until you reach the quest marker. Two of them are fairly easy, but the third group starts out as a lone boss named Straut Flamebourne, who, when attacked, will cause a Charr Effigy to spawn.

It is advised to bring skills and spells that interrupt or slow down spell casting; otherwise, both Strout Flamebourne and his Charr Effigy will cast Breath of Fire frequently, enough to quickly wipe your group. Both Straut Flamebourne and his Effigy have to be killed.

After killing these two, Gwen will talk and mention to inform Captain Langmar of the events. Map back to Longeye's Edge, proceed outside towards Grothmar Wardowns, and see Captain Langmar for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:66803/sections/notes-1/.text: Several items can trigger the quest dialogue; whichever is used will be removed upon accepting the quest. (If you wish to keep any particular item, do not accept the quest and return later with a different one.) The possible items are:
Red Iris Flower (easily obtained from Gwen's garden, just outside of Eye of the North).
Gwen will self-resurrect if needed to complete the end-quest dialogue.
This quest is more difficult to complete with The Smell of Titan in the Morning active; Ignus the Eternal and other groups will spawn along the quest route.
The reward dialogue seems to suggest that this quest takes place after The Smell of Titan in the Morning; however, the two quests can be completed in either order or together.

quests/quest:gww:25365/sections/requirem.text: Summit Slaves active in quest log.

quests/quest:gww:25365/sections/objectiv.text: Go to the last place where the flame djinn was last seen.
Hunt down and destroy the flame djinn.
See Krak Flamewhip for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25365/sections/walkthro.text: On the path to the Flame Djinn, you will encounter four burnt corpses. When you get close enough, the djinn will charge after you. The djinn has a monster skill, Consuming Flames, that could be problematic if your party does not stay close together. Consuming Flames will heal the djinn as well as any party members close to it, so minor healing is all that is needed. To quickly kill the djinn, follow the green star on your compass to the right. There will be dredge there who will help you fight it, as well as give you a boon that makes you hit for 15 points extra. Doing this will drop the djinn quickly. Note, the djinn will follow you anywhere you go, so you do not have to continually draw him to the dredge. Return to Krak Flamewhip for your reward when you have destroyed the djinn.

quests/quest:gww:25365/sections/notes-1/.text: The Iron Arch can be scouted for Summit Slaves while fighting the Flame Djinn.
Enable the Gathering Resources quest prior to attempting this one -- you will pass a number of iron ore boxes on the way to the djinn.
The quest name is likeley a pun on the fact that the Flame Djinn is found in a room with multiple levels (the "hole")

quests/quest:gww:25270/sections/objectiv.text: Find the Charr fires northeast of the Frontier Gate. Kill the Flame Keepers and extinguish the flames.
Return to Captain Arne for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25270/sections/walkthro.text: Start from Frontier Gate heading northeast. Soon you can find several Flame Keepers. After eliminating them you can travel back to Ascalon City for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25270/sections/notes-1/.text: The 10/10 Sundering Sword Hilt can be salvaged from the Long Sword.

quests/quest:gww:15321/sections/objectiv.text: Find the Charr fires along the southern edge of the Diessa Lowlands. Kill the Flame Keepers and extinguish the flames.
Return to Duke Barradin for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:15321/sections/walkthro.text: Exit Nolani Academy into Diessa Lowlands and head north east around the stairs and across the bridge. When fighting the first mob of Gargoyles, be sure to target and kill Resurrect Gargoyles first. If you aggro the Storm Riders under the bridge, just move across it and ignore them. Once across the bridge, take the east fork in the path and then head north and east around the edge of the valley carefully so as not to aggro the very large mob of Charr below. Move through the ruins with the fountain and continue east up the stairs and then down into the next valley toward the quest marker. Kill the three Flame Keepers to complete the quest.

Alternatively, exit Grendich Courthouse and head west down the path until you can turn south to go over the hill. Follow the path of Charr until you reach the Flame Keepers. Make sure not to head east immediately exiting Grendich Courthouse; it leads to a bridge that veers away and around the Flame Keepers' location.

quests/quest:gww:15321/sections/notes-1/.text: When also working towards completing The Duke's Daughter, the objective for that quest can sometimes be found adjacent to the location of the Flame Keepers.
Once the quest is completed, the compass marker will point towards Captain Arne in Ascalon City, instead of Duke Barradin in Piken Square.

quests/quest:gww:25656/sections/requirem.text: Wait for Healer Zenwa to finish his eulogy for Nehbawa Wahmeh

quests/quest:gww:25656/sections/objectiv.text: Speak to Mutu Wahmeh to learn if he is worthy of his father's inheritance.
Kill the Corsairs that stole the old fisherman's life savings.
Bring the fisherman back his life savings.
See Healer Zenwa for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25656/sections/walkthro.text: Talk to Mutu and then follow the compass point south to defeat a group of corsairs. Pick up the Chest of Coin, and carry it back to Horat (the fisherman).
Mutu must survive to complete the quest.

A group of skale spawns close to the corsairs. It may be worth going ahead to take care of them before talking to Mutu, to reduce the risk of him dying if you aggro both the skale and the corsairs at once. The corsairs will not spawn until you've spoken to Mutu.

quests/quest:gww:10463/sections/objectiv.text: Meet up with Jerob No-Spine in the Sunward Marches
You've been tricked! Kill the Kournan soldiers before they kill you!

quests/quest:gww:10463/sections/walkthro.text: Meet up with Jerob No-Spine in the Sunward Marches (just outside the Command Post), and follow his directions to the Kournan soldiers nearby. Unfortunately, Jerob's double-crossed the party and the soldiers are expected to capture you!
Fight them off! If you survive, return to the Sunspear Sanctuary and see Lonai for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:284113/sections/objecti.text: Clear the Flame Temple Corridor in Ascalon of all enemies in hard mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:284113/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 50 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:284113/sections/instruc.text: "Clear the Flame Temple Corridor in Ascalon of all enemies in hard mode."

quests/quest:gww:284113/sections/target-.text: To reach this explorable area, you must travel through the tar pit in the northeastern part of Diessa Lowlands. The nearest outpost is Grendich Courthouse.
The following quests may affect the spawns in this area:
The Titan Source (You will encounter one of the Charr bosses listed under the quest data, guarding the Altar)
The charr and hydra in the southeast corner are hostile to each other.

A squad of four Ascalon soldiers will start heading towards the temple (specifically, the Charr Altar) in a slow walk. They usually die rather quickly if left alone, especially in hard mode. If they manage to reach the altar, they will simply wander around it.

Mid-level groups arriving here for quests should find the isolated Charr groups around the temple complex to be manageable. Be careful when moving in towards the altar though, aggroing two or three groups may easily wipe a party. Pick the groups off one-by-one by pulling them.
Complete exploration of this area contributes approximately 0.5% to the Tyrian Cartographer title.

Consider taking advantage of the four Ascalon soldiers against the first few groups. But given that the foes near the temple complex should be pulled carefully, it may be better to use them as bait or as additional corpses.
Also consider starting from Yak's Bend to benefit from a party size of 6.
With patience, it is possible to bring a party of eight from Temple of the Ages.
During Special Ops: Flame Temple Corridor, you will be transported to an alternative version of the area.

quests/quest:gww:25647/sections/objectiv.text: Shoo the troublesome flamingos out of Kanyama's south field.

quests/quest:gww:25647/sections/walkthro.text: Use the command /shoo to shoo out flamingos in south field. You only need to shoo each flamingo once, after which it will keep running from you and you can simply run after it to chase it away. Try to herd them into groups to save time, and be aware that they can wander back into the field after you shoo them out.
The quest will update once there are no flamingos left in the field, and you can claim your reward from Kanyama.

quests/quest:gww:25647/sections/notes-1/.text: Despite what Kanyama says, the worst the flamingos will do is body block you.
It is possible to charm the flamingos.
Having multiple human players helps to save time on this quest.
It may help to come directly from Beknur Harbor, giving the flamingos as little time as possible to spread out before you arrive.
While you are nearby, you should open the Buried Treasure on the edge of the field if you have not done so recently.

quests/quest:gww:21295/sections/objectiv.text: Find Sergeant Bokkun in Sebelkeh Basilica. He'll know where the heket are.
Eavesdrop on the heket warrior's conversations. Glean information about the upcoming heket attacks.
Gather more details about the arriving shipment.
See Commander Tanmod for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:21295/sections/walkthro.text: Start at Dzagonur Bastion. At point one, you will find Sergeant Bokkun, who will know where the Heket are. He will send Scout Dehra to take you to point two, where you will wait and eavesdrop on two Heket. Do not get into aggro range. Once the two Heket are finished talking, Scout Dehra will lead you to point three, where you will eavesdrop on two more Heket. Once this is finished, go to point four, which is Dzagonur Bastion. You can map there. Collect your quest reward, and you're done.

quests/quest:gww:21295/sections/notes-1/.text: After talking to Sergeant Bokkun, an additional NPC, Scout Dehra, will join your party and follow you, but doesn't appear under the party ally list.
It may be possible to combine this quest with The Search for Survivors, for an enlarged party with extra allies.
The quest states to find Sergeant Bokkun in Sebelkeh Basilica, although he actually stands just outside Dzagonur Bastion.

quests/quest:gww:66727/sections/objectiv.text: Meet Vael in Sacnoth Valley to begin your mission.
Follow Vael to the hierophant's stronghold.
You have three minutes to sneak in and out of the stronghold.
Your mission has been compromised! Kill Gharaz the Glutton at all costs!

quests/quest:gww:66727/sections/walkthro.text: After accepting this quest, head through the Grothmar Wardowns and take the portal in the southeast corner into Sacnoth Valley. Vael is just inside, across from the shrine (shrine blessings are not necessary; no kills are required for this quest). After speaking to Vael he will run to the stronghold and ask if you're ready, agree that you are. Vael will disappear and a three minute timer will appear. During this time all of the Charr inside of the stronghold are incapacitated. There are no enemies to fight during the three minutes.

You have three minutes to poison all five stacks of food supplies. Just follow the green quest marker to the two locations where food supplies are kept (marked 1 and 2 on the map, above). Make sure to click on each food supply. Failing to click on all five will result in the mission being compromised - requiring you to kill Gharaz the Glutton.

After you've poisoned all five food supplies, run outside of the stronghold, back to Vael. If done correctly, Vael should have the exclamation mark over his head. If Vael does not, you've missed something and the mission will be compromised.

quests/quest:gww:66727/sections/notes-1/.text: Because the gas bombs technically kill and then resurrect the Charr (including Gharaz the Glutton) in the fort, they will not yield any experience, reputation points or drops after the bombs have been set off. Gharaz the Glutton will be resurrected with the other Charr in the fort even if you poisoned the food, which means that he will still be alive during the following quest if you remain in the zone.
Heroes can be flagged outside of the stronghold, near Vael's starting location, for smoother running animations since they are not needed.

Compromised your mission? Instead of fighting Gharaz the Glutton, consider stepping through the nearby portal into the Grothmar Wardowns and then back into the Sacnoth Valley. This will reset the quest, giving you the opportunity to play without having to fight this boss.

If you have not yet captured Eviscerate, it can be easily captured from Gharaz the Glutton even without fighting him, since the "dozing" Charr are technically dead. There is plenty of time to poison all of the supplies and still capture the skill.

quests/quest:gww:209521/sections/objecti.text: See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:209521/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 40 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the *BONUS* Objective for an additional 100 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:67607/sections/objectiv.text: Locate the cave where the captives are being held in the Dalada Uplands.
Bushwhack the Charr guarding the prisoners.
Check on the Flaming Scepter Mages.
See Sergeant Weststar for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:67607/sections/environm.text: After completing this quest, the Flaming Scepter Mages will be replaced with Hodat the Tumbler and a group of Stone Furies.

quests/quest:gww:67607/sections/walkthro.text: Obtain the quest from Sergeant Weststar just outside of Doomlore Shrine and follow the object marker southeast. Heading to the south first will provide a Siege Devourer, making the journey faster and easier.

The Flaming Scepter Mages can be found in the cave near the southeast corner of Dalada Uplands. Defeat the group of Charr guarding the entrance to the cave and head in. If the party leader has completed the Nolani Academy mission, the mages will become hostile. Once you have defeated them, they will once again become friendly.
Once their dialogue is completed, the quest will update and you may return to Sergeant Weststar to collect the reward.

quests/quest:gww:67607/sections/notes-1/.text: This quest reunites you with the Flaming Scepter Mages.

The dialogue by the Flaming Scepter Mages refers to their use in the Prophecies campaign of standing in obelisks and attacking any nearby foes, usually Charr. They were last seen prior to the final battle of the Nolani Academy mission on Horn Hill, where they were apparently captured by retreating Charr.

Sergeant Weststar appears just outside Doomlore Shrine to give out the quest. However, when zoning into the area again while Falling Out is active, he will not appear in his initial location. Doing Falling Out to the end will lead you into Sacnoth Valley where Sergeant Weststar will be right outside Rragar's Menagerie to give you the reward for that quest, as well as the quest The Hunting of the Charr. He will not give you the reward for Forgotten Relics. This appears to be some sort of bug, as the quest marker will point back to the Dalada Uplands. He will spawn here again only if at least one member of your party has completed Falling Out and no member of your party has Falling Out active.
If you cannot find Sergeant Weststar, make sure you complete the Falling Out quest.

quests/quest:gww:19222/sections/objectiv.text: Kill 40 Margonites. You have destroyed [0...40] Margonites.
See Vissh Rakissh for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:19222/sections/walkthro.text: Find and kill 40 Margonites, then return to Vissh for your reward. The Margonites can be from any area, they do not have to be found in The Desolation; however, killing Margonites in the Domain of Anguish do not count towards the 40 Margonites killed.

quests/quest:gww:19222/sections/notes-1/.text: Vissh's master difficulty quest The Cold Touch of the Past and its followup provide enough Margonites to complete this quest. This quest can also be completed at the same time as Getting Even.

Plenty of Margonites can also be found in Vabbi and the Realm of Torment to fulfill the requirements of this quest. Most likely, players will complete it by simply playing through the storyline if they pick it up before arriving in the Realm of Torment.
This quest is very similar to Wicked Wardens in the Factions campaign.

quests/quest:gww:38767/sections/objectiv.text: Seek out Siliss Yassith in the Arid Sea.

quests/quest:gww:38767/sections/walkthro.text: After accepting the quest, head directly south to The Arid Sea exit from Skyward Reach. To find Siliss Yassith you must go to the platform East of where the indicator points and cross the bridge of rocks. Though the quest marker looks to be fairly obvious and easy to reach, Siliss Yassith's location is trickier to access than it may seem. Approaching the quest marker the player should notice a statue of a female warrior in the distance. This will collapse as the player draws nearer.

Upon reaching the mesa that Siliss is standing upon, head further south, around the mesa and up a small trail. From there the ruins of the statue actually form a bridge that can be used to reach Siliss. Then speak with him to receive the reward for the quest.

quests/quest:gww:38767/sections/notes-1/.text: The statue of a female warrior falls and forms the bridge to get to the mesa. You do not actually see it crumble, but instead it will sway from right to left and as you come within a certain distance from it, it will be standing up at one moment and the next suddenly lie collapsed with only the feet still standing.

quests/quest:gww:12196/sections/objectiv.text: Invite a henchman into your party, then speak to Ludo in Sunqua Vale.

quests/quest:gww:12196/sections/walkthro.text: Add at least one henchman to your party. They are standing right next to Ludo. Either click on one and add them to your party through the Party Window or use the Party Search panel. Ludo will be waiting right outside the monastery in Sunqua Vale. Speak to him for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:320073/sections/notes-1.text: While the initial quest Long Thought Forgotten takes you to the entrance to the east of the Northlands, completing that quest opens up the west entrance, just north-east of Piken Square behind the charr encampment.
Because this area is mechanically part of the Depths of Tyria, the Vanguard Initiate and Reforged Mode effects are not applied.
Like in pre-Searing Ascalon, however, party members do not suffer Death Penalty, and enemies have reduced health in Reforged Mode.
Progress through this dungeon depends on multiple quests:
The dungeon cannot be entered if any party members have Across the Wall or A Bastion In the North active in their quest log.
If no party members have Charr in the Tunnels or The Scourge Beneath, or if any party member has Long Thought Forgotten, the party cannot advance to the second level.
If no party members have The Scourge Beneath, or if any party member has Charr in the Tunnels, the party cannot advance to the third level.
Quest spawns will not appear if any member of the party is not in Reforged Mode. This prevents access to levels two and three, since Wyle Brimscourge will not spawn.
If every member of the party who has The Scourge Beneath leaves after reaching level 2 of the dungeon, remaining players can still fight Maz Scourgeheart and spawn the reward chest.
The presence, level, and skills of some Charr foes in the dungeon scale with that of the lowest-leveled player in the party:

If any party member has Long Thought Forgotten, Charr in the Tunnels, or the first-time version of The Scourge Beneath in their quest log, or if any party member is not in Reforged Mode, the party level is set to 1-9.
If Devona is present in the party as a hero, her level does not influence the party level.
Similar to Vanguard quest foes, these Charr do not drop any loot, except for Maz Scourgeheart.
The rewards dropped by Maz's Chest are improved when higher-level foes are present.
Similarly, the size of the chest also increases.

Walking over the patches of blue, crystalline ground will inflict the Crippled condition for 15 seconds and the Dazed condition for 20 seconds. This environment effect affects all allies, including pets and owned minions, but does not affect any foes.
The plants and bandits are hostile towards all other creature types, including each other.
No Locked Chests or Hidden Stashes spawn inside the dungeon.
The dungeon's icon on the map does not change when a character completes the dungeon.

quests/quest:gww:320073/sections/shared-.text: The map in the Northlands points you towards the eastern entrance, but the western entrance is actually closer to Piken Square. Moreover, Artificer Mullenix is immediately present after going through the western entrance, making it likely the intended one.

Exit Piken Square through the northern exit and head north to locate the tunnel entrance (see map). If a player has not completed Long Thought Forgotten, this entrance will be closed, forcing you to go to the eastern entrance.

If any member of the party is doing the quest for the first time, Devona will join you as a level 5 ally, and the enemies you face will be similar to those found during Long Thought Forgotten and Charr in the Tunnels. Devona has a high damage output for her level, but she is not very durable against the enemies in the dungeon. Fortunately, if she is killed, she will resurrect herself as soon as no foes are within earshot.

On repeated visits to the tunnels, you will have to deal with additional Charr foes whose levels scale with that of the lowest-leveled member of the party, up to a maximum of level 18. It is advisable to bring Devona as a hero so that you can make use of skills unlocked outside Pre-Searing Ascalon.
Level 1

This part of the quest is the same as Charr in the Tunnels, except that the inhabitants of Wyle Brimscourge's chamber may be slightly more numerous, and you will have to deal with the more powerful Charr on repeat visits. Fight your way down to the south end of the dungeon as usual, pull Wyle Brimscourge and kill him for the Dungeon Key, then run or fight your way to the Dungeon Lock and the portal to level 2.
Level 2

Once again, you need to make your way from the south side of this floor to the north side. Sneak or fight your way through the large atrium to the stairs and northern tunnels; it may be easiest to keep close to the eastern side. Your quest marker will be pointing you to the crystal gate where the northern patrol was found during Charr in the Tunnels, but you actually need to go to where you found the northeastern patrol first (at the exclamation point on the map to the right). In the far northeastern tunnel, you will need to kill some Shard Elementals, unless the nearby Ironheart has already taken care of them for you. Pick up the Elemental Crystal bundle they drop, and carry it west to the crystal gate. When you approach the gate, the crystal will disappear, and the gate will open to reveal the entrance to level 3.
Level 3

You start at the middle of the south side of this floor, and will need to follow the purple path on the map to the right. Head northeast until you reach a large chamber filled with ruins and Charr, then hug the left wall heading north until you can start heading west again. Pass under the bridge, being careful of any Charr above. Just after the bridge, you may want to take a short detour south to clear out the Charr atop another bridge you will be passing under later. Continue west and you will reach a large foundry area, where your goal is to reach one of the stairways leading up to the higher walkways to the southwest. There is a resurrection shrine nearby, and from there you should be able to see the Boss Key lying on the overlook further south. After picking up the key, return to the red path on the map to the right, and fight your way around to the Boss Lock, then to the large open area to the southwest where Maz Scourgeheart and his elementals await you.
Maz Scourgeheart

The elementalist boss is fought three times. The first two times he reaches 10% health, he will turn friendly, taunt the party, summon a large group of Shard Elementals and teleport to a side of the arena. His new location will be locked behind a crystal gate. To open it, you must kill the Shards elementals, pick up the Elemental Keystone one of them is carrying, and carry it to the crystal gate.

Maz will start with Fire Magic, including Mark of Rodgort, Fireball and Lava Font. After teleporting once, he will switch to Air Magic, with Lightning Javelin and Whirlwind to interrupt attackers and Lightning Strike to hit without line of sight. For the last confrontation he will use Water Magic, snaring his enemies with Deep Freeze and Shard Storm while protecting himself with Blurred Vision and Swirling Aura. In all three fights, he will also use Earthquake for AoE knockdown and Kinetic Armor to increase his armor rating.

His elementals are identical to the other elementals in the dungeon, and behave as a group. While they can deal significant melee damage at low levels, sufficient AoE damage should dispatch them quickly.

Maz and his minions shouldn't pose too much of a threat compared to the other mobs in the dungeon, especially if you are a spellcaster with high firepower. His spells are also slow to cast, giving you a generous window to spike him down before he becomes a problem. Armor-ignoring damage in particular bypasses Kinetic Armor, and Backfire will shut him down completely. Should you still face difficulties, equipping Devona with interrupts and/or enchantment removal can counter most of Maz's tactics.
Upon his death, Maz's Chest will spawn. After every player in the party has opened the chest, a countdown will start and the party will be returned to Piken Square.
Talk to Devona to finish the quest.
Although this quest can be acquired without Reforged Mode enabled, the quest NPCs will not spawn and the objectives will not progress while any member of the party is not in Reforged Mode.

Adding a player without Reforged Mode to the party will prevent enemies from spawning in the northern part of the Northlands, making it slightly easier to reach the Forsaken Tunnels. The quest can still be completed if all players without Reforged Mode log out or map travel away before entering the dungeon.

When repeating the quest, there will be additional Charr groups throughout the dungeon with no loot and levels that scale with the weakest member of the party. Players interested in speed clears and safer runs may therefore prefer to abandon the quest after opening the reward chest, though this means never unlocking Devona as a hero.
An alternative is to join a party with another player who is doing the first-time version of the quest, or with a player whose level is lower than 10.

The quest spawns, including Wyle Brimscourge and the Elemental Crystal on level 2, will be overridden if any party members have Long Thought Forgotten or Charr in the Tunnels active in their quest log.

If another player in the party has Charr in the Tunnels active, the party can complete that quest by killing all of the Charr Patrol Stalkers, then use the portal back to level 1 to reset the map, enabling access to level 3 without returning to the surface. This makes the run slightly longer, but allows the party to kill three additional charr bosses along the way.
It is possible to kill Maz Scourgeheart by dealing damage at range (typically with spells such as Fire Storm or Symbol of Wrath or a bow with long enough range) without opening any crystal gate.

Once Maz is killed, the remaining Shard Elementals of the second wave (with the exception of the one carrying the Elemental Keystone) will have a special animation and stop attacking the players. They won't retaliate even when attacked.

quests/quest:gww:15812/sections/objectiv.text: Travel to Fort Aspenwood and speak to the Luxon Commander.

quests/quest:gww:15812/sections/walkthro.text: Leaving from Zos Shivros Channel, head west through Boreas Seabed (explorable area) and Mount Qinkai. Alternatively, you can leave from Cavalon into Archipelagos and through Breaker Hollow.

quests/quest:gww:15812/sections/notes-1/.text: The Kurzick equivalent of this quest is Defend Fort Aspenwood.

quests/quest:gww:202578/sections/objecti.text: Push the invading Charr forces back to the Great Northern Wall.
*BONUS* Rescue Deeter Saberlin from the Charr.
*BONUS* Complete the mission in Hard Mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:202578/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 15 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the first *BONUS* Objective for an additional 22 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the second *BONUS* Objective for an additional 37 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:202578/sections/walkthr.text: As per the Fort Ranik mission.

quests/quest:gww:283041/sections/objecti.text: Clear the Forum Highlands in Vabbi of all enemies in hard mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:283041/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 150 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:283041/sections/notes-1.text: Unlike other Zaishen Vanquish quests that require vanquishing areas in Vabbi, this quest awards 3,500 Sunspear Promotion Points instead of 750.

quests/quest:gww:283041/sections/instruc.text: "Clear the Forum Highlands in Vabbi of all enemies in hard mode."

quests/quest:gww:283041/sections/target-.text: Characters will pass through here out of Vehtendi Valley as part of the primary quest Rally The Princes, on their way to meet with Priestess Haila in the center of the plaza.
The elemental groups are concentrated towards the south. Their groups, although small, are close to each other. Careful pulling is recommended.
The Desperate Measures quest in particular will produce additional Harpy and Heket spawns.
The Hekets and Harpies in this area are hostile to each other. After one group wipes another out, take advantage of the winner's weakened state.

Korshek the Immolated can easily wipe out unprepared groups. Protective Spirit and Pain Inverter are highly recommended, as the first will lower his damage output, and the second will reflect the damage back to him. See Korshek the Immolated (Zaishen quest) for additional strategies.

quests/quest:gww:25716/sections/objectiv.text: Escape through the back exit to the Foundry.
Defeat the Black Beast of Arrgh and his minions.
See General Yendzarsh for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25716/sections/walkthro.text: After taking this quest, clear the entire Foundry of enemy patrols before attempting to complete the quest objectives. Patrols will consist of Titans, Margonites, Greater Dream Riders and Tortureweb Dryders. Unlike previous rooms, the Foundry itself is spacious and allows for kiting and evading enemies.

Once the Foundry is cleared, the prisoners can be freed. When speaking to each prisoner, a spawn will appear when choosing the related quest dialog. Captain Valkyss is guarded by Tortureweb Dryders and Greater Dream Riders. Silzesh is guarded by fourteen Dementia Titans and General Yendzarsh is guarded by a mixed group of Titans.

After all three are freed, the quest marker will point southward. The party should send their tank or puller to the gate. This will trigger the spawn of The Black Beast of Arrgh. He will be accompanied by a small group of Titans. The Beast is a Dervish with a very nasty skill called "Touch of Aaaaarrrrrrggghhh", which will set the target's attributes to zero for 20 seconds. However, it is fairly easy to kill the Beast if the party can offer him a tank who can keep him from laying his touch on other party members.
After the Beast and his original minions are killed (spawns of the Titans do not count), the quest will be completed and the three prisoners will, thankfully, be removed from the party list.

Be careful when accepting the quest reward. When you do, The Fury and his minions will spawn at the location indicated on the map - if General Yendzarsh happens to stand there, they will spawn right next to you. Killing those will spawn a Titan Chest (containing Titan Gemstones), open the path to the City of Torc'qua and progress the quest Mallyx the Unyielding. See there for a walkthrough.

quests/quest:gww:25716/sections/notes-1/.text: Greater Dream Riders will follow indefinitely. Separate them from their patrols and then pull them far from the Dryders and then try to destroy them with regular attacks or Lightbringer's Gaze. Avoid using enchantments when engaging them as their Shatter Enchantment will deal a lot of damage when they are "Enraged".

Keeping the prisoners alive can be quite difficult. First, the prisoners do not follow anyone in particular, instead they tend to follow the party member who is moving most frequently and/or calling targets. Having one member of the party constantly moving to keep the prisoners towards the back of the party is helpful, along with resisting the temptation to call targets as much as possible.

Bonding the prisoners makes it easier to keep them alive. Also, casting Spell Breaker on Captain Valkyss as he runs from the Tortureweb Dryders is recommended. Summoning Ritualist spirits near the prisoners before talking to them can help distract the enemies while the prisoner gets away.

quests/quest:gww:212709/sections/objecti.text: Kill Fozzy Yeoryios in Sacnoth Valley.
*BONUS* Kill Fozzy Yeoryios in Hard Mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:212709/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 30 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the *BONUS* Objective for an additional 75 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:212709/sections/walkthr.text: [Incomplete source section] This is a Grawl boss, near the center of Sacnoth Valley. He is surrounded by many Grawl followers. In particular, there are quite a few Grawl Dark Priests in the area, which can keep each other, and Fozzy, alive for a very long time. When coming from Doomlore Shrine it's very easy when you take the siege devourer.

quests/quest:gww:289186/sections/objecti.text: Meet Soar Honorclaw and his forces in Xaquang Skyway.
Fight your way inside the "Tengu Containment Zone."
Locate and free the Tengu Prisoners.
Escort the prisoners to the Shenzun Tunnels.
At least one Tengu Prisoner must survive.
See Soar Honorclaw for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:289186/sections/shared-.text: Meet up with Soar Honorclaw and her Angchu Tengu allies east of the entrance to Senji's Corner. Note that Soar's group of Angchu will resurrect after a short time out of earshot of foes. Head north, being careful not to aggro too many Ministry fighters at the same time. Once you reach The Roost, wait for the short dialogue between Elite Ministry Captain and the party leader, after which the Ministry will turn hostile and Tengu from the Roost will become allies. More Ministry fighters will arrive; defeat them and lead the Tengu to the exit to Shenzun Tunnels. Map travel back to Ran Musu Gardens and return to Aerie to claim your reward.
The Ministry foes here are very aggressive: they will chase your party farther than most other foes.
If you're having trouble keeping the prisoners alive, you can take several steps before approaching the prisoners.
Clear the path to Shenzun Tunnels.
Setup a Spirit wall before the fight begins, to delay the Ministry reinforcements from south.
Bring speed boosts for two reasons
This will help you pull speed-boosted foes away from the slower-moving casters.
To help counter the snares used by the Ministry.
Skills that affect allies in an area are very effective due to the large amount of allies in this quest, especially Ebon Battle Standard of Honor.

quests/quest:gww:66643/sections/objectiv.text: Clear out the frogmen. You have [3...0] of 3 groups remaining.

quests/quest:gww:66643/sections/walkthro.text: Exit into Sparkfly Swamp. Hayda will be directly north a short walk, you shouldn't need to fight any mobs on the way to get her. The three groups of hekets are to the north, you'll have to clear out some other mobs along with way but none should pose any problem to a full party. Map travel back to Gadd's Encampment for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:66643/sections/notes-1/.text: Consider combining this quest with Finding Gadd, since you will have Hayda as additional support.
Also consider saving this quest until vanquishing Sparkfly Swamp.

quests/quest:gww:207139/sections/objecti.text: Kill Fronis Irontoe in his lair.
*BONUS* Kill Fronis Irontoe in Hard Mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:207139/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 20 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the *BONUS* Objective for an additional 50 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:207139/sections/walkthr.text: The easiest way to receive credit for this quest is to receive Kilroy Stonekin's buff, "Kilroy Stonekin", and run past all of the enemies directly to Fronis Irontoe. You can bypass the final blockade by staying to the right side.
Alternatively, see the walkthrough at Kilroy Stonekin's Punch-Out Extravaganza!.

quests/quest:gww:67109/sections/notes-1/.text: It is only possible to enter this dungeon via dialogue in the required quest.

500 Deldrimor reputation points are awarded for completing this dungeon for the first time in normal mode, and 250 points are awarded for subsequent completions. 750 Deldrimor reputation points are awarded for completing this dungeon in hard mode for the first time, and 375 points are awarded for subsequent completions.
There is a total of 56 enemies in this dungeon.
Sometimes Kilroy will run past some enemies. To prevent them from being missed, he sometimes runs back, even when there are no enemies there.
Although both bosses have an elite skill, neither can be captured because your character's skill set is replaced by the Dwarven Brawler set.
Completion of this dungeon will fill in page #16 of the Master Dungeon Guide storybook.

Sometimes the locked chest will spawn inside a wall. Sometimes Kilroy may get stuck behind the locked chest that has spawned in his way, if you lure a Stone Summit near him he will often get free, otherwise you will have to continue without him. The first Enslaved Ettin doesn't refresh the duration of Scroll of Rampager's Insight, but works properly with Scroll of Berserker's Insight.

quests/quest:gww:67109/sections/shared-q.text: Upon entering Fronis Irontoe's Lair, your skills will be replaced with the Brawling build (an extra skill will become available in Hard mode, Brawling Combo Punch). Kilroy Stonekin will fight along side you and use his shout "Kilroy Stonekin". Make your way through the Stone Summit one by one.

At one point, you'll come across an entire room of Stone Summit, but they only turn hostile two or three at a time. Focus on one target at a time (preferably the same targeted by Kilroy Stonekin), as defeating a foe will refill some of your health. If you are knocked down, use STAND UP! repeatedly until your energy is fully restored. If Kilroy KD'd, he will revive when no foes are around. If you just want to complete the dungeon, you can run all the way to Fronis and punch him down, bypassing the blockade by Lieutenant Mahgma and his companions.
At the end of the cave, you will encounter Fronis Irontoe and an Enslaved Ettin. Although you only need to kill Fronis to finish the quest, it is easier if you kill the Ettin first.
Normal Mode tactics
Keep moving. Killing a foe heals you fast and preserves your adrenaline.
Engage a new group with Brawling Uppercut, Brawling Headbutt, or both ready. This takes down their numbers quickly and provides you with healing and adrenaline at the same time.
Save Brawling Uppercut for the carvers and crushers. The rangers are merely annoying unless you're already badly injured. Don't waste these powerful skills on foes that are near death.

Pack a bow, wand, or staff. As soon as you defeat Lieutenant Mahgma, run for the final encounter. Plink the ettin with your bow until Kilroy catches up to you. This preserves (and builds) your adrenaline for the final encounter.

Any customized Flatbow can be used against the Stone Summit Rangers; although it will deal only 1 damage per hit, the rangers will not retaliate and you can (very slowly) take them down without threat of getting KO'd. If you use a Vampiric Bow, you will do 6 damage per hit.
Advanced tactics
When starting the game, run up near the two first mobs and wait for Kilroy to catch up. Run in front of him and attack them. Save your adrenal attack and double combo punch for the next group.

When approaching the second group, quickly attack one of the two first melee Stone Summit Dwarves. Unleash your adrenal attacks on him starting with your knockdown. If you knocked him out quickly enough you and Kilroy should have no problems finishing the rest.

On the third group, run straight up to the ranger on the far right. Kill him and move on to Ettin. Then run up and kill the three Dwarves in the doorway. Unleashing an adrenal chain here is beneficial.

On the fourth group, run towards the dwarf on the right side. Run straight past the wolf and knock him out. Kilroy will follow you, if the other dwarf joins combat, kill him next as that will usually be the target Kilroy attacks. Finish up the wolves.
In the hallway, Kilroy will often die, and so will you. Kill them and move on towards the entrance of the boss room.

Wait for Kilroy to be near you, and move on to the big room. Pull the mobs to the top of the small hill there by the doorway, and unleash a big attack chain at once. If you did this correctly, you will now have aggro and will be defeating the next dwarf. If you are standing on the top of the hill, most of the dwarves will be running in to the middle before running up to you. That means you will fight all the dwarves two versus one, and will be able to finish up the room very quickly. If Kilroy dies, try to continue as long as possible. But if you die, it is very slow to get a good hold on the situation when fighting three versus one all the time. So pull the mobs far away from Kilroy's corpse and resurrect him.

On the first boss group, Kilroy will almost always start with the far left dwarf. Unleash a big attack chain and kill him first, then kill the second. Kill boss last. If Kilroy dies pull him away. The boss will follow you indefinitely while the other dwarves will move back. Kilroy will not move in to the boss room without you being near him, and he will take care of the returning dwarves in the hallway.

In the final boss room, it is perfectly applicable to attack the ettin directly without delay. As long as you pull it a little back so Kilroy starts attacking it earlier, killing it and giving you a health boost. Use knockdowns on Fronis Irontoe instead of the ettin as the ettin is immune to knockdown.

When you are fighting 3 or more foes at the same time, let Kilroy attack first and choose the same target as he does. A quick kill provides you with a health bonus and reduces the total damage you take.

While KO'd and surrounded by several foes, pick the opponent with the lowest HP and use Brawling Combo Punch or Brawling Straight Right as your first attack after standing up. Taking a dwarf down quickly decreases the threats and potential damage against you, gives you an easier route to retreat, and boosts your health.
Additional tips
With assassin as one of your professions, maximize dagger mastery. This gives a chance of double strikes, which give extra adrenaline and a little extra damage.

Your Brawling Combo Punch recharges when you get knocked out. If your energy is low, you can use this to take care of the bosses. However, Lieutenant Mahgma will most likely interrupt it immediately if his Dwarven Battle Stance is active. Instead, use Brawling Block, wait 2-3 seconds, then unleash the combo punch on him.

If Kilroy dies in the room with Lieutenant Mahgma, you can pull the mobs far enough away from him that he self-resurrects. However, this requires that you be under the effects of a consumable-based speed boost (e.g. Rock Candy).
Special considerations for Survivor candidates

The quest is renowned for its part in easily obtaining the Survivor Title: it is repeatable and death is easily avoided. The following ideas are designed for Survivors, but are generally useful in completing the Dungeon. The quest is riskier for caster professions, with a maximum AR of 60.
Be sure to use maximum armor.
There are several useful Insignias and Runes.
Map STAND UP! to more than one key and/or alternate mouse-clicks with the 8 key; this will make it easier to regain your energy quickly, even if you need to recharge it to 140 energy.
With full adrenaline, use the following skill chain for a quick kill: Brawling Combo Punch > Brawling Uppercut > Brawling Straight Right.

Use extreme caution when resigning. You can die a real death (losing progress towards the Survivor title) if you resign while knocked out or if you get knocked out before the game acknowledges your resignation. Try to reach a safe area and map out instead (your Guild Hall is usually the easiest place to reach, using the default keyboard shortcut of [G]).
Maximizing experience gains

Use experience scrolls to reduce the number of times you need to complete the quest. (You need just under 1.2 million experience to go from L20's 140,600 xp the 1,337,500 xp for Legendary Survivor .) Repeating this in normal mode requires about 140 visits, since each run earns about 8,468 experience without scrolls.
You can reduce the number of normal mode runs to 104 runs using Scrolls of Adventurer's Insight.
It takes only 29 runs in hard mode using Scrolls of Slayer's Insight (42,000 xp/run).
The most cost-efficient choice is a Scroll of Berserker's Insight, if you can make it last until you kill Lieutenant Mahgma.
Since experience gain is capped at 300% in hard mode, there is no additional value in paying for scrolls offering more than a 250% XP bonus from kills.
You cannot use more than one scroll at a time.
For farming Irontoe's Chest
You can farm this dungeon without killing any mobs except for Fronis Irontoe.

As soon as you zone into the lair start running towards the group of four dwarves (two archers, two melee) at the exit to the first room. Before you arrive at the dwarves Kilroy will use his shout, increasing your movement speed - this will allow you pass between the two archers and proceed into the second room.

In the second room run slightly to the right of the archer. The three melee dwarves will begin to run towards the exit but if you continue running past the archer you will overtake them and enter the third room before they arrive. If you target the archer he will use one of these three tactics: take no shots and run past and then follow you a short bit, use Point Blank Shot then stand around, or use Marauder's Shot and take 1-2 more shots, possibly including Point Blank shot. Use Brawling Block to block as many attacks as needed.
The third room is relatively straightforward; run past the wolf and melee dwarf, and between the two melee dwarves at the exit to the room.
It is very easy to rubberband if you have any latency when attempting to exit this room. To help avoid rubberbanding avoid getting into melee range with the dwarves for as long as possible.

The archers in the fourth room can cause a significant amount of damage and it is not uncommon to be 'knocked out' near the exit to this room. Hugging the left wall will minimize the time you are in this room and in range of the archers and Brawling Block can be used to negate some of the damage.
There is also a patrol of two melee dwarves in this room (not marked on the map.)
The following room (number five) can be bypassed by passing on the right side of the rightmost allied dwarf near the exit.

As you pass the allied dwarf, strafing to the left can cause any pursuers to get body blocked by the allied dwarves. This is also a common place for rubberbanding (using /stuck is handy to make sure you got between dwarf and wall)
The final room contains only Fronis Irontoe and an Enslaved Ettin. At this point Kilroy's shout will have expired but it should not be problematic to kill Fronis without it.
Ignore the ettin; it cannot be knocked down and does not need to be killed to cause Irontoe's Chest to spawn.
It is probable that you get 'knocked out' once or twice during this fight.
To minimize time between runs:
Map travel to Gunnar's Hold after you have looted Irontoe's Chest.
Accept the quest reward from Kilroy.

Switch districts (switch to International from your district, or vice-versa, if there is only one local district.) or return to the character selection screen and select the same character again (F12, c, space/enter).
Speak to Kilroy, accept the quest, and enter the Lair.
In hard mode this run takes around ten minutes. Rewards:
2500 exp
375 Dwarf Reputation Points
250 gold
1 Locked Chest
2 Aged Dwarven Ale, 2 Dwarven Ale or one of each
Recommended equipment
Dwarven brawling#Recommended equipment
Adding 5x Stalwart Insignias gives you an additional AR +10 against physical damage. If you are having trouble, you can use an Armor of Salvation, Drake Kabobs, Skalefin Soup, or War Supplies.
Regardless of your primary profession, ensure that you set your Dagger Mastery to at least 9.
You can apply useful mods to Thunderfist's Brass Knuckles:
Dagger Tangs: Sundering (for armor penetration), Furious (to recharge Brawling skills more quickly)
A Dagger Handle of Shelter will add additional armor protection.
A "Brawn over Brains" Inscription adds 15% to your damage without any penalties (for this mission).
General tips
You can use items and switch weapons while Knocked Out, since the KO does not count as a Death. Use the opportunity to refresh experience scrolls.
You can damage Stone Summit Rangers using a Vampiric Long or Flatblow; they will not retaliate if you stand outside of aggro range..
Almost every foe has the same health: 80 in normal mode and 200 in hard mode. Exceptions: Ettins, Wolves and bosses.
Kilroy Stonekin doesn't gain health from enemy deaths, he does however have some natural health regeneration.
Attacking the same foe as Kilroy allows you to regain health more quickly; each death boosts your health substantially.

Kilroy is vulnerable to the archers past the second door; try to pull them out of the hallway so that he can survive longer. Similarly, pull the next set of enemies into the archers' now-empty area, so that you need only fight a few at a time. If you find yourself overwhelmed, run away; the dwarves will return to their original positions while you take time to heal.
Treasure Hunters should enter the dungeon in normal mode, grab the loot from the locked chest, and zone out quickly, avoiding any fighting at all.
To quickly repeat the quest, you can rezone or switch districts after accepting the reward.
There are several differences between Normal and Hard modes:
The dwarves have 80 health in normal mode and 200 in hard mode.
You have 500 health in NM and 600 in HM.
When a foe dies, you gain 200 health in NM and 300 in HM.
In HM, the rangers use Broad Head Arrow if you have a caster weapon equipped.
If Kilroy does more damage to an enemy, you will gain experience, but any experience scroll effects will not be renewed.
Standard attacks don't affect you, only skills.
Kilroy is affected by standard attacks.
Kilroy does not gain +200/300 health after a monster is killed, so to keep him alive, make sure you lead the way.
This quest is a reasonable way to earn money quickly: assuming you identify and sell everything, you should expect to earn 1 — 31 platinum per run.
As with other solo quests, you may not use summoning stones.
You can repeat this quest to level up heroes if you add them into your party before accepting the quest reward.
During special events, you have the same chances of getting special drops as anywhere else.
If you resign after opening the dungeon chest, you will receive a note stating that you failed the quest. However, you still be able to collect the reward from Kilroy.

If one levels up while knocked down (e.g. because Kilroy kills an enemy) STAND UP! has no effect and you will be kicked out of the dungeon. Unfortunately, this counts as a death towards a Survivor title — be sure to map out of the dungeon if this happens.

As in other areas, locked chests can spawn inside a wall. Should you be able to open the chest but cannot pick up the loot, complete the dungeon and wait 3 minutes for the game to return you to Gunnar's Hold. The item will then appear in the Unclaimed Items window.
Sometimes Kilroy may get stuck on a chest that has spawned in his way, if you lure a Stone Summit near him he will often get free, otherwise you will have to continue without him.

quests/quest:gww:10454/sections/objectiv.text: Search the Eastern Frontier and Pockmark Flats for Footman Tate and Footman Quinn. Bring them to justice.
Footman Tate surrendered. Lead him back to the Frontier Gate.
Return to Warmaster Riga for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:10454/sections/rewards-.text: Halves Skill Recharge of Spells (10% chance)

The Jeweled Chakram has what would normally be the skin and attribute of a Jeweled Chalice. Conversely, the quest A Mission of Peace rewards a Jeweled Chalice with the skin and attribute of a Jeweled Chakram.

quests/quest:gww:10454/sections/walkthro.text: To get to Footman Tate, travel southeast from the Frontier Gate. You'll encounter some Devourers along the way as they pop out of the ground, but if you take them a group at a time, you'll have no problems defeating them. The path will curve around east and then veer northeast after the collector, then turn sharply back towards the south. Keep following the path and hug the wall (being careful not to aggro the Devourers on top of the plateau). Round the corner and head northeast in the chasm before tapering off east. Round the corner south and climb the small knoll. A group of Devourers may be waiting for you, but they're not too tough. Defeat them, and speak with Footman Tate (location marked by the green indicator on the first map).

If you choose the conversation choices "Don't make me kill you" or "If you run, I'll find you," he'll simply respond with "I don't know what to do. This is all very confusing." He'll agree to follow you if you tell him that "everything will be all right." Simply reverse the path you took to get to him and escort him back to the Frontier Gate.

It's quicker to reach Footman Quinn by departing from Fort Ranik. Travel south and walk under the aqueduct/series of arches. You'll encounter some Renegades and some Charr (depending on what quests you have active), but they're relatively easy to take care of. Some Devourers may pop up from the ground, but defeat them and head east. Walk through the zone to Pockmark Flats.

Once you're in Pockmark Flats, head east and follow the path. You'll encounter a Crimson Devourer or two along with some Flash and Shatter Gargoyles and perhaps a Storm Rider or two. Head north until you reach the aqueduct/series of arches and head east, following the structure. You may have to fight some Wind Riders, Hulking Stone Elementals, and a Stone Elemental, but fight the Riders and the Elementals separately and you shouldn't have too much of a problem. Stick with the path and follow it southeast. You'll reach a point where you can take the first path north, but keep heading down until you reach the shoreline and follow that north. You'll have to follow a winding path up northeast, but after you crest the hill, Footman Quinn will be waiting for you (the green indicator on the second map). Alternatively, you can travel south from Serenity Temple through Pockmark Flats.
Once you kill him, map back to the Frontier Gate to get your reward from Warmaster Riga.

quests/quest:gww:10454/sections/notes-1/.text: Footman Tate will continue to spawn in the Eastern Frontier even after you lead him back to the Frontier Gate.

Completion of this dungeon will fill in page #6 of the Master Dungeon Guide storybook.

quests/quest:gww:63616/sections/shared-q.text: Level One

This level is fairly straightforward and the exit to the next level is very close. There are a lot of mobs and snowballs along the way, therefore it is advisable to tread slowly, and pull each mob to prevent the party from getting overwhelmed. The area map for this level is unnecessary, but can be found by the entrance door.
Level Two

Upon entrance, a player may find an area map nearby. Near the bottom of the icy area Frost Wurms and Frostmaw Spawns will popup. Just outside of that room, there will be a group of Chromatic Drakes, Frozen Elementals, and a Frostmaw Spawn. It is essential, especially in hard mode to carefully pull each group to prevent a party wipe.

The portal to level 3 can be approached from either the left or the right path. The path to the left has (3) popup mobs of Stormcloud Incubi (8 to 10 total) which appear just past the doorway into the final chamber. Careful sweeping and pulling can prevent a party wipe, but the path to the right is safer with less popups. Combined mobs of Frozen Elementals and Chromatic Drakes in the confined corridors of the right hand path, can easily wipe an un-prepared party without careful pulling. This path does offer at least (3) Light of Deldrimor treasures, scattered throughout the passages.
Level Three

Keep left on entry. The first open area will contain Ice Imps, Frost Wurms, 3 large mobs of Whirling Wisps, Frozen Elementals, Ice Imps and a Frostmaw Spawn. Frost Siege Wurms and the Frostmaw Spawn tend to popup while attacking any mob near the entrance to the level. This area leads to a path with a side hallway on left. This left hallway is a dead-end but contains an area map and a collection of Dwarven Powder Kegs. The kegs can be used to break down walls but are not necessary. When the wurms near each wall are defeated a large snowball spawns and crashes into the wall, breaking it down. The path leads to a small open area to the north which can be bypassed. To the east, the path forks north and east. The fork is guarded by 3 mobs of popup Stormcloud Incubi, which should be carefully sweeped and pulled. The northern path contains a number of wurm popups and leads to a Beacon of Droknar. The eastern path leads to more wurm popups and a large empty chamber to the south. The next chamber to the northeast is guarded by Ice Imps, Frozen Elementals, Whirling Wisps, more mobs of popup Stormcloud Incubi, as well as 2 more popup groups of Frost Wurms and Frostmaw Spawn. Careful pulling here is advised to prevent a party wipe. When the last of the wurms guarding the cracked wall blocking the exit to the 4th level is defeated, a snowball will spawn and break the wall down.
Level Four

Upon entrance, the area map is on your right. Since approaching the Siege Wurm causes another Frost Wurm to spawn, carefully pulling the Incubi and the Mandragors away from the wurms is recommended. It's possible to hide behind the ice to prevent the Siege Wurm from hitting you while you bring down the other wurm. Past the ice bridge, a Frostmaw Spawn will popup so it's best to pull the Mandragors across the bridge and dispatch them separately. Run to the right past the Icy Stalagmite into the next chamber and ignore the Siege Wurms if you can. From the next doorway, a group of Siege Wurms are visible, accompanied by Mandragors. Lure the Mandragors away, and kill them while out of range of the Siege Wurms. Next, a group of Jotun are guarding the path to the Level 5 entrance. You need to pull the Jotun away from their post since a Frostmaw Spawn and one or more, Frost Wurms popup and aggro with them. It is best to attack from the hillside to the right of the Jotun spawn. Finally, the gate itself is guarded by two Icy Stalagmites.
Level Five

The area map is in the top left corner of the cavern. To make Frostmaw the Kinslayer spawn, you will need to kill the Frost Wurm Youngs and Frost Wurm Larvae, which will make her appear along with 2 Frostmaw Spawns and 3 Frost Siege Wurms. Once Frostmaw is dead, a reward chest will appear. (You are not required to kill all of the siege wurms, although it does make it easier to reach the chest and claim the quest reward from Latham.)
General suggestions

Dust rises and the ground starts to shimmy and shake as Frost Wurms and Frostmaw Spawns approach. You could try to avoid your entire party being covered in Wurm Bile by using one player as a lure while the others back away: the wurms will concentrate on just that character and the rest of the party will avoid the area of effect of Wurm Bile (which is point-based rather than targeted).
These wurms tend to remain for a while before moving to your party's new location; this usually gives you enough time to kill them.
Bring Lockpicks and/or Light of Deldrimor; this dungeon is rich in chests and Hidden Treasure.
Proceed carefully to avoid the numerous popups.
As with any quest allies, the accompanying Norn NPCs can be difficult to control. However, they are extremely sturdy and self-resurrect, making them ideal meat shields.
Threat assessment
Frostmaw does not regenerate health; you can keep whittling her down even after accumulating a high Death Penalty.
Keep spread out; most of the foes on this level deal significant AoE damage.

In the final chamber, there is a safe spot (near a gate) that you can use for staging your assault. Attack the siege wurms from there and pull back; Frostmaw and her spawns will chase you, allowing you to divide and conquer.
Skill recommendations

Bring hex removal skills: Wurm Bile is deadly unless countered by removal, regeneration, or lots of healing. Complicate counters the bile. Hex Eater Vortex, Inspired or Revealed Hex are ideal; the latter two recharge immediately when removing monster skill hexes. Alternatively, Withdraw Hexes removes all hexes from a cluster of allies.
Bring skills that prevent knock down (e.g. "Don't Trip!") to prevent being hampered by mobs of Wurms and Jotun.
"Can't Touch This!" to counter air elementals and Mandragor.
Wurms and Jotun are themselves immune to knock down; Earthbind is the only skill that can bypass that immunity.
The elemental mobs are vulnerable to fire-damage, however there are many spirits of Winter throughout the dungeon that convert elemental damage to cold damage.

Nature's Renewal to mitigate damage and aid in interrupts; avoid using any hexes and non-dervish enchantments. When taking on the wurm mobs, put down Nature's Renewal, flag your team a bit closer to the fight, and then pull solo with a bow getting the agro on you/allies. This helps to keep the wurms from going after your casters and the NR spirit.

quests/quest:gww:14920/sections/objectiv.text: Kneel to water the garden plants. You have [6...0] more plants to water.
Pick up all fallen leaves. [10...0] leaf piles left.
Carry the leaf bags up the stairs. [3...0] leaf bags left.

quests/quest:gww:14920/sections/environm.text: Once this quest is completed, the Seborhin Pests will no longer spawn in the Garden of Seborhin.

quests/quest:gww:14920/sections/walkthro.text: All the tasks here are pretty easy to perform and take place in the paved garden area in front of Mabai.

The groups of Seborhin Pests are all located near to Mabai. To water the plants, walk over and stand by each one indicated on the map, and use the /kneel emote to water them. The leaf piles can be picked up by clicking on them like loot items. Likewise, each of the leaf bags must be picked up and carried to the top of the stairs to the left of where Mabai is waiting: you will automatically drop each bag once it has been carried far enough to satisfy the quest.

Note that the tasks do not have to be done in order: the plants can be watered as soon as the quest is accepted from Mabai as long as you know where you need to kneel, without needing to kill the pests first (the quest log does not reflect this). The leaf piles will appear as soon as all six plants are watered, and the quest log will simultaneously display the objectives for both killing the pests and picking up the leaf piles. The leaf bags appear once all the other objectives are completed.

quests/quest:gww:284735/sections/target-.text: The entrance to this area is right outside the northwestern exit of Tihark Orchard outpost. Talk to Seborhin Protector Zuor outside the entrance in the Forum Highlands.

To be allowed entry, Tahlkora must be in your party, unless the party leader has already completed Abaddon's Gate. In addition, this area is inaccessible if any party member has completed Grand Court of Sebelkeh but has not yet completed Abaddon's Gate. Completion of Grand Court of Sebelkeh changes this area into the Nightfallen Garden instead. Only by completion of Abaddon's Gate will it revert to its pre-Nightfall state.

This area is converted to the Nightfallen Garden after the Grand Court of Sebelkeh mission, until the completion of the Nightfall campaign. Therefore, you can only vanquish this area either before the mission is done (if you completed Nightfall with another character) or after you have completed the campaign.
It is possible to retain access to both this area and the Nightfallen Garden.
Tahlkora must be in your party to explore this area before conversion to Nightfallen Garden.
These quests affect the spawns in this area:
Garden Chores
One Man's Dream
Plague of Frogs
Which Way Did He Go?
Norn Catering
Complete exploration of this area contributes approximately 3.2% to the Elonian Cartographer title track.
It is possible to completely explore this area by yourself during the Tihark Orchard mission, with no enemies to fight.

This can be done at the very beginning of the mission with the use of the Assassin skill Death's Retreat, Return, Recall, Heart of Shadow or Viper's Defense, the Elementalist skill Ride the Lightning or the PvE skill Ebon Escape to get past the guards set to stop your access.

If you do not have access to any of these skills, you can also play the mission until the Harpies attack. The guards will move to attack and you can just pass through them, allowing you to explore the area.
