quests/quest:gww:25517/sections/objectiv.text: Defend the Released Spirits while they escape from the Pit.
Protect the Released Spirits while they travel to the Reaper.
Return to the Reaper of the Bone Pits for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25517/sections/walkthro.text: It is highly advisable to have only one player take the quest while the rest of the party waits near the Bone Pit, where a group of four Tortured Spirits will spawn one by one as soon as the quest is taken. If any of these spirits are killed, you will be forced to go back to the outpost, so make sure that your team protects them. These spirits will attack foes, and actively run to enemies if they come within aggro range.

Almost immediately upon taking the quest, three Skeletons of Dhuum will spawn, one at each spawn point. Shortly after, a group of Terrorweb Dryders (both standard and silver) will spawn to the south (near the bridge), followed by another smaller group spawning to the northeast (by the small hooked pathway). It is important to position your party more or less on the spawns, so that the dryders do not more forward and aggro the Spirits. A third group of three Terrorweb Dryders will spawn near the bridge, further south than the first, about a minute after the quest begins. If your group is fast enough with DPS, both other groups will be dead by the time they spawn. If the Tortured Spirits hadn't taken any aggro, they will have already begun moving towards the Reaper.
Once you've killed the dryders and skeletons the spirits will walk to the Reaper and the quest will be completed.

quests/quest:gww:25517/sections/notes-1/.text: Chained Souls keep spawning in the area. They will draw the aggro of the spirits and slow you down, but they do not pose a threat. There is not much you can do about this.

Sometimes, the spirits will not spawn at all, obliging the players to get back to the outpost. Sometimes, a Locked Chest will spawn blocking the pathway of the Tortured Spirits which will also oblige the players to return to the outpost.

quests/quest:gww:22176/sections/objectiv.text: Travel to Resplendent Makuun and protect the theatre against the besieging demons.
See Prince Bokka the Magnificent for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:22176/sections/walkthro.text: For this quest, Prince Bokka will spawn in the northeastern plaza, in the vicinity of the resurrection shrine, rather than his usual location in the throne room. This is also where the enemies are headed.

When you arrive at the quest marker, four Margonite groups will spawn outside and split up and approach from both sides of the central stairway. Confront the groups on one side to avoid letting them join up; even if the other groups slip past you, there is a delay before they will attack Bokka, so you have plenty of time.

You also have time to set traps or spirits on the stairs before the party triggers the quest start. Take advantage of the natural choke-points (such as narrow archways & stairs) that the party can retreat to and block/hold off the Margonites.
If you have some difficulties and wipe, there is a resurrection shrine near Bokka, so you should still be able to complete the quest.

quests/quest:gww:25277/sections/objectiv.text: Find Melka Blanston, outside of Ascalon City, and tell her that Gurn loves her.Objective for Deliver a Message to My Wife
Find Melka Blanston, just outside of Ascalon City, and inform her of the death of Paulus.

quests/quest:gww:25277/sections/walkthro.text: Map travel to Ascalon City and then exit into Old Ascalon. Melka will be to the left, at the top of the slope.

quests/quest:gww:25277/sections/notes-1/.text: The wrong objective in the quest log for this quest is displayed. It is the objective for the quest Deliver a Message to My Wife, another quest involving Melka.

quests/quest:gww:18617/sections/objectiv.text: Find and enlist four recruits into the Luxon army. [4...0] recruits remaining.

quests/quest:gww:18617/sections/walkthro.text: The recruits are scattered around the area. The map shows the location of 8 recruits, but you only need 4. To get one to follow you (and join your group as an ally), speak to them once and click on the dialogue option. You can lead them back to the recruiter or caravan up to four recruits together. If one dies after joining, they cannot be resurrected, so you have to find a replacement.

Although they do try to keep out of harm's way, they walk slowly and can fall far behind; keep an eye out to make sure that they follow you (otherwise you have to go back for them). To start over, you need to map back to Bai Paasu Reach (which automatically abandons this quest), then re-enter Maishang Hills and get the quest again from Recruiter Lysandra.

quests/quest:gww:18617/sections/notes-1/.text: When you accept this quest, additional Kurzick enemies will popup at specific locations in the area. (Like other popups, these can also spawn additional chests.)
All of the recruits are monks, use swords, and do not activate any skills, regardless of their named profession.

quests/quest:gww:25444/sections/objectiv.text: Find and enlist four recruits into the Kurzick army. [4...0] recruits remaining.
Escort the recruits to Recruiter Sigmund.
See Recruiter Sigmund for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25444/sections/walkthro.text: The goal is to bring four recruits back to Recruiter Sigmund. You can bring recruits to him singly or in groups of up to four at a time. There are eight candidates available, but you may not recruit more than four at one time. If a recruit dies, you can use a replacement recruit from those remaining.

The candidates are scattered across the map. Although there is no map indicator for them, they are in the same locations every time. While recruits are following you, you can trigger Luxon pop-ups in various locations on the map.

The two biggest obstacles to completing the quest are the recruits themselves: they can get stuck on corners or objects. They also move very slowly and can get caught by patrols that your party has managed to otherwise avoid.
You must complete the quest before leaving the map to receive your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25444/sections/notes-1/.text: The recruits can be used during vanquishes or quests as non-renewable fodder.
The Luxon equivalent is In the Army (Luxon).

The quest can sometimes fail after a recruit dies, if the journal fails to update properly to acknowledge the loss — this prevents you from replacing them with one of the alternatives. There is no known work-around.

Despite the profession suggested by their names (e.g. Kurzick Elementalist Recruit), all the recruits are monks and carry swords. The recruits have dialogue that appears to be in response to an encounter with Luxons. However, it can be triggered any time after they join your party.

quests/quest:gww:64463/sections/objectiv.text: Find the Stone Summit camp concealed in Drakkar Lake.
Eradicate all Stone Summit in the camp.
See Orozar Highstone for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:64463/sections/environm.text: Dvalinn Stonebreaker will no longer spawn after this quest is completed.

quests/quest:gww:64463/sections/walkthro.text: Go to the western side of the mountains and you'll start to come across plenty of Stone Summit. Follow the path to their camp, and pull groups away from the others, as they tend to be quite close together. At the end of the camp, you'll come across Dvalinn Stonebreaker amongst other Stone Summit. You have to kill everyone in the camp.

quests/quest:gww:64463/sections/notes-1/.text: Occasionally the quest will be completed without killing Dvalinn Stonebreaker and his group.

quests/quest:gww:23516/sections/objectiv.text: Feed Toma as many enemies as possible in 3 minutes.

quests/quest:gww:23516/sections/rewards-.text: 1 Branch of Juni Berries for every 5 enemies eaten

quests/quest:gww:23516/sections/walkthro.text: Take Toma and attack enemies until they are injured enough for him to eat. While this quest is active, some Mandragors will spawn outside the village along the dry waterway.

In order to get credit for a kill, Toma has to eat the foe using Feeding Frenzy (any foe deaths for other reasons do not count). Toma will only use the skill when the target is at 20% health or lower, which makes the timing tricky. There are several ways to increase the number of available snacks:
Take only healing heroes or henchmen, then weaken the enemies enough for Toma to kill them. This usually provides 10 kills (2 berry branches) each round.

This method can also be approximated by running one's usual setup but setting all heroes to Avoid Combat as it won't prevent the healers and protectors from doing their job but still keep offensive skills available to be called. This will also prevent them from doing unnecessary damage by autoattacking.
Use the quest Undead Defenders to generate foes.

After the Kournan Commander finishes speaking, speak to Chuno to activate Toma, who should have plenty to eat while you attack the incoming foes. Collect the reward from Chuno, but not from Elder Jonah. You can abandon and restart the quest repeatedly this way in order to easily collect many branches of juni berries.
To ensure Toma spawns, wait until Elder Jonah is done speaking, accept the quest, then rezone via Sunspear Sanctuary; Toma will spawn when you return.
Create masterless minions to provide food for Toma without leaving the village; at maximum efficiency, this can produce four or more branches per run.

One efficient method uses two minion masters and a Mesmer/Monk to resurrect them quickly. Sacrifice the first necro to provide a corpse for the second to use for minions. Sac the second necro to make the minions masterless (after which Toma will begin munching them quickly). Repeat this until the time limit is reached.
Call targets and flag heroes a short distance away from an enemy when it reaches 20% health.

quests/quest:gww:23516/sections/notes-1/.text: After the time limit runs out, Toma will return to Chuno on his own.

This quest will not appear in the quest log. Toma will not spawn if Undead Defenders is active; if needed, complete that quest and rezone to finish Insatiable Appetite. (After the initial dialogue for Undead Defenders between Elder Jonah, Tuma, and the herdsmen, Chuno disappears.) After 10 feedings, 20 seconds are added to the count-down clock. However, the total duration of the feeding time does not change, so that it appears that 20 seconds remain when Toma stops accruing additional kills. Make sure you have room to accept the quest reward: if your inventory is full when speaking to Chuno, you will not be able to receive any branches, despite Chuno's offer to "speak to [him] again, once you have made space."

quests/quest:gww:69874/sections/objectiv.text: See Justiciar Naveed for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:69874/sections/walkthro.text: Talk to Glayvin and you will be taken into the Insidious Remnants zone, a quest-specific version of Tarnished Haven. After some dialogue, you will fight the Aspect of Lazarus, a level 28 Elementalist boss.

quests/quest:gww:69874/sections/notes-1/.text: During this quest the outpost portals have no effect. This allows a player to completely explore Alcazia Tangle without any foes for Master of the North.
Unlike most Mursaat, the Aspect of Lazarus does not use Spectral Agony.
When the Aspect of Lazarus has no health left, it will vanish - it will not actually "die" and leave a corpse. As a result, players cannot capture Blinding Surge or any other skills from it.

If you warp out of the area before the fight is over and the quest log is updated, you won't be able to return, because the quest NPCs do not offer the relevant dialogues; in this case, the only way to do the quest is by abandoning and retaking it.

quests/quest:gww:284000/sections/objecti.text: See Xan Hei for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:284000/sections/shared-.text: Your stated goal is to prevent the courier from reaching his vessel in Bejunkan Pier. However the quest will succeed as long as you kill him and pick up his Am Fah Case; it does not matter if he reaches the boat. As he runs to the docks, he will taunt you. Groups of Am Fah will popup along the way and attempt to prevent you from following. This allows you to take several distinct approaches:

Simple: follow the courier slowly, spawning one group of foes at a time. You can use the same 8-member party that has worked for you for other Winds of Change quests (these Am Fah are weaker than most Afflicted groups). There is no need to follow the courier all the way down to the lowest level of the docks. Once he gets to his end point, he can be reached by longbow from the platform one level higher and will merrily run all the way up to you, reducing the number of groups that spawn by three.

Snare: using a combination of Dash (to catch up with the courier), "You Move Like A Dwarf!" (to knock him down early), and Mind Freeze or other hexes (to prevent him from getting away). The courier and his Am Fah allies will heal him and remove his conditions, so you will have to be able to spike him quickly.

Degen: Instead of chasing or snaring the courier, let him go down the stairs. Kill just the first group and then spam health degeneration skills on him. Be careful not to go down the stairs yourself (or let any heroes do so), which will spawn a new group of Am Fah (that could heal and/or remove hexes and conditions). Useful skills include Life Siphon, Conjure Nightmare, and Illusion of Pain.

Shadow step: equip all party members and heroes with a shadow step skill, the remainder of their builds can be as normal. Allow the courier to run down the stairs then kill the first group. While remaining up the top, edge into the corner closest to where the courier stops. You can then shadow step the team to him and kill him; as this bypasses the normal trigger point, the courier does not attempt to run off. If high damage skills are used the team can easily spike him and retrieve the case before the surrounding Am Fah pop.
Bodyblock upon entering dash to the courier and use "You Move Like a Dwarf!" on him, bodyblock him on the stairs as he used antidote signet preventing him from escaping.

Long range damage: Take casters with you and after you killed the first spawn the courier will be standing still. You can hit him with long range damage from the top and he will not run away, if you have enough firepower you can kill him this way.

quests/quest:gww:10599/sections/objectiv.text: See Commander Tanmod for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:10599/sections/walkthro.text: Meet with Scout Dehra outside Dzagonur Bastion and head south with her to intercept and destroy the Kournan caravan. Be aware of the groups of creatures and Margonites along the way. Once the Kournans have been dealt with, return to Dzagonur Bastion for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:10599/sections/notes-1/.text: Combines well with The Search for Survivors to give some useful warrior allies.

Leaving from Honur Hill and killing the Shipment Guard Captain without meeting Scout Dehra first does not mark the quest as complete. You must meet with Scout Dehra just outside the Bastion to get credit first.

quests/quest:gww:11508/sections/objectiv.text: Head to The Breach and repel the Charr attacks.
Return to Warmaster Grast for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:11508/sections/environm.text: The allies that are spawned by this quest will continue to remain in The Breach after this quest is completed.

quests/quest:gww:11508/sections/walkthro.text: Talk to Warmaster Grast and head west until you reach the Hammer Gate where Gate Guard Hollis is posted. Enter The Breach and head towards the quest marker to find Captain West's group, help them fend off three waves of incoming Charr groups. Once all three waves are defeated, return to Warmaster Grast to claim your reward.

quests/quest:gww:14246/sections/objectiv.text: Uncover the fate of The Oddbodies.
See Captain Yithlis for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:14246/sections/walkthro.text: Start from Gate of Fear, which is the only entrance to the Domain of Pain. Thenemi is waiting just outside. From there, follow the quest pointer to the other Oddbodies; you must find each of them before Captain Yithlis will be ready to speak with you. Each Oddbody will follow you as an ally, making the fights easier as you proceed; they do not need to survive to complete the quest.

Although there is no visible bridge between Scout Ahktum and The Lost, the river of souls can still be crossed just like in the mission. Eventually, you will reach the captain; speak to him to receive the reward.

You can talk to Captain Yithlis at any time, however you still need to talk to each Oddbody NPC to get the reward dialogue from Yithlis. If you talk to Yithlis before the last, the Oddbodies will not join you as allies, but instead stay still after being talked to.

quests/quest:gww:14246/sections/notes-1/.text: There is a Treasure Chest near Igraine.

There are two other quests inside the Domain of Pain (given by the Wandering Soul in the Leech Tunnels), namely a Faded Memory and the follow-up A Fleshy Operation. You can use the Oddbodies to help complete these quests. After picking up Igraine, instead of heading to Captain Yithlis, proceed to perform these quest first and then return to Captain Yithlis to finish "Into the Fire".

quests/quest:gww:20061/sections/objectiv.text: Meet your friends in Skyward Reach.
Find Aidan and get a good look at the mesa.
Return to Jorn Kudebeh for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:20061/sections/walkthro.text: Exit Augury Rock to meet Cynn, Devona, and Mhenlo. Follow them on a short walk through Skyward Reach until you reach Aidan at the quest marker, and map travel back to Augury Rock after the quest updates to see Jorn Kudebeh.

quests/quest:gww:20061/sections/notes-1/.text: It is possible to complete the quest just by visiting the target location, without waiting for your allies to reach it.
This quest can be done with no fighting.

It is very easy for Mhenlo, Cynn and Devona to be killed due to the sheer amount of area of effect damage hydras put out. However, their deaths will not cause the quest to fail and it can still be completed.

Sometimes Mhenlo will continue to follow you and heal your party after you reach the mesa. Aidan's second line, "Impressive. I assume that completing these trials will open the way for us?", should be spoken by Devona.

quests/quest:gww:20303/sections/objectiv.text: Seek out Rukkassa in Nightfallen Jahai.
See Keeper Jinyssa for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:20303/sections/walkthro.text: Rukkassa spawns a short distance away from the Gate of Pain in Nightfallen Jahai, guarded by two Terrorweb Dryders. Consider exiting from the Gate of Pain in order to kill the Terrorwebs before triggering the quest marker. After the dryders are defeated, walk past Rukkassa to the quest point. After a short dialogue, he will become possessed and attack, but as a lone monk, poses little threat. Defeating him completes the quest.

quests/quest:gww:10944/sections/objectiv.text: Invoke Saint Anjeka of House Vasburg.
Invoke Saint Melodie of House Lutgardis.
Invoke Saint Perahta of House Brauer.
Invoke Saint Ehren of House Durheim.
See Count zu Heltzer for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:10944/sections/walkthro.text: This is a very simple quest: map (or walk) to each of the Kurzick family outposts and speak to the relevant NPC there, then return to House zu Heltzer for your reward.
The saints are invoked as follows:
Saint Anjeka, speak to Baroness Attia Vasburg at Vasburg Armory.
Saint Melodie, speak to Duke Holtz Lutgardis at Lutgardis Conservatory.
Saint Perahta, speak to Count Archek Brauer at Brauer Academy.
Saint Ehren, speak to Countess Sandra Durheim at Durheim Archives.

quests/quest:gww:10944/sections/notes-1/.text: In the dialogue used by Count Archeck Brauer, he refers to Saint Perahta, the patron saint of House Brauer, as "the most revered ancestor of House Lutgardis".

quests/quest:gww:276657/sections/objecti.text: Clear the Iron Horse Mine in the Northern Shiverpeaks of all enemies in hard mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:276657/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 150 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:276657/sections/instruc.text: "Clear the Iron Horse Mine in the Northern Shiverpeaks of all enemies in hard mode."

quests/quest:gww:276657/sections/target-.text: Travel northwest from Yak's Bend through Traveler's Vale. Alternatively, travel the northeast from Ice Tooth Cave via Anvil Rock.
The Minaar's Trouble, Minaar's Worry, Stone Summit Beastmasters, and The Wayward Monk quests affect the spawns in this area.
Complete exploration of this area contributes approximately 1.4% to the Tyrian Cartographer title.

The Dolyak Riders may prove difficult to kill with their use of Mark of Protection. Consider bringing enchantment removal or interrupts; although, it will also work by getting the Dolyak Rider to use Mark of Protection on another foe before focusing on killing the Dolyak Rider.
Consider coming from Ice Tooth Cave rather than Yak's Bend. Traveler's Vale contains large numbers of Stone Summit, whereas in Anvil Rock you will face only Minotaurs and a few Frostfire Dryders.
With patience, it is possible to bring a party of eight from Temple of the Ages.
Some Stone Summit groups have long patrol paths, so to find them you might need to revisit places you've already cleared.

quests/quest:gww:25311/sections/objectiv.text: Go to the Iron Horse Mine. Sabotage the control levers around the equipment used by the Stone Summit.
Return to Rangil Ironbow for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25311/sections/walkthro.text: After obtaining the quest, go through the portal into the Iron Horse Mine. Once there, follow the map marker to a Dwarven Powder Keg Station, obtain a keg and drop near a lever. While you are doing this watch out for patrols. Drop a keg on each of the 3 clusters of levers to finish the quest, and return to Rangil Ironbow for your reward. Try to drop the keg in the centre of the lever clusters, otherwise it might not destroy all three levers with one keg.
If you are not planning on doing any other quests after this or do not mind the death penalty, a quick way back to Rangil is to allow your party to die and respawn at the entrance to Traveler's Vale.

quests/quest:gww:25311/sections/notes-1/.text: The reward staff possess an inherent +5 armor vs physical damage (and is not due to a staff wrapping). In addition, it can be dyed, unlike other weapons sharing its skin.

quests/quest:gww:204684/sections/objecti.text: Find the traitor in the Iron Mines of Moladune. Defeat him and his guards.
*BONUS* Complete the mission in Hard Mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:204684/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 30 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the first *BONUS* Objective for an additional 45 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the second *BONUS* Objective for an additional 75 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:204684/sections/walkthr.text: As per the Iron Mines of Moladune mission.

quests/quest:gww:275971/sections/objecti.text: Clear the Issnur Isles in Istan of all enemies in hard mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:275971/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 150 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:275971/sections/instruc.text: "Clear the Issnur Isles in Istan of all enemies in hard mode."

quests/quest:gww:275971/sections/target-.text: This area lies between the outposts of Beknur Harbor and Kodlonu Hamlet. The only way to arrive here for the first time is exiting from Beknur Harbor. The primary quest Isle of the Dead leads through this location.
This area contains the first boss in the Nightfall campaign that has an elite skill.
Complete exploration of this area contributes approximately 2.6% to the Elonian Cartographer title track.
Is it possible to explore this area without any foes by entering the quest Assault on Beknur Harbor, and running through the gates from the Beknur Harbor outpost.
Vanquishing this area up to 10 times on an Elonian Support weekly bonus will allow any character to achieve Legendary Spearmarshal.
The Skale Blighters will spread disease so condition removal skills will come in handy.
For non-Nightfall characters (only), there are several quest-related spawns or triggers that are incorrect. These quests cannot be done by non-Nightfall characters yet they affect the instance.
Healer Zenwa will always initiate his speech for the First Born quest chain and the many Mourning Villagers will always spawn.
Troublesome Flamingos for the quest Flamingo-ing... going... gone. always spawn.

quests/quest:gww:10446/sections/objectiv.text: Destroy the fire golems. You have [5...0] fire golems remaining.
See the Emperor's Hand for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:10446/sections/walkthro.text: Exit from Nahpui Quarter into Wajjun Bazaar and head to the Undercity portal, killing any Am Fah groups you happen to run into. (This is a lot quicker if you have Seek out Brother Tosai active, since there are no foes in Wajjun Bazaar.)
Simply head southeast once inside the Undercity and kill the Fire Golems.

quests/quest:gww:10446/sections/notes-1/.text: The so-called "fire" golems are the same as Flesh Golems from the Ring of Fire Islands.

quests/quest:gww:276046/sections/objecti.text: Clear the Jaga Moraine in the Far Shiverpeaks of all enemies in hard mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:276046/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 250 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:276046/sections/instruc.text: "Clear the Jaga Moraine in the Far Shiverpeaks of all enemies in hard mode."

quests/quest:gww:276046/sections/target-.text: Jaga Moraine is directly accessible from the outpost of Sifhalla. An alternative access route is to head north from Gunnar's Hold into Bjora Marches, then walk up the west side of that area to the portal with Jaga Moraine.
This area contributes approximately 6.88 exploration points towards the Master of the North title track.

On rare occasions, you can see a group of Snowmen fighting off Grentches at the entrance of the abandoned village in the southeastern corner. If your party kills the Grentches, they will yield Norn Hunting Party points.
Watch out for ice boulders in the northern parts.
There are 4 Jars of Healing Salve at Egil's Perch.
There are more Vaettir in hard mode; some groups find it more efficient to bring a vaettir farmer to deal with them.

Pairs of hidden Frost Wurms can spawn in six different spots in the northeastern quarter. If you wait to vanquish that section last, you might not have to kill any of them. The Mountain Pinesouls are hostile to these Frost Wurms.
The patrol paths of Mandragors and Minotaurs overlap in certain areas.
There are hidden Mountain Aloes in the southwestern section.
If Kilroy Stonekin spawns and you accept his challenge, there will be additional Stone Summit troops.

quests/quest:gww:276283/sections/objecti.text: Clear the Jahai Bluffs in Kourna of all enemies in hard mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:276283/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 250 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:276283/sections/instruc.text: "Clear the Jahai Bluffs in Kourna of all enemies in hard mode."

quests/quest:gww:276283/sections/target-.text: Exiting via the east exit of the Command Post will bring characters here, most likely while following the primary quest Centaur Blackmail.
Despite having hidden Mandragors spread out in the open areas of this location, Mandragor Hunt is not available here.
Complete exploration of this area contributes approximately 3.3% to the Elonian Cartographer title track.
Be aware that the fortress ramps to the northeast contains several large groups of elite Kournan military. Careful pulling is critical. Anti-melee skills and physical damage mitigation is helpful.
A huge mountain can be seen when looking west-northwest, it is clear when entering from Kodonur Crossroads. It is probably the mountain seen on the map southwest of The Sulfurous Wastes.

quests/quest:gww:205329/sections/objecti.text: Kill Jarimiya the Unmerciful in the Vehtendi Valley.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:205329/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 20 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the *BONUS* Objective for an additional 50 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:205329/sections/walkthr.text: Proceed west from Yahnur Market, down the hills, across several bridges and into the plains area near the center of Vehtendi Valley. Note that this boss is near several patrols of other Heket, including other bosses. It is possible to get to this boss while avoiding the other groups.

Alternately take the easier route, heading south into Forum Highlands from the Kodash Bazaar and hugging the eastern-most wall, where you will only have to fight 1 to 3 mobs of heket. Continue south through the portal into Vehtendi Valley. Head south, around the slope and Jarimiya is directly ahead of you.

quests/quest:gww:275670/sections/objecti.text: Clear the Jaya Bluffs on Shing Jea Island of all enemies in hard mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:275670/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 150 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:275670/sections/instruc.text: "Clear the Jaya Bluffs on Shing Jea Island of all enemies in hard mode."

quests/quest:gww:275670/sections/target-.text: Exit from Seitung Harbor located North in the Outpost or travel west through Haiju Lagoon from Zen Daijun.
The primary quest Looking For Trouble will lead Factions characters here.
These quests will affect the spawns in this area:
Death with Honor, Looking For Trouble and The Rite of Valor.
This area is a popular choice for Feather farming.
Complete exploration of this area contributes approximately 2.4% to the Canthan Cartographer title.
When mapping, there is a small path in the top NW area, where one of the main Factions quests leads to, that may be missed.

The Yeti and the Sensali Tengus are hostile to each other. The Yeti bosses might get killed before your arrival, particularly Ahvha Sankii. Letting them fight each other will ease clearing this place.
There are pigs in this area that have strange animations- it can be seen here.
Gull Hookbeak and Yorrt Strongjaw will always spawn for non-Factions characters, despite the fact that non-Factions characters cannot acquire either of the quests that these two NPCs can offer.

quests/quest:gww:205612/sections/objecti.text: Kill Jedeh the Mighty in Crystal Overlook.
*BONUS* Kill Jedeh the Mighty in Hard Mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:205612/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 20 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the *BONUS* Objective for an additional 50 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:205612/sections/walkthr.text: The recommended way to reach Jedeh is to start from the Mouth of Torment. Take the western exit to the Ruptured Heart and make your way to the portal to Crystal Overlook. There will be a few mobs of Graven Monoliths, Margonites and Giants to defeat or avoid. Once you reach the Overlook, the most direct route to Jedeh is indicated by the blue line on the map. However, this will take you through several groups of Djinn, who can be tough to fight especially in Hard Mode. An alternative that is more time-consuming but less lethal is to turn left after entering the map, and board a Junundu. Go through the sulfurous area in the middle of the map and approach Jedeh from the east rather than the northeast. All the mobs you meet along the way should be small and easily disposed of.

quests/quest:gww:25706/sections/requirem.text: Mutu, the Oldest Child quest not active
Misela, the Middle Child quest not active

quests/quest:gww:25706/sections/objectiv.text: Search the ruins of Fahranur to find where Nehbawa Wahmeh has hidden the family inheritance.
Jedur Wahmeh must survive to recover his inheritance.
See Healer Zenwa for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25706/sections/walkthro.text: After accepting the quest, accept Zenwa's offer to transport you to the ruins of Fahranur. Once you are there, fight your way through the undead hordes to Nehbawa Wahmeh's inheritance, which is marked by the compass point.
Be careful walking around corners. Giant bells drop from above to crush the unwary.
If using a survivor character, beware the boss right before the end - he can hit in excess of 150 before protection on an AL 40 target.
Once you make it to the inheritance, Jedur will retrieve it, and you will be transported back to Issnur Isles.
If you are finding this quest difficult, start in Kodlonu Hamlet, which allows up to 8 party members and provides access to level 15 henchmen.

quests/quest:gww:206563/sections/objecti.text: Take Koss and defend the Garden of Seborhin against the demon horde.
*BONUS* Defeat two additional Harbingers and accompanying foes.
*BONUS* Complete the mission in Hard Mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:206563/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 30 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the first *BONUS* Objective for an additional 45 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the second *BONUS* Objective for an additional 75 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:206563/sections/walkthr.text: As per the Jennur's Horde mission.

quests/quest:gww:204688/sections/objecti.text: Kill Joffs the Mitigator in Riven Earth.
*BONUS* Kill Joffs the Mitigator in Hard Mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:204688/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 20 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the *BONUS* Objective for an additional 50 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:204688/sections/walkthr.text: It is highly recommended to bring enchantment removal skills as this boss will use Stoneflesh Aura and Armor of Earth, potentially reducing any damage dealt to him to 0. Also, make sure to space everyone out accordingly as this boss can wipe out your entire party with just one Shockwave if you're balled up. On the other hand, Pain Inverter can cause massive damage to him when he uses Shockwave, so consider bringing a minion master. Bringing a source of the Dazed condition (such as Broad Head Arrow) is also useful.

quests/quest:gww:204688/sections/notes-1.text: Consider bringing two minion masters. After a couple groups of Raptors you will have plenty of minions, thus making this quite easy to accomplish with the Pain Inverter strategy.

quests/quest:gww:203119/sections/objecti.text: Take Melonni to investigate the deaths of workers at the Jokanur Diggings in the ruins of Fahranur, the First City.
*BONUS* Complete the mission with two Sunspear Ghosts left alive.
*BONUS* Complete the mission in Hard Mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:203119/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 15 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the first *BONUS* Objective for an additional 22 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the second *BONUS* Objective for an additional 37 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:203119/sections/walkthr.text: As per the Jokanur Diggings mission.

quests/quest:gww:203119/sections/notes-1.text: Kahdash is considered a Sunspear Ghost, so the first bonus objective is not completed if he dies. The bonus objective text should instead be Complete the mission with three Sunspear Ghosts left alive.

quests/quest:gww:281004/sections/objecti.text: Clear Joko's Domain in the Desolation of all enemies in hard mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:281004/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 250 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:281004/sections/instruc.text: "Clear Joko's Domain in the Desolation of all enemies in hard mode."

quests/quest:gww:281004/sections/target-.text: The primary quest A Deal's a Deal is the first quest that will lead characters into this area.

This area is accessible via Basalt Grotto before completing Gate of Desolation, which introduces you to Junundu. You can reach the exits to the Remains of Sahlahja and the Shattered Ravines from here by hugging the walls and so avoiding the sulfurous sands, but this is very difficult.
Despite the availability of the Margonite Battle bounty, there are only a handful of Margonite groups here (although you can find more depending on which quests are active).
Vanquishing: 326–438 foes.
This area can take more time to vanquish than others, in part due to the large number of foes, but also because of their resurrection skills. Consider bringing Frozen Soil to counter this.
Arneh the Vigorous will spam Signet of Return; try to pull him within range of Junundu, after which you can kill his group faster than they can be resurrected.

Shekoss the Stony is a lethal earth elementalist grouped with several undead, including Dune Carvers and Acolytes; spread out before engaging to avoid his Aftershock. You can pull the group apart, but you won't be able to bring them within range of Junundu.
Consider going for the above two bosses first and restarting if you fail to kill them without too much Death Penalty.
Elementals are often found in groups of five or six foes, which is more than sufficient to take out Junundu in hard mode; be prepared to retreat when necessary.
Death Penalty removers can be helpful; while inside the wurms, it is easy to accumulate 30%-50% DP without noticing.

You can easily miss a group of Mandragors on a rocky island towards the east; you can reach them by heading southeast from the area below three bridges that are patrolled by insect groups and then crossing a bridge.
Undead and Margonites have potent anti-shout abilities with Vocal Minority and Well of Silence respectively, hindering shout-based builds.
Holy damage can be very helpful against the undead, especially from skills such as Light of Deldrimor, Heart of Holy Flame or Ray of Judgment.
Hex based teams will encounter Hex Eater Vortex from the Awakened Thought Leeches.
During the Halloween quest Open the Flood Gates of Death, you receive six Mad King's Guards as allies and the vanquish is decreased by up to 100 foes (excluding the quest foes).
This area can still be vanquished even if you have abandoned A Deal's a Deal. However, you can not leave from Bone Palace, as the gate will remain closed.

The Wurm Spoor outside the Bone Palace is located very close to rocky ground. Because of this, henchmen/heroes in your back row may inadvertently be ejected from their Junundu right after entering. Check that everyone is in a Junundu before moving out.
If A Deal's a Deal is active, you may not receive credit for vanquishing even if the party defeats the last foe before triggering the cinematic.
de:Jokos Domäne

quests/quest:gww:206398/sections/objecti.text: Kill Justiciar Thommis and accompanying foes in Slavers' Exile.
*BONUS* Kill Justiciar Thommis and accompanying foes in Hard Mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:206398/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 40 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the *BONUS* Objective for an additional 100 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:206398/sections/walkthr.text: Justiciar Thommis is the left most boss on the map. The Stone Summit Warders should be the first target as they have protective wards and can deal massive area of effect damage. The other main target should be Stone Summit Defenders because they have Power Drain and Waste Not, Want Not allowing them to spam protection spells as well as interrupt
Frozen Soil, as most of the Stone Summit have a resurrection skill.
Anti-knock down, there are large mobs of Modniir on the path to Justiciar Thommis.

quests/quest:gww:199318/sections/objecti.text: See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:199318/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 60 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the *BONUS* Objective for an additional 150 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:199318/sections/walkthr.text: Completing this quest requires completion of the Deep, an elite mission. See that mission's article for details.

quests/quest:gww:67380/sections/objectiv.text: Return Kathandrax's Crusher to Swithin Nye in Sacnoth Valley Missing period

quests/quest:gww:67380/sections/walkthro.text: The main issues with this dungeon are the groups of Elementals, bring spell caster shutdown and spread out when facing them.

Go north through the tunnel and head left through the flame traps, then proceed northwest. You need to kill the Infernal Siege Wurm in the trench for the Dungeon Key - casters and ranged attacks can reach it from the cliffs east of the wurm, but you will have to venture into the pit to pick up the key (be wary of flame traps). Head west for the dungeon gate and to the portal to level 2.

Kill the southern Regent of Flame to obtain the Dungeon Key. The southern route is shorter and poses fewer problems for melee characters as there are fewer burning surfaces. After unlocking the gate be wary of the burrowing Infernal Wurm.

If you kill the Becalmed Djinn then the spiders will patrol super-fast around the room, in addition to procuring at least one additional spider group. After clearing the spiders out, head for the gate - just as you reach the gate a Flame Djinn will appear.

Stand your group close to the Djinn when fighting it, as this will lower the damage inflicted by Consuming Flames (equip heroes with melee weapons) and also the amount the Djinn is healed by. Pain Inverter and knock downs are particularly effective. Unlock the gate with the key it drops. Carefully cross the Elemental infested area, heading left when in the room with the bridges and multiple Wurms.

After aggroing Ilsundur, Lord of Fire, 2 lava boulders will appear: One lava boulder travels clockwise around the inner perimeter and the other counterclockwise around the outer perimeter, so flag heroes not engaged in melee in between. Like other boulders they will instantly kill a player (but will not inflict death penalty).

Ilsundur has no natural health regeneration, so he can be worn down with patience if you are having problems. Note that Ilsundur uses Firebomb, which forces heroes, henchmen and even pets to hold a bundle. AI controlled allies will drop it immediately and cause area of effect damage. If you find yourself holding it, you should drop it away from any allies. Also, be mindful of the two lava boulders previously described.

It is highly recommended that when the dungeon has been completed, you wait for the timer to finish counting down so that you will be transported to Sacnoth Valley where you can claim your reward from Swithin Nye.
Caster shutdown - useful against the many Roaring Ethers, Burning Spirits and Flowstone Elementals.
Pain Inverter or knock downs - useful against the Flame Djinn & Ilsundur.
There are not many corpses on levels 1 or 2, so minion masters won't be suitable.

quests/quest:gww:200414/sections/walkthr.text: If you follow the path in the the map posted on the right, you will only encounter Marrow Scarabs, Minotaurs, Rockshot Devourers, and Scarab Nest Builders on your way to Kepkhet Marrowfeast. Hex removal skills are unnecessary, as the aforementioned foes do not cast hexes.

Avoid using condition-inflicting skills on Marrow Scarabs, as they will use Plague Touch and then Virulence. Marrow Scarabs use Well of the Profane, so either interrupt its activation, avoid bringing enchantments with long recharge times, and/or move away from corpses before they are exploited to create a Well of the Profane.

Rockshot Devourers and Scarab Nest Builders use Distracting Shot, so skills that block, inflict the blind condition, cause misses, or prevent interruption can be helpful. They also use numerous traps, so it may be a good idea to have one party member walk ahead of the party to trigger the traps and prevent the entire party from taking damage.

Sometimes Kepkhet Marrowfeast is hidden at first and won't popup until a party member approaches her spawn point. The Scarab Nest Builders surrounding Kepkhet Marrowfeast won't move if attacked from flatbow or longbow range, so you can cause Kepkhet Marrowfeast to deplete her energy by healing and protecting the Scarab Nest Builder prior to your party engaging Kepkhet Marrowfeast. When you go near Kepkhet Marrowfeast, several Marrow Scarabs will popup. If Kepkhet Marrowfeast casts Mark of Protection on herself, applying a condition or hex will cause her to use Contemplation of Purity and remove Mark of Protection.

quests/quest:gww:25349/sections/walkthro.text: Follow the starburst to the Lake of Fire southeast of the Eternal Forgemaster. In the Lake of Fire area, you will run across groups of Obsidian Furnace Drakes, Smoke Walker monks, and a few Infernal Wurms. Khobay's group itself isn't hard to dispose of, but it is next to an Infernal Wurm that can be a problem due to its siege attacks. Pulling Khobay away from it, into a chasm that your team passes through, is a recommended tactic as it blocks the siege attack's line of sight.

quests/quest:gww:25360/sections/objectiv.text: See Kilroy Stonekin for your reward

quests/quest:gww:25360/sections/walkthro.text: Find Kilroy Stonekin in Grenth's Footprint, just south west of exit from Deldrimor War Camp, and escort him to Sorrow's Furnace. Along the way you'll face a number of Stone Summit bosses, but nothing difficult. Kilroy will stay in the rear, and neither attack nor be attacked.

After you enter Sorrow's Furnace and speak to Kilroy, he will begin to run ahead of you through the caverns. Your objective now is to keep him alive. If Kilroy Stonekin dies, you lose the mission and will be teleported back to Deldrimor War Camp. If you exit the Furnace without completing the quest, Kilroy gets teleported to where you first found him in Grenth's Footprint, and you'll have to start again.
The mobs in the Furnace are fairly easy. Just watch that the Priests of Sorrows don't resurrect the dead Stone Summit.

A couple of times Kilroy will start fighting without you, but mostly he'll run to the next checkpoint and wait for you to catch up to him. You normally have time to pick up loot, and, as you draw near to the next checkpoint, to check out the composition of the mob ahead and to cast enchantments before you walk up to Kilroy and start the fight. If you want to stay on the safe side, pick up loot during each battle and keep following Kilroy, who will begin to run to the next checkpoint as soon as all foes around him are dead.
Selecting his name and pressing spacebar to follow comes in handy.
In the final part of this quest, there will be three mobs facing you. Stay with Kilroy — he'll run for the monk boss, Gulnar Irontoe.

When Kilroy stops at his "checkpoints" and waits for you to catch up, it is possible to sneak past him, thus allowing your party to eliminate remaining enemies (including Irontoe) without him engaging.

quests/quest:gww:25360/sections/notes-1/.text: At three times during this quest, an unlocked chest will spawn. Opening it will reveal one to three purple items assigned to random party members within compass range.

This is a fairly easy repeatable quest with a 3,000 experience reward. Characters farming the Survivor title without other players may use this quest for cheap, easy experience. Note that sometime the hardest part of this quest can be getting from Kilroy in Grenth's Footprint into Sorrow's Furnace. Having good running and survival skills can be critical during this part.

quests/quest:gww:63349/sections/objectiv.text: Speak to Kilroy when you are ready to hunt for Fronis Irontoe.
Accompany Kilroy. Find and defeat Fronis Irontoe using nothing but brass knuckles.
See Kilroy Stonekin for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:63349/sections/walkthro.text: Upon entering Fronis Irontoe's Lair, your skills will be replaced with the Brawling build (an extra skill will become available in Hard mode, Brawling Combo Punch). Kilroy Stonekin will fight along side you and use his shout "Kilroy Stonekin". Make your way through the Stone Summit one by one.

At one point, you'll come across an entire room of Stone Summit, but they only turn hostile two or three at a time. Focus on one target at a time (preferably the same targeted by Kilroy Stonekin), as defeating a foe will refill some of your health. If you are knocked down, use STAND UP! repeatedly until your energy is fully restored. If Kilroy KD'd, he will revive when no foes are around. If you just want to complete the dungeon, you can run all the way to Fronis and punch him down, bypassing the blockade by Lieutenant Mahgma and his companions.
At the end of the cave, you will encounter Fronis Irontoe and an Enslaved Ettin. Although you only need to kill Fronis to finish the quest, it is easier if you kill the Ettin first.
Normal Mode tactics
Keep moving. Killing a foe heals you fast and preserves your adrenaline.
Engage a new group with Brawling Uppercut, Brawling Headbutt, or both ready. This takes down their numbers quickly and provides you with healing and adrenaline at the same time.
Save Brawling Uppercut for the carvers and crushers. The rangers are merely annoying unless you're already badly injured. Don't waste these powerful skills on foes that are near death.

Pack a bow, wand, or staff. As soon as you defeat Lieutenant Mahgma, run for the final encounter. Plink the ettin with your bow until Kilroy catches up to you. This preserves (and builds) your adrenaline for the final encounter.

Any customized Flatbow can be used against the Stone Summit Rangers; although it will deal only 1 damage per hit, the rangers will not retaliate and you can (very slowly) take them down without threat of getting KO'd. If you use a Vampiric Bow, you will do 6 damage per hit.
Advanced tactics
When starting the game, run up near the two first mobs and wait for Kilroy to catch up. Run in front of him and attack them. Save your adrenal attack and double combo punch for the next group.

When approaching the second group, quickly attack one of the two first melee Stone Summit Dwarves. Unleash your adrenal attacks on him starting with your knockdown. If you knocked him out quickly enough you and Kilroy should have no problems finishing the rest.

On the third group, run straight up to the ranger on the far right. Kill him and move on to Ettin. Then run up and kill the three Dwarves in the doorway. Unleashing an adrenal chain here is beneficial.

On the fourth group, run towards the dwarf on the right side. Run straight past the wolf and knock him out. Kilroy will follow you, if the other dwarf joins combat, kill him next as that will usually be the target Kilroy attacks. Finish up the wolves.
In the hallway, Kilroy will often die, and so will you. Kill them and move on towards the entrance of the boss room.

Wait for Kilroy to be near you, and move on to the big room. Pull the mobs to the top of the small hill there by the doorway, and unleash a big attack chain at once. If you did this correctly, you will now have aggro and will be defeating the next dwarf. If you are standing on the top of the hill, most of the dwarves will be running in to the middle before running up to you. That means you will fight all the dwarves two versus one, and will be able to finish up the room very quickly. If Kilroy dies, try to continue as long as possible. But if you die, it is very slow to get a good hold on the situation when fighting three versus one all the time. So pull the mobs far away from Kilroy's corpse and resurrect him.

On the first boss group, Kilroy will almost always start with the far left dwarf. Unleash a big attack chain and kill him first, then kill the second. Kill boss last. If Kilroy dies pull him away. The boss will follow you indefinitely while the other dwarves will move back. Kilroy will not move in to the boss room without you being near him, and he will take care of the returning dwarves in the hallway.

In the final boss room, it is perfectly applicable to attack the ettin directly without delay. As long as you pull it a little back so Kilroy starts attacking it earlier, killing it and giving you a health boost. Use knockdowns on Fronis Irontoe instead of the ettin as the ettin is immune to knockdown.

When you are fighting 3 or more foes at the same time, let Kilroy attack first and choose the same target as he does. A quick kill provides you with a health bonus and reduces the total damage you take.

While KO'd and surrounded by several foes, pick the opponent with the lowest HP and use Brawling Combo Punch or Brawling Straight Right as your first attack after standing up. Taking a dwarf down quickly decreases the threats and potential damage against you, gives you an easier route to retreat, and boosts your health.
Additional tips
With assassin as one of your professions, maximize dagger mastery. This gives a chance of double strikes, which give extra adrenaline and a little extra damage.

Your Brawling Combo Punch recharges when you get knocked out. If your energy is low, you can use this to take care of the bosses. However, Lieutenant Mahgma will most likely interrupt it immediately if his Dwarven Battle Stance is active. Instead, use Brawling Block, wait 2-3 seconds, then unleash the combo punch on him.

If Kilroy dies in the room with Lieutenant Mahgma, you can pull the mobs far enough away from him that he self-resurrects. However, this requires that you be under the effects of a consumable-based speed boost (e.g. Rock Candy).
Special considerations for Survivor candidates

The quest is renowned for its part in easily obtaining the Survivor Title: it is repeatable and death is easily avoided. The following ideas are designed for Survivors, but are generally useful in completing the Dungeon. The quest is riskier for caster professions, with a maximum AR of 60.
Be sure to use maximum armor.
There are several useful Insignias and Runes.
Map STAND UP! to more than one key and/or alternate mouse-clicks with the 8 key; this will make it easier to regain your energy quickly, even if you need to recharge it to 140 energy.
With full adrenaline, use the following skill chain for a quick kill: Brawling Combo Punch > Brawling Uppercut > Brawling Straight Right.

Use extreme caution when resigning. You can die a real death (losing progress towards the Survivor title) if you resign while knocked out or if you get knocked out before the game acknowledges your resignation. Try to reach a safe area and map out instead (your Guild Hall is usually the easiest place to reach, using the default keyboard shortcut of [G]).
Maximizing experience gains

Use experience scrolls to reduce the number of times you need to complete the quest. (You need just under 1.2 million experience to go from L20's 140,600 xp the 1,337,500 xp for Legendary Survivor .) Repeating this in normal mode requires about 140 visits, since each run earns about 8,468 experience without scrolls.
You can reduce the number of normal mode runs to 104 runs using Scrolls of Adventurer's Insight.
It takes only 29 runs in hard mode using Scrolls of Slayer's Insight (42,000 xp/run).
The most cost-efficient choice is a Scroll of Berserker's Insight, if you can make it last until you kill Lieutenant Mahgma.
Since experience gain is capped at 300% in hard mode, there is no additional value in paying for scrolls offering more than a 250% XP bonus from kills.
You cannot use more than one scroll at a time.
For farming Irontoe's Chest
You can farm this dungeon without killing any mobs except for Fronis Irontoe.

As soon as you zone into the lair start running towards the group of four dwarves (two archers, two melee) at the exit to the first room. Before you arrive at the dwarves Kilroy will use his shout, increasing your movement speed - this will allow you pass between the two archers and proceed into the second room.

In the second room run slightly to the right of the archer. The three melee dwarves will begin to run towards the exit but if you continue running past the archer you will overtake them and enter the third room before they arrive. If you target the archer he will use one of these three tactics: take no shots and run past and then follow you a short bit, use Point Blank Shot then stand around, or use Marauder's Shot and take 1-2 more shots, possibly including Point Blank shot. Use Brawling Block to block as many attacks as needed.
The third room is relatively straightforward; run past the wolf and melee dwarf, and between the two melee dwarves at the exit to the room.
It is very easy to rubberband if you have any latency when attempting to exit this room. To help avoid rubberbanding avoid getting into melee range with the dwarves for as long as possible.

The archers in the fourth room can cause a significant amount of damage and it is not uncommon to be 'knocked out' near the exit to this room. Hugging the left wall will minimize the time you are in this room and in range of the archers and Brawling Block can be used to negate some of the damage.
There is also a patrol of two melee dwarves in this room (not marked on the map.)
The following room (number five) can be bypassed by passing on the right side of the rightmost allied dwarf near the exit.

As you pass the allied dwarf, strafing to the left can cause any pursuers to get body blocked by the allied dwarves. This is also a common place for rubberbanding (using /stuck is handy to make sure you got between dwarf and wall)
The final room contains only Fronis Irontoe and an Enslaved Ettin. At this point Kilroy's shout will have expired but it should not be problematic to kill Fronis without it.
Ignore the ettin; it cannot be knocked down and does not need to be killed to cause Irontoe's Chest to spawn.
It is probable that you get 'knocked out' once or twice during this fight.
To minimize time between runs:
Map travel to Gunnar's Hold after you have looted Irontoe's Chest.
Accept the quest reward from Kilroy.

Switch districts (switch to International from your district, or vice-versa, if there is only one local district.) or return to the character selection screen and select the same character again (F12, c, space/enter).
Speak to Kilroy, accept the quest, and enter the Lair.
In hard mode this run takes around ten minutes. Rewards:
2500 exp
375 Dwarf Reputation Points
250 gold
1 Locked Chest
2 Aged Dwarven Ale, 2 Dwarven Ale or one of each
Recommended equipment
Dwarven brawling#Recommended equipment
Adding 5x Stalwart Insignias gives you an additional AR +10 against physical damage. If you are having trouble, you can use an Armor of Salvation, Drake Kabobs, Skalefin Soup, or War Supplies.
Regardless of your primary profession, ensure that you set your Dagger Mastery to at least 9.
You can apply useful mods to Thunderfist's Brass Knuckles:
Dagger Tangs: Sundering (for armor penetration), Furious (to recharge Brawling skills more quickly)
A Dagger Handle of Shelter will add additional armor protection.
A "Brawn over Brains" Inscription adds 15% to your damage without any penalties (for this mission).
General tips
You can use items and switch weapons while Knocked Out, since the KO does not count as a Death. Use the opportunity to refresh experience scrolls.
You can damage Stone Summit Rangers using a Vampiric Long or Flatblow; they will not retaliate if you stand outside of aggro range..
Almost every foe has the same health: 80 in normal mode and 200 in hard mode. Exceptions: Ettins, Wolves and bosses.
Kilroy Stonekin doesn't gain health from enemy deaths, he does however have some natural health regeneration.
Attacking the same foe as Kilroy allows you to regain health more quickly; each death boosts your health substantially.

Kilroy is vulnerable to the archers past the second door; try to pull them out of the hallway so that he can survive longer. Similarly, pull the next set of enemies into the archers' now-empty area, so that you need only fight a few at a time. If you find yourself overwhelmed, run away; the dwarves will return to their original positions while you take time to heal.
Treasure Hunters should enter the dungeon in normal mode, grab the loot from the locked chest, and zone out quickly, avoiding any fighting at all.

quests/quest:gww:63349/sections/notes-1/.text: To quickly repeat the quest, you can rezone or switch districts after accepting the reward.
There are several differences between Normal and Hard modes:
The dwarves have 80 health in normal mode and 200 in hard mode.
You have 500 health in NM and 600 in HM.
When a foe dies, you gain 200 health in NM and 300 in HM.
In HM, the rangers use Broad Head Arrow if you have a caster weapon equipped.
If Kilroy does more damage to an enemy, you will gain experience, but any experience scroll effects will not be renewed.
Standard attacks don't affect you, only skills.
Kilroy is affected by standard attacks.
Kilroy does not gain +200/300 health after a monster is killed, so to keep him alive, make sure you lead the way.
This quest is a reasonable way to earn money quickly: assuming you identify and sell everything, you should expect to earn 1 — 31 platinum per run.
As with other solo quests, you may not use summoning stones.
You can repeat this quest to level up heroes if you add them into your party before accepting the quest reward.
During special events, you have the same chances of getting special drops as anywhere else.
If you resign after opening the dungeon chest, you will receive a note stating that you failed the quest. However, you still be able to collect the reward from Kilroy.

If one levels up while knocked down (e.g. because Kilroy kills an enemy) STAND UP! has no effect and you will be kicked out of the dungeon. Unfortunately, this counts as a death towards a Survivor title — be sure to map out of the dungeon if this happens.

As in other areas, locked chests can spawn inside a wall. Should you be able to open the chest but cannot pick up the loot, complete the dungeon and wait 3 minutes for the game to return you to Gunnar's Hold. The item will then appear in the Unclaimed Items window.
Sometimes Kilroy may get stuck on a chest that has spawned in his way, if you lure a Stone Summit near him he will often get free, otherwise you will have to continue without him.

quests/quest:gww:63192/sections/objectiv.text: Speak to Kilroy Stonekin to start the brawling tournament.
Defeat eight opponents in a row to win the brawling tournament.
See Kilroy Stonekin for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:63192/sections/walkthro.text: When entering, first make sure you equip your Brass Knuckles if you haven't already. After the timer has finished counting down, the doors to the arena — which should be quite familiar to you by now — will open. You will have to defeat the eight enemies one by one. The enemies that spawn are random but a good general piece of advice is to go behind a wall if you are facing a ranged enemy and are low on hp. Another good idea is to save Brawling Straight Right and sometimes even Brawling Headbutt until it matters. If you are facing a warrior you can expect it to have Healing Signet.

TIP: If/when you are knocked down, use one hand to "button mash" the number 8 on your keyboard (or the button you have assigned to skill 8), and use the other hand on the mouse to spam click the skill to generate energy even faster. You can also assign additional keys to activate skill 8 and "button mash" all of them to regain energy extremely quickly.

quests/quest:gww:63192/sections/notes-1/.text: Even though this is not specified during the tournament, you are permitted to use Thunderfist's Brass Knuckles instead of regular Brass Knuckles; this will increase your chances of winning.
Though the foes you face are random, research shows that there appears to be a list of foes which may occur each round (for example, the 6th round seems to be a Heket most of the time).

This quest seems to be a safe, albeit slow, way to gain experience for the Survivor title seeing as when you die, you have 10 seconds to either map out or get back on your feet using STAND UP!. Your death counter will not increase unless the timer runs out and you don't have full energy after you get knocked down.

quests/quest:gww:203120/sections/walkthr.text: Korshek's group includes several Roaring Ethers and at least one other Djinn. There are also up to three satellite groups, each consisting of more Djinn and Roaring Ethers. In hard mode, Ruby Djinn can hit very hard with Liquid Flame (over 200 damage) and Korshek follows with Searing Flames which can deal over 250 damage against 60 armor rating characters. This means, even with no death penalty, the entire party can be wiped in two to three hits, as these are AoE attacks. Consider getting the Shielding Branches blessing from the Melandru's Watcher outside of Tihark Orchard to reduce the damage caused by Korshek and Ruby Djinn.
There are several techniques to effectively counter Searing Flames:
Bring skills that interrupt or inflict Dazed.
Use Frigid Armor to prevent being set on fire.
Signet of Humility will prevent Searing Flames from being cast; Diversion will disable it for an extended period.
The boss will quickly kill itself while hexed with either Pain Inverter or Spoil Victor.
Ward Against Elements or Ward Against Harm will reduce the elemental damage.
Winter converts all elemental damage to cold damage, which deals more damage to Ruby Djinns.
Extinguish and Breath of the Great Dwarf remove Burning from all party members.
Frozen Soil will prevent the Roaring Ethers from using Resurrection Signet.

The ethers are the only fleshy foes in Korshek's group, so it does not help much to bring skills that cause Bleeding, Disease, or Poison; similarly, skills that exploit corpses are ineffective for this battle.

quests/quest:gww:203120/sections/notes-1.text: Consider going to open the Do Not Touch Treasure in Forum Highlands after killing Korshek the Immolated, which is near the boss' location.
