quests/quest:gww:14270/sections/walkthro.text: Make the trek into Mamnoon Lagoon from either Druid's Overlook or The Wilds. Once there, you will find groups of Jungle Skale and patrols of 5 Wind Riders circling the lagoon that can be quite challenging for mid-level characters; however, it is possible to avoid the Wind Rider patrols.

Put the message in the log (simply click on the Hollow Log, it's an interactive object) and circle the lake to get to the next zone, Silverwood. From there head west and talk to Alari Doubleblade. Alternatively, if you have been to either Quarrel Falls or Bloodstone Fen, you can map travel and start from there.
When you will have noticed Alari, the Wind Riders nearby may start to attack her. Try to reach her quickly and defeat the foes, otherwise she may be killed and you will need to re-enter the zone.

Note: Although Alari appears close to the Bloodstone Fen entrance to Silverwood, the path to her is actually a lot shorter from the Quarrel Falls entrance which you'll pass right by if you use the Bloodstone Fen entrance. Save yourself some time and take the right-hand fork immediately outside Quarrel Falls.

quests/quest:gww:14270/sections/notes-1/.text: This quest may confuse players playing through the Prophecies storyline for the first time, because when you get to Druid's Overlook in the storyline, you are chasing the Shining Blade to save the Chosen they've kidnapped.
Players should instead take the quest A Brother's Fury from Trader Versai, which will lead them on through the storyline in the correct order.
Alari further compounds the confusion by giving you The Price of Steel, which sends you to Quarrel Falls and can cause you to skip those missions and break the storyline.

Foreigners to Cantha need to speak with First Mate Xiang at Kaineng Docks, who will ship characters to Seitung Harbor. From there, players enter Jaya Bluffs, a pass by explorable area, to finally arrive to Haiju Lagoon at the East. Nagas are found walking by the beach. Zen Daijun is the closest outpost to renew farming runs.
Once obtained, return to any of those collectors and deliver the quest item to the Emperor's Hand at Raisu Pavilion.

It may be difficult to pick up the termite legs as they don't drop as often as they should, but with a little patience, you can farm them yourself. There is a herd of Juvenile Bladed Termites in a river near the west side of the Plains of Jarin (Near the single dark colored island that appears on your map).

When you have the two Juvenile Termite Legs in your inventory, come back to Kamadan and give them to Nenah. She'll give you the belt pouch through the collector screen. Speak to her again to receive the remainder of the quest rewards.

quests/quest:gww:10150/sections/objectiv.text: Bring Tahwaj Zing the head of Xiriss Stickleback.

quests/quest:gww:10150/sections/walkthro.text: Exit Jade Flats (Luxon) into the Archipelagos and head north to speak to Reaver Tammox (just outside the portal). Next, head north then east to the big island. Among the Naga groups are two bosses: the first boss, Ssyn Coiled Grasp, is just over the bridge. The second is Ssuns, Blessed of Dwayna, who can be bypassed by moving along the southern rim and avoiding the small lake. Xiriss Stickleback is at the top of the hill. After defeating him, pick up the Head of Xiriss Stickleback.

Map travel to Eredon Terrace and exit into the Maishang Hills, heading southwest toward the shrine. A stationary group of foes and a patrol can be passed without fighting if timed correctly. Tahwaj Zing is in the village to the east of the shrine, up some stairs, at the back of the village. Talking to him will complete the quest.
Alternatively, skip the conversation with Tammox and head for Xiriss Stickleback directly from Cavalon, retrieve its head, and then go to Tahwaj Zing for the reward.

quests/quest:gww:10150/sections/notes-1/.text: This quest can be completed at the same time as the Ssuns, Blessed of Dwayna Zaishen quest.

quests/quest:gww:25358/sections/objectiv.text: Follow Orozar Highstone to the meeting place.
See Orozar Highstone for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25358/sections/walkthro.text: Find Orozar Highstone in Grenth's Footprint, and lead him to Sorrow's Furnace.

Once inside Sorrow's Furnace, speak to Highstone again, and he'll tell you he's bribed the guards and wants you to find his brother. Follow him through the cavern. You'll fight one easy mob, and a dialog will start where a Priest of Sorrows (accompanied by some Summit Deep Knights) tells Highstone that they have tricked him, upon which they will run away.

He'll remain in one spot, and then you'll face four waves of Stone Summit, including a lot of Summit Deep Knights, Summit Taskmasters, Summit Dark Binders, Summit Surveyors, Summit Wardens, a couple of Priest of Sorrows, and two random bosses (one in the second wave; second in the fourth -- see the entry "Sorrow's Furnace" for a guide to the bosses). There's a brief pause between each wave to pick up loot (there will be a lot of it) and to regenerate.

Tactically, it's probably easiest to stay with Highstone rather than split your party trying to attack each mob as it approaches (they come from different directions). Flag your heroes/henchmen to the one spot. You lose and get teleported back to the outpost if Highstone dies, but the foes will prioritize your party over Highstone. So long as you aggro them before they reach Highstone, they'll attack you even with Highstone in their aggro range.
A resurrection shrine is very close by, so even if the party wipes, you should still be able to complete this quest.

Upon completion, speak to Highstone to be awarded 4000 experience points (which will restore 53% of negative morale up to zero which takes care of most Death Penalty). Gather all drops before speaking to him again for Noble Intentions Plan B.
A minion master will make this quest a lot easier.

quests/quest:gww:25358/sections/notes-1/.text: The Priest of Sorrows will remain allied even after the waves of enemies begins to spawn and if using a minion master he will often ignore his path and return to heal your minions.
Also note that unlike many similar normally hostile creatures turned into allies they will be attacked by the other hostile stone summits and likely killed.
Bosses appear randomly; there is a chance that the boss from whom you need to capture a skill won't appear at all.

quests/quest:gww:25359/sections/objectiv.text: Keep Orozar Highstone alive as he leads you to the exit of Sorrow's Furnace. Bring the shackled Ural Highstone with you.
See Orozar Highstone for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25359/sections/walkthro.text: After the big battle at the end of Noble Intentions, speak to Orozar Highstone again to trigger Plan B. He'll begin to rush off through the caverns. Follow him to keep him alive as you will automatically fail this quest when Orozar dies. You'll face a couple of groups of Stone Summit and find Orozar's brother, Ural Highstone. There will be a cutscene and Highstone will transform his brother into a bundle item.

After the cutscene Orozar will tell you to pick up a master gear to lower the bridge and to pick up his brother and escort both of them out of Sorrow's Furnace. If you're the only player, just pick up his brother for now. He'll rush to a raised bridge. Defend him from the two foes there. If you're the only player, you will have to temporarily drop his brother and go back to grab the gear located by his brother's initial location.

Once the bridge is lowered Orozar will continue running ahead and rushing into battle, make sure to keep him safe. Occasionally he will not advance as he attempts to engage the Stone Summit in the path underneath the bridge. Soon more foes will also come from behind you. You will be defending Orozar in a bottleneck situation, but there is a very limited amount of area of effect damage enemies can do. Fight until Orozar does start to advance. If Orozar does not run in range of the Stone Summit on the path underneath the bridge, you can slow down the enemies advancing from behind by leaving spirits, though this is optional.
If you run too much ahead of Orozar he may switch to walking instead of running. You can prompt him back to running by approaching him.
Eventually you'll reach the exit, where Ural will automatically drop and the quest will be complete. Remember to accept your reward from Orozar before exiting Sorrow's Furnace.

There are two ways to make this quest easier, should your party be unable to handle the Stone Summit numbers or if you prefer not to fight so much. Proceed along the quest as normal until you reach the bridge. Do not lower the bridge, but instead do either:

Backtrack to the starting cave, and head in a northeasterly direction, aiming for the other end of the bridge. You will pass by a resurrection shrine, some heavy machinery, and a big cavern hung with chains. This is aimed at clearing away the stationary mobs before returning all the way to Orozar to lower the bridge. The subsequent run to the entrance will be much easier. An option here is that you bring with you a Master Gear from a gearbox (there is one by the brother and some on the way) and use that to lower the bridge from the other side (saving you the time to run back) - hurry over the bridge to pick up the brother and continue the quest because lowering the bridge will trigger some large patrols that will come the way you used when first entering the brother's cave.

Exploit the quest trigger for quest completion. Simply carry Ural Highstone all the way back to the entrance until he is automatically dropped. Then run all the way back to Orozar for the reward. Keep in mind that the foes on your path, friendly during Noble Intentions, will now have turned hostile.

Do not try to clear the way before activating the quest. When you return to the front of Sorrow's Furnace this room is full of stone summit. Additionally, lowering the bridge will spawn foes at Highstone's location and kill him very quickly.

quests/quest:gww:25359/sections/notes-1/.text: Orozar may get caught in a chest on his way to save his brother. Try to pull some enemies to the spot where he is stuck, and if he engages to fight he will then proceed to his brother. If that is not possible, you are forced to restart the quest by zoning out.

quests/quest:gww:206409/sections/objecti.text: Help Prince Rurik exit the besieged Nolani Academy and return to Rin.
*BONUS* Return the Tome of the Fallen to its pedestal.
*BONUS* Complete the mission in Hard Mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:206409/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 15 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the first *BONUS* Objective for an additional 22 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the second *BONUS* Objective for an additional 37 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:206409/sections/walkthr.text: As per the Nolani Academy mission.

quests/quest:gww:16339/sections/requirem.text: Norgu must be present to continue.

quests/quest:gww:16339/sections/objectiv.text: Watch "Norgu's Nightfall" while it is performed for Academy consideration.
Find out if "Norgu's Nightfall" gets nominated.
Attend the Entertainment Academy awards show.
Receive the "Greatest Play in Vabbi and, Indeed, the Whole World" award.
See Prince Bokka the Magnificent for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:16339/sections/walkthro.text: Leaving from The Kodash Bazaar makes the trip shorter. Then just travel a short distance to 'attend the performance'.

When it is done, map to The Kodash Bazaar and speak with Records Keeper Palin for an update. Map to Honur Hill and walk to the Bokka Amphitheatre. Talk to Bahskir for your update to see Prince Bokka the Magnificent for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:16339/sections/notes-1/.text: Although the initial dialogue does not indicate Norgu as a requirement for the whole quest, there will be pauses during the performance of the play, where his comments would be, and the objectives will state that Norgu must be present to continue.
If you are near the "play" without Norgu in your party, the remaining dialogue will continue, including the acted "Norgu". Only the actual Norgu's dialogue will be missing.

However you do need to have Norgu in your party at the "Receive the "Greatest Play in Vabbi, and Indeed, the Whole World" award." part of the quest, because if that condition is not fulfilled, you will not be able to talk to Bashkir to receive the award. Parties should ensure that Norgu is at least present before entering Resplendent Makuun to attend the awards ceremony.
When "Abaddon" is "killed" he leaves a corpse that can be exploited.
If anyone on the team has the first stage of this quest active Butoh the Bold will not spawn near the Font of Lyss for the primary quest, Attack at the Kodash, to continue.

quests/quest:gww:271155/sections/objecti.text: Slay the Alpha Tyrannus inside Alcazia Tangle for fine, slow roasted Tyrannus Fillets.
Hunt down the Elusive Black Moa inside Mourning Veil Falls for Spicy Moa Wings.
Defeat 3 Ripened Mirage Ibogas inside the Garden of Seborhin for the Gourmet Iboga Salad.
See Lieutenant Thackeray for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:271155/sections/walkthr.text: Defeat the targets in any order and return to Thackeray for your reward.
Start from either Rata Sum or Tarnished Haven. Despite its high level, the Alpha Tyrannus (and the surrounding dinosaurs) can be easily defeated using standard anti-melee techniques.

Start from Durheim Archives. The Elusive Black Moa will escape the first few times you approach, spawning a group of Wardens each time, though most of the groups are easy to avoid because of their location and the delay before spawning (the Wardens are also highly aggressive to the local Mantid). Continue to follow the quest marker until it turns hostile, at which point another Warden group will appear. This moa can be difficult to kill using only spells because it uses Shadow Form.

Start from Tihark Orchard. The locations of the Ripened Mirage Ibogas are not indicated by the quest marker, but the map on the right will show you their locations. Their skills are the same as any other Mirage Iboga, but with a slightly higher Illusion Magic attribute. Note that the Garden of Seborhin can only be accessed under certain conditions.
All three ibogas have to be killed in the same instance; re-zoning will reset the counter back to 3.

quests/quest:gww:271155/sections/notes-1.text: This quest can be completed before or after completing The Wedding.

quests/quest:gww:64480/sections/objectiv.text: Track down and destroy the troublesome jotun to prove Kahmu's worthiness.
See Magni the Bison for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:64480/sections/walkthro.text: The jotun that you have to defeat is Lann Browsmasher, who can be found in Drakkar Lake. The fastest way to reach him is to head south from Sifhalla. Along the way, Kahmu will point out clues. The clues also appear as Suspicious Markings (holding down the ALT key). If you do not see the Suspicious Markings while heading south, Lann Browsmasher will spawn to the west of the wolf shrine. He seems to spawn in three locations:
Near the Stone Summit encampment, the Jotun boss near Sifhalla.
West of the wolf shrine or Curse of the Nornbear mission marker in the cave hallway.
Along the eastern shore of the lake.
Lann Browsmasher will become visible. Killing it will complete the quest.

quests/quest:gww:64480/sections/notes-1/.text: You must start from Sifhalla. Kahmu's hints will only trigger at the first Suspicious Markings outside of Sifhalla. If you entered Drakkar Lake from the south, you must still go to Sifhalla's entrance and then start the quest from there.

quests/quest:gww:278583/sections/objecti.text: Clear Norrhart Domains in the Far Shiverpeaks of all enemies in hard mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:278583/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 150 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:278583/sections/instruc.text: "Clear Norrhart Domains in the Far Shiverpeaks of all enemies in hard mode."

quests/quest:gww:278583/sections/target-.text: This is directly accessible from Gunnar's Hold, Bjora Marches, Varajar Fells, Drakkar Lake and Ice Cliff Chasms. This can be initially reached through Ice Cliff Chasm.
This area cannot be entered until every player in the party has watched the First Vision cinematic.
In normal mode, the low level Charr from the Charr Invaders quest do not count as enemies for the Norn Hunting Party blessing.
Baglorag Grumblesnort's group is easy to miss as they patrol a long route in the northwestern section.
There are fewer foes during Tracking the Nornbear, but more during Charr Invaders.
There are several frost traps near the Modniir in the northeast.
The Modniir centaurs are hostile to the Mountain Pinesouls.
Near the exit into Drakkar Lake, 6 neutral Jotun giants circle two hostile Jotun warriors dueling with each other; you can safely watch the contest from an overlook.

During the competition, the duelers are automatically healed when their health drops below 5%, making them invulnerable. You do not need to engage these other Jotun to complete a vanquish, unless they become hostile.

To end their auto-heal, you must interrupt the event by approaching the ring from the west and aggroing the neutrals. You can pull them into two groups, each composed of a dueler with three of his "fans".

If you attack the two Jotun with a longbow and pull them out of the ring, they could follow the party without losing their invulnerability. If you approach the ring and the auto-healing Jotun turn hostile, it will be impossible to vanquish the area.

quests/quest:gww:278005/sections/objecti.text: Clear the North Kryta Province of all enemies in hard mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:278005/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 150 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:278005/sections/notes-1.text: Prophecies characters who have not completed The Ascalon Settlement can have Mhenlo, Cynn, Devona, and Aidan help vanquish the area. (They will be level 20 but possess no elite skills.)

quests/quest:gww:278005/sections/instruc.text: "Clear the North Kryta Province of all enemies in hard mode."

quests/quest:gww:278005/sections/target-.text: Head north from Lion's Arch or D'Alessio Seaboard.
Complete exploration of this area contributes approximately 1.6% to the Tyrian Cartographer title.
Elemental damage protection can help against the Fire and Inferno Imps. Remember to spread out before engaging them.
Prophecies characters who have not completed the Ascalon Settlement can have Mhenlo, Cynn, Devona, and Aidan help vanquish the area. (They will be level 20 but possess no elite skills.)
Defend North Kryta Province (Hard Mode) in conjunction with War in Kryta spawns may, accounting for the completion of the quest and hidden spawns all over the area, drive the enemy count up to 300.

quests/quest:gww:201196/sections/objecti.text: Kill Nulfastu, Earthbound in Drakkar Lake.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:201196/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 30 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the *BONUS* Objective for an additional 75 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:201196/sections/notes-1.text: The quest Worthy Deeds (Done Dirt Cheap) has this boss as one of its objectives.

quests/quest:gww:204217/sections/objecti.text: Take Melonni and defend the village of Ronjok.
*BONUS* Defeat two additional Harbingers of Nightfall.
*BONUS* Complete the mission in Hard Mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:204217/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 30 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the first *BONUS* Objective for an additional 45 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the second *BONUS* Objective for an additional 75 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:204217/sections/walkthr.text: As per the Nundu Bay mission.

quests/quest:gww:66674/sections/objectiv.text: Guide Erff to a potential settlement location in Arbor Bay.
Help Erff scout out another potential settlement location.
Defend the work krewe from the invading Destroyers.

quests/quest:gww:66674/sections/walkthro.text: Follow the map markers as Erff scouts out various locations in Arbor Bay. The local fauna in the first stage are easily dealt with. However, Erff eventually takes you to the top of a ruined building, where you must defend the party against waves of Destroyers and ultimately, the Shock of Destruction (a Destroyer boss). The destroyers only come from one direction so there is no need to worry about defending the north side of the pyramid too.

When the Destroyers approach, position the team just behind the top of the stairs. While the melee attackers will get to you, the rangers will stay on the stairway and attack, but will not be able to hit you. Take out the warriors and any other Destroyer that makes it to the top of the platform and then deal with those below. Pull back from the stairs after each wave to regenerate health and energy.
Switch to Stout-Hearted against the destroyers unless your Deldrimor rank is extremely low.
Pain Inverter is useful against the boss and the various destroyers.
Group-wide protection and healing skills are helpful for the final battle, e.g. Union or Shelter.
Ward spells are useful here, since the party is defending a particular spot.
Anti-melee skills help against the Destroyer waves, particularly Clumsiness or Wandering Eye.

quests/quest:gww:66674/sections/notes-1/.text: If Erff and the artisans are not outside Vlox's Falls then continue to the pyramid where you will find them waiting for you.
If your party wipes, a resurrection shrine is close enough to admit another try.

If you walk to the first island in Arbor Bay without talking to Erff first, the quest will update and say that you have completed the second objective, even though Erff and the Krewe will remain stationary at the entrance to Vlox Falls. Upon reaching the third location, however, you will not be able to complete the quest without having talked to Erff. If you are concerned about the safety of the Krewe, you can have one player stay at the entrance to Vlox Falls, then once the party is in position on the pyramid, the player who stayed behind can talk to Erff to trigger the destroyer spawn, then rejoin the party. Sometimes one of the destroyers will be caught in a rock, requiring nonprojectile damaging spells to kill it.

quests/quest:gww:25235/sections/objectiv.text: Return to Kasha Blackblood for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25235/sections/walkthro.text: Oberan and four of his minions will advance down the road from the east. Intercept the necromancer, strike him down, and return to Kasha Blackblood to claim your reward.

quests/quest:gww:278201/sections/objecti.text: Clear Old Ascalon of all enemies in hard mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:278201/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 150 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:278201/sections/instruc.text: "Clear Old Ascalon of all enemies in hard mode."

quests/quest:gww:278201/sections/target-.text: New Prophecies campaign characters will enter this area automatically upon completion of the Ascalon Academy mission. Travel north to find the exit into Ascalon City.
Factions and Nightfall characters will need to travel back from Lion's Arch to Ascalon City. See this map.
If a Tyrian (Prophecies) character is present, Sergeant Clark and 2 or 3 Ascalon Guards will offer their help regardless of whether the quest Military Matters is active.
There are many hidden Devourers and Crowns of Thorns throughout the entire area.
Gwen's Broken Flute can be found in the ruins of Ashford.
Complete exploration of this area contributes approximately 1.8% to the Tyrian Cartographer title.
Vanquishing: 200–312 foes. The Eastern portion has numerous Devourer and Crown of Thorns pop-ups.
Most enemies are hostile towards other types of enemies, letting them fight it out can save a couple dozen kills.

quests/quest:gww:14220/sections/objectiv.text: Speak with Sergeant Bokkun about the heket rumor.
See Commander Tanmod for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:14220/sections/walkthro.text: Go to Dzagonur Bastion. Walk out to the Mirror of Lyss, and talk to Sergeant Bokkun. Go back in to Dzagonur Bastion, and collect your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25423/sections/objectiv.text: Travel to Raiyan Cave and kill the bedeviled Naga.
See Headmaster Kuju for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25423/sections/walkthro.text: Upon leaving Shing Jea Monastery, you will find Su standing right in front of you in Sunqua Vale. After talking to her, head north over to Reng Ku near Zhengjo Temple (which you cleared out in your first Necromancer training quest). Once you are done talking with him, you can map travel to Tsumei Village. Enter Panjiang Peninsuala, then over to Raiyan Cave (the cave where your second Necromancer training quest took place).

Upon entering the cave, you will find three groups of Naga. Depending on your level, it may be best to pull some of them away. Once they are dispatched, head farther into the cave and battle the Bedeviled Naga. Once it is killed, map travel back to Shing Jea Monastery and claim your reward from Headmaster Kuju.

quests/quest:gww:25623/sections/objectiv.text: Cleanse the area of Kournans. [5...0] groups of Kournans remain.

quests/quest:gww:25623/sections/walkthro.text: In order to get the quest you must approach Engineer Tosi and a ghost will appear which scares Engineer Tosi. He will then run up the stairs and back down the other stairs in a circle two times before giving the quest. Follow the map to the river ghost Yartu and talk to him to receive your task. Then, travel south and dispatch the Kournan groups. Be careful when attacking; there are many Kournans and Corsair as well as Kournan and Corsair bosses, which may overwhelm even the best prepared parties. Kournan and Corsair Mesmers Shatter Enchantments, Rangers use Whirling defense, the bosses deal large amounts of damage and the Scribes deal AoE damage. Make sure to lure carefully. Once you kill all the Kournan groups, return to Yartu for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25623/sections/notes-1/.text: Yartu will not spawn if the quest Weird Waters is active.
Do not leave the area - you will have to restart the quest if you only partially finished it.
Once you accept the reward and leave, Yartu will not spawn anymore. If you want the items she offers, make sure to bring the Kournan Pendants along.
All 5 mobs of Kournans will spawn at the Kodonur Crossroads exit after finding Yartu. If you are attempting to get the Survivor title, don't use this exit while not having finished the quest.
Even if you finished the quest but left the area before receiving your reward, Yartu will not spawn, making it impossible to get the reward.

quests/quest:gww:25638/sections/objectiv.text: Deliver to Captain Gudur on the Plains of Jarin the proposed Sunspear duties needed during the visits of the diplomats from Kourna and Vabbi.
Inform Elder Belin in the Zehlon Reach of the need for fresh game at the scheduled banquet.
Speak with Stonecutter Ged on the Cliffs of Dohjok about meeting with the representative from the Wilderness of Bahdza.
See Clerk Arlon for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25638/sections/walkthro.text: Enter Plains of Jarin via the Sunspear Great Hall and speak with Captain Gudur, who is directly east. To get to Elder Belin, exit Jokanur Diggings into Zehlon Reach and head north to the village. For the next step exit Blacktide Den to Cliffs of Dohjok and speak with Stonecutter Ged. These are all simple talk-to-and-go-on steps with very little fighting required. Finally go back to Clerk Arlon and get your reward.

quests/quest:gww:14928/sections/objectiv.text: Meet Hedge Wizard Mabai in the Forum Highlands.
Seek the wish grantor using the clues in the ancient parchment.
Find Hedge Wizard Mabai in the Halls of Chokhin.

quests/quest:gww:14928/sections/walkthro.text: After starting the quest with Hedge Wizard Mabai in the Garden, map travel to Jennur's Horde and exit through the east portal. Hedge Wizard Mabai is immediately to your right. After talking to him again, map travel to Tihark Orchard and exit through the west portal. Head roughly south (trend west) to a spot just north of the second resurrection shrine (see the map) to find the dusty urn. It is advisable to clear the immediate area of enemies and spread out your party before interacting with the urn, as the spawns will use powerful AoE that can instantly wipe an unprepared party if it is clustered together around the urn. This is because the djinns will spawn on top of your party and immediately subject it to Searing Flames, Fire Storm and Dervish attacks. Additionally, Mabai will body block and impede the party's escape.

When ready, rub the dusty urn (by selecting it) three times and defeat the Djinn Overseer who appears (along with a Ruby Djinn and 2 Sapphire Djinns). Defeat them and the Overseer turns friendly. Talk to the now friendly Djinn Overseer. Travel to the Halls of Chokhin (inside the Holdings of Chokhin) and talk to Mabai, now Prince Mabai.

quests/quest:gww:14928/sections/notes-1/.text: If you zoom in and look up after turning south you will see a series of jeweled mirrors with rays of light pointing towards another mirror. Follow it to easily complete the quest.
It is not required to talk to Hedge Wizard Mabai in Forum Highlands - the quest will update anyway after talking to the Djinn Overseer.

quests/quest:gww:67929/sections/notes-1/.text: The Area Map incorrectly shows the location of the Dungeon Key on the first level. The Dungeon Key is actually dropped by Xien, and you can only kill him at the end of the first level.

Xien will not spawn without the required quest (Little Workshop of Horrors — obtained from Blimm in Rata Sum), thus preventing access to level 2. You cannot pass beyond the gate near the second Flame Guardian.
Completion of this dungeon will fill in page #13 of the Master Dungeon Guide storybook.

Two bugs can force the party to restart the dungeon: (a) On the first level, the gate leading to the middle area sometimes fails to open. (b) The first floor Dungeon Key sometimes fails to appear after killing Xien. There are no work-arounds for either problem. On the second level, the AI-controlled creatures will attack and kill fire traps. Once they start attacking, you can also cause AoE damage to them.

quests/quest:gww:67929/sections/shared-q.text: In the first level, you must kill Xien to get the dungeon key. He appears and disappears at several points in the dungeon. Just keep heading towards level two and you'll eventually be allowed to kill him for the key. The boss icons on the map for this level mark the locations of Flame Guardians. For an easier trip, destroy these boss Golems to disable the Fire Dart traps along the way.

To obtain the dungeon key you must destroy the Malfunctioning Enduring Golem. In order to destroy the Malfunctioning Enduring Golem, you need to pick up the nearby Flux Matrix and bring it to the Unstable Magical Energy Storage, then drop it next to the Golem to damage it. This may take 2-3 times until the Malfunctioning Enduring Golem is finally destroyed.

In the third level, destroying one of the the 2 Flame Guardians will disable half the Fire Dart traps around the TPS Regulator Golem. Destroying both Flame Guardians will disable all the Fire Dart traps within the area. To make destroying the TPS Regulator Golem easier, you can attempt to lure the Flame Guardians and/or the TPS Regulator Golem down the stairs of the Fire Dart trapped area. After destroying the TPS Regulator Golem, Oola's Chest will appear within the area of the Fire Dart traps, so it is recommended to destroy the Flame Guardians.
The golems tend to bunch up together since they are warriors and dervishes. Bringing skills that cause area of effect damage is recommended.
Minion masters will find that there are few corpses to animate and Skelk Corrupters use Verata's Aura.
Conditions are prevalent here, especially blindness and burning. Skills to remove conditions are very helpful.

Do not confuse this dungeon with the entry in the Hero's Handbook - which is also called Oola's Lab. Despite having the same name, the handbook requires you to complete the quest The Elusive Golemancer.
Insects and golems are both hostile to each other. You can use this to your advantage.

quests/quest:gww:66795/sections/notes-1/.text: If you enter without the required quest, you cannot pass the door in the southwest just before the second Beacon of Droknar.

1,000 Deldrimor reputation points are awarded for completing this dungeon for the first time in normal mode, and 500 points are awarded for subsequent completions (as long as you are below Rank 8). 1500 Deldrimor reputation points are awarded for completing this dungeon in hard mode for the first time, and 750 points are awarded for subsequent completions.
Some Ooze may drop Unstable Gelatinous Material bundles.
The area in the northwest of the map that contains two Albino Rats is not accessible.
Completion of this dungeon will fill in page #4 of the Master Dungeon Guide storybook.

quests/quest:gww:66795/sections/shared-q.text: After accepting the quest from Seer Fiercereign, map to Longeye's Ledge and head for the Ooze Pit in Grothmar Wardowns. Your party can fight its way there or a single character can run there by carefully waiting out the patrols along the way (go east from Longeye's, cross the bridge, and then head south to the dungeon).

Nearly every foe in the pit is a jelly, each of which can deal powerful area of effect (AoE) damage. Many of the jellies will split into two identical foes using Ooze Division: each new foe has the same build as the parent, but half the health; this makes them easier to kill, but allows mobs to deal twice as much damage. Be careful to keep spread out or use a tank to ball up the oozes away from the party. Beware of the rolling boulders that appear at several locations in the dungeon.

At the beginning, the route is obvious: go west briefly and then head north until you get to the first pressure plate. (You can leave it closed while tackling the oozes on the other side.) Once through the gate, you need to kill Gloop to get the Boss Key. There are several possible routes to Gloop, some of which require opening a gate via another pressure plate and some which require breaking down Cracked Walls with Unstable Gelatinous Material, a bundle dropped by some of the dungeon's jellies.

If you follow the route on the map (which bypasses the second pressure plate and second gate), you will approach Gloop from the north and requires a Unstable Gelatinous Material to break down a Cracked Wall. Pull and destroy the nearby oozes before tackling that boss; several can be pulled one at a time or in pairs but there is one larger group. Gloop can be pulled without engaging the four Oozes behind the boss. If you approach Gloop from the southeast (via the second gate using the second pressure plate), you can pull Gloop without having to deal with any other foes. Afterward, retrace your steps and then head to the Boss Lock to reach the final room in the dungeon.

The end-battle requires defeating three Prismatic Oozes, each of which spawns around a dozen new oozes when it dies. In addition, the boss-like foes use Gelatinous Absorption to turn damage into healing.
Pre-cast protections and enchantments before aggroing the group.
Focus on one ooze at a time; call the target to make this easier players and so that heroes and henchmen react more quickly.
Switch targets as soon as you notice an ooze start to heal quickly.
After each Prismatic Ooze dies, you have a few seconds to regroup or retreat to prevent getting overwhelmed by the jellies that spawn afterward.
Killing the third Prismatic Ooze will cause the Prismatic Chest to spawn, which will drop the Prismatic Gelatinous Material that Seer Fiercereign requested.
Skill recommendations
Avoid skills that inflict or require bleeding, disease or poison, or exploit corpses:
The only fleshy creatures in the dungeon are Albino Rats and a very few Stormcloud Incubii (only one popup group will be encountered when following the route on the map provided above).
In addition, Ominous Oozes can steal minions using Verata's Aura and Shimmering Oozes use Spiritual Pain.

Bring skills that can bypass Gelatinous Absorption, i.e. those that cause health degeneration or health loss instead of damage. Spoil Victor is especially effective here, due to the high health of the boss-like foes.
Damage reduction skills help prevent wipes caused by multiple jellies dealing simultaneous AoE damage:
Pain Inverter will often kill a single foe outright.
Pre-cast Shelter and/or Union to keep them out of the aggro-range of the oozes.
Armor of Unfeeling helps to prevent spirits from being destroyed quickly by the various AoE damage skills, such as Spiritual Pain.
See also: threshold damage reduction skills.
Ebon Vanguard Assassin Support can be used to ball up foes and to dispose of Volatile Oozes (those jellies will waste their Unstable Ooze Explosion on the summon).

"Can't Touch This!" can prevent the use of Unstable Ooze Explosion and other touch skills (such as Headbutt used by Aggressive Oozes and Ancient Ooze, and Vile Touch used by Ominous Oozes) on your party members.

If your party does not bring "Can't Touch This!", consider bringing skills that transfer conditions among foes (i.e. Epidemic, Extend Conditions or Fevered Dreams) to transfer daze from Aggressive Oozes' Headbutt to the ooze spellcasters in its proximity.
Letting the timer run out, after all players open the chest, returns the party to Dalada Uplands next to Seer Fiercereign.
If someone in your party doesn't have the quest, Seer Fiercereign won't appear in the Dalada Uplands, so you won't be able to claim your reward.
When Seer Fiercereign does appear, anyone can claim the reward if they have the quest item, regardless of whether they completed the dungeon.
This can give easy experience for the Survivor title track. Simply getting the gelatin via trade and turning it in gives lots of experience without risk of death.

quests/quest:gww:24458/sections/objectiv.text: Find The Hunter within the Domain of Secrets.
Defeat the Hunter. Be mindful of the Pack that guards him.
See Keeper Kauniss for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:24458/sections/walkthro.text: The party will need to explore the Domain of Secrets to find the Hunter. Note that in addition to the usual mobs, there will also be Shiro'ken Assassins wandering around as well. The Hunter himself will be accompanied by 3 Shiro'ken Assassins, whom you must kill in order to complete the quest.

quests/quest:gww:24458/sections/notes-1/.text: This quest combines well with the quest Blueprint of the Fall
When zoning from the Domain of Secrets, you can move into the clearing directly to your south to quickly check for The Hunter in the first spawn point.

quests/quest:gww:20893/sections/objectiv.text: Go north from Ashford to find the road to Green Hills County. Once in Green Hills County, question at least three locals about opposition to the king.
Return to Devona for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:20893/sections/walkthro.text: Head north from Ashford and cross the portal to Green Hills County in the northwest. Near Balthazar's statue, talk to the three closest NPCs, Farrah Cappo, Grazden the Protector and Kasha Blackblood.
You can also talk to Little Thom and Duke Barradin in the Barradin Estate, but since you need three witnesses, you will still need to talk to at least one person near the Balthazar statue.

quests/quest:gww:25265/sections/objectiv.text: Return to Magi Malaquire for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25265/sections/walkthro.text: Head outside into North Kryta Province and follow the quest marker to the northeast corner of the map. Alternatively, you can start from Gates of Kryta for a shorter trip through Scoundrel's Rise, which connects to North Kryta Province very close to where you need to go.

The area marked on the map is only accessible from the sea. There is a path in the cliff that can be entered from a sand bank in front of the shore, to the east of the beach. Usually there is a group of Mergoyles around the beach.
When you head up the hill, you'll be faced with a relatively large group of Enchanted Clay. They shouldn't be too difficult to kill, and using AoE skills will make it significantly easier.

Once they're all defeated, you'll find they'll have dropped 20 Orrian Tablet Shards in total, not just the 5 you need to complete this quest. As long as you pick up the five you need, you don't need any more: you won't get an extra reward for it. Once you've collected what you need, head back to Magi Malaquire to collect your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25265/sections/notes-1/.text: Upon completion, Magi Malaquire will take all the shards in your inventory. If you wish to keep any extras, put them in storage or give them to a different character first.

quests/quest:gww:14271/sections/objectiv.text: Search the Ascalon Foothills for Oswalt's Headstone.
Inscribe Elsa's words on the headstone.
See Oswalt Alston for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:14271/sections/walkthro.text: Leave Traveler's Vale to the southeast and enter The Ascalon Foothills. Oswalt's grave can be found in the northern portion of the Foothills.

quests/quest:gww:14271/sections/notes-1/.text: The epitaph reads, "Oswalt Alston. Loving husband in life. Savior in death. My strength. My inspiration. My love."
When acquiring this quest, occasionally it will immediately update to indicate that you have completed the second objective ("Inscribe Elsa's words on the headstone"), but not the first objective.

quests/quest:gww:10070/sections/objectiv.text: Clear the Jade Quarry of all Outcast raiders. You have [5...0] groups remaining.
See Great Reaver Rixor for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:10070/sections/environm.text: While this quest is active, two additional groups of Outcasts will spawn in areas unreachable by foot in Unwaking Waters (even though none of the quest objectives take place there): one on the path traversed during the mission, the other inside the Kurzick outpost.

quests/quest:gww:10070/sections/walkthro.text: After receiving the quest from Rixonon, map to Seafarer's Rest and speak to Rixor, then exit via the northeastern portal into Rhea's Crater where the jade quarry is located. Rion is standing just outside along with his party: Khim, Ting and Hannai.

After you have spoken to Rion, the quest pointer will be updated to indicate the first Outcast group you must find and defeat. Simply follow your quest pointer to each of the five groups and eliminate them all, but be wary of overlapping patrol routes. It can be helpful to stay back and observe the movements of hostile groups before attacking, luring single groups towards the party whenever possible.
Once complete, return to Seafarer's Rest and collect your reward from Rixor.

quests/quest:gww:10070/sections/notes-1/.text: Note that although Rion's group will follow the party and fight any creatures, they do not join the party as allies, and it is not necessary for any of them to survive to complete the quest. That said, their assistance can complete fights more quickly, and Ting uses his healing spells on the party.
Note at each checkpoint, there are two or three groups. For the quest to complete, you may not need to kill all the groups, sometimes one group is sufficient.

quests/quest:gww:280328/sections/objecti.text: Clear Panjiang Peninsula on Shing Jea Island of all enemies in hard mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:280328/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 150 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:280328/sections/instruc.text: "Clear Panjiang Peninsula on Shing Jea Island of all enemies in hard mode."

quests/quest:gww:280328/sections/target-.text: This area lies to the southwest of Tsumei Village. Several early profession-related quests will lead players here.
These Shing Jea Island quests will affect the spawns in this area:
Cash Crops
Quimang's Last Stand
Reaping the Naga
Shackled Spirits
Sparring Elements
The Box of Illusions
The Crop Thieves
The Siege at Tsumei Village
The Threat Grows
These festival quests will also affect the spawns in this area:
Darkness at Kaitan
Hopeless Romantic
Just My Luck
The Big Bang
Complete exploration of this area will yield approximately 3.3% to the Canthan Cartographer title track.
Kappa and Crimson Skull are hostile to each other, though their patrols only overlap in a small area.
Vanquishing: 131–235 foes.
Skills like Shelter, Union, Shield of Absorption, and Protective Spirit are highly recommended as this area is populated by numerous Elementalists and damage-dealing Ritualists.

The vast majority of damage dealt by foes in this area comes from projectile attacks and/or projectile spells. Conveniently, the area's naturally hilly/mountainous terrain makes it very easy to break line of sight.
Mantra of Frost and Mantra of Lightning are also very effective in this area due to the prevalence of cold and lightning damage.
Without active quests the area east of the Tsumei Village entrance doesn't have any enemies.
A hidden Naga group in Raiyan Cave will spawn if one ventures close to the waterline at the southern edge of the cave.
A hidden pair of Kappa will appear if one ventures along the beach immediately north of Pei the Skull Blade's ship. There's another hidden Kappa group south of Kaitan Village, on the sandy beach.
Naga groups will also appear if one traverses the water along the western edge.

Starting from the resurrection shrine along the southern edge west of Raiyan Cave, and at several points along the path towards and around Port Kaimu, are many hidden groups of Crimson Skull. At least one of the hidden groups at Port Kaimu may be required to be killed in order for the vanquish to complete.
There are two hidden Lesser Oni in this area:
On the southwestern sandy beach.
Along the curving mountain path west of Losai Hapatu, the Kappa Shell collector.
The Lesser Oni that spawns west of Losai Hapatu has to be killed to complete the vanquish even when it is still hidden.
Vanquishing during Darkness at Kaitan (during the Dragon Festival) produces some spawn changes.
Naga groups spawn in the village, in groups of five.
Raiyan Cave is filled with groups of 1-2 Lesser Grasps.
The "s"-shaped area east of the bridge on the southern edge of the map is empty - this eliminates several closely packed groups of Crimson Skull.
Overall, the result is a slight reduction in the total number of foes.
Vanquishing during Togo's Ultimatum will affect the spawns in this area.
The Crimson Skull at the harbor will not turn hostile and Cho Wei the Skull Axe does not spawn.
The bridge after the "s"-like mountain will not have Crimson Skull popup.

quests/quest:gww:9631/sections/walkthrou.text: Leaving from Kaineng City, head directly southeast through Bukdek Byway and cross the bridge to receive the quest from Minister Tahlen, then talk to Minister Khannai who is nearby. Map travel to The Marketplace, exit south into Wajjun Bazaar and talk to Minister Baasong who is just outside the portal. Head back through the marketplace to the northeast over the bridge to talk to Minister Onghsang. Map travel to Nahpui Quarter (outpost) and exit north into Wajjun Bazaar, following the last quest marker to talk to Guardsman Pah to receive the quest reward.

quests/quest:gww:278457/sections/objecti.text: Clear Perdition Rock in the Ring of Fire Islands of all enemies in hard mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:278457/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 250 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:278457/sections/instruc.text: "Clear Perdition Rock in the Ring of Fire Islands of all enemies in hard mode."

quests/quest:gww:278457/sections/target-.text: The Final Blow primary quest will take characters through this area on their way to the next mission outpost.
You can get the Volcanic Rock for the Black Moa Chick from the northeast part of this area.
Watch out for Mahgo Hydras with their Meteor Shower. They can also do massive damage through other fire skills.
Martial Professions will want to bring a way to deal with Blind as Phantoms pop up throughout the zone.
Caster Professions will also want to bring a way to deal with Interrupts as Phantoms carry 3 with one of them being Cry of Frustration which is an area of effect interrupt.
Titles
Complete exploration of this area contributes approximately 1.2% to the Tyrian Cartographer title track.
Vanquishing: 215–252 foes.
There are less foes after accepting the quest reward for Final Blow.
Having Proof of Triumph in the inventory will make a further group with Abaddon's Cursed spawn.
Not all of the elite skills are available for capture in any one instance of the map.
Bosses
Not all bosses listed above will spawn in the same map instance. Generally, only one boss will spawn at each spawn point.
Any spawn point may spawn more than one boss.
Occasionally no boss spawns at a spawn point for Abomination or Ghost bosses.
Sometimes, not all of the Phantom bosses will spawn.
Harn and Maxine Coldstone will not spawn in the same instance.
Since there are four spawn points shared by the Ettin boss and two Hydra bosses, one of the spawn points will be empty.

An easy way to capture the elite skills of the Ghost and Abomination bosses is to exit from Ember Light Camp and then run to the first boss location to the east (one or two bosses will spawn there). If the boss you are looking for is not there then rezone. This could take many tries since there are 5 Abominations and 3 Phantom bosses and their spawn is random.

quests/quest:gww:14618/sections/objectiv.text: Travel to Shing Jea Monastery and get a kappa trap for Farmer Zinhao.
See Farmer Zinhao for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:14618/sections/walkthro.text: Map travel to Shing Jea Monastery and talk to Suhkaro. Return to Farmer Zinhao in Panjiang Peninsula for your reward. He may not be present, if you have already got an active quest in the area.

quests/quest:gww:65490/sections/objectiv.text: Escort the ghost Ganji to the spot Krahm fell.
Guide the wandering spirits to Allura's last resting place.
Walk to the spot where Shandara and her daughter were lost.
Reunite the spirits with Shahin to complete the pilgrimage.

quests/quest:gww:65490/sections/environm.text: Upon completing this quest, Allura, Ganji, Krahm, Shahin, and Shandara will be placed outside Augury Rock, finally completing their Pilgrimage.

quests/quest:gww:65490/sections/walkthro.text: Ganji is in The Ruptured Heart near the southwestern exit into the Alkali Pan. After you accepted the quest, just follow the quest markers. To complete the last objective and reach Shahin you need a Junundu. There is a Wurm Spoor southeast from the quest marker (right of the writing "The Ruptured Heart"). Alternatively just follow the path on the map.

quests/quest:gww:25709/sections/requirem.text: Guild Wars factions on the account
Mhenlo's Request neither active nor completed
You must also have completed and accepted the reward for The Time is Nigh

quests/quest:gww:25709/sections/objectiv.text: Speak to Funwa Shento in Kamadan, Jewel of Istan to be directed to Mhenlo.
Speak to Mhenlo at the Consulate Docks to learn about what is occurring in Cantha.
Tell Mhenlo when you are ready to leave for Cantha.
Find Dockhand Quangnai to learn more about the situation in Cantha.

quests/quest:gww:25709/sections/walkthro.text: Just follow the radar indicators. There will be no fights in this quest. Although this can be done solo, players may want to bring lower level heroes to make the most of the experience received.

quests/quest:gww:25709/sections/notes-1/.text: This quest unlocks Kaineng City port (once you have arrived at Bejunkan Pier).

A Nightfall character with this quest can ferry characters of any level (from any Campaign) to Cantha, provided that they have the Consulate Docks unlocked (i.e. by either having completed The Time is Nigh themselves, or having previously received a ferry to the docks from Kamadan via that quest).
You can be taken to Benjunkan Pier by Mhenlo multiple times without restarting the quest and even after accepting the reward. There is no reason to keep this quest in your log.
Ferried characters can map travel to Kaineng Center right away and do not have to walk there.

In order to take the follow-up quest, Welcome to Cantha, you must either accept the reward for this quest or abandon it. You can also skip Welcome to Cantha if you are ferried into Vizunah Square (Foreign Quarter) by another character with that quest.
See Campaign travel and Ferry for additional information.

quests/quest:gww:206188/sections/objecti.text: Kill Plague of Destruction and accompanying foes in Raven's Point.
*BONUS* Kill Plague of Destruction and accompanying foes in Hard Mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:206188/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 40 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the *BONUS* Objective for an additional 100 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:206188/sections/walkthr.text: As per Defending the Breach. Note that unlike that quest, you have to defeat all the Destroyers in the final room to finish this (as with spawning the chest).

quests/quest:gww:21030/sections/objectiv.text: Kill the heket in the Garden of Seborhin. You have X of 10 groups remaining.
See Horticulturist Hinon for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:21030/sections/walkthro.text: This quest is a simple process of following the pointer to each group of heket, and eliminating them. These heket groups are in addition to those that normally spawn in this area. These new groups are located around or inside the garden compound. The plague cannot be done when the garden is under nightfall so do it before you trigger that or after you have completed the campaign.

quests/quest:gww:21030/sections/notes-1/.text: After receiving the quest, it's a good idea to speak to the Vabbian Scout nearby, since he has a Heket Hunt blessing which will earn sunspear promotion points for any player taking it.
This quest cannot be completed in Nightfallen Jahai. If Nightfall has occurred, you must complete the campaign before completing this quest.

quests/quest:gww:276774/sections/objecti.text: Clear the Plains of Jarin in Istan of all enemies in hard mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:276774/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 150 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:276774/sections/instruc.text: "Clear the Plains of Jarin in Istan of all enemies in hard mode."

quests/quest:gww:276774/sections/target-.text: The Plains of Jarin connects Kamadan and three other outposts. Leaving Kamadan for the first time using the northwestern exit will bring players here. A variety of quests available in Kamadan and the Sunspear Great Hall lead to and take place here.
The Juvenile Bladed Termites are passive. There's a large group of them in the western waters. Watch out for the lone hostile Irontooth Drake in their midst.
Complete exploration of this area contributes approximately 2.7% to the Elonian Cartographer title.
Be careful with the hidden mandragor groups near Tarom Rockbreaker; the boss itself is part of a hidden group.

This area will yield about 1,800 Sunspear Promotion Points with all bounties. When vanquishing with non-Elonian characters this area will offer Istani bounties as long as you are below Sunspear rank 6. A Land of Heroes is the easier method for non-Elonian characters to reach rank 6.
If the quest Zaishen Elite is active, you must defeat the two Acolytes to successfully vanquish the area.
The festival quest White Mist adds three allied Humbugs to your team.
It is possible to vanquish this area with a party of eight members. See Kamadan, Jewel of Istan notes for details.
It is also possible to get a party of eight members from the Sunspear Great Hall under the same conditions after completing Blacktide Den mission.

quests/quest:gww:69323/sections/objectiv.text: Meet Vael at the rendezvous point in Grothmar Wardowns.
Get into position and wait for Vael to create a diversion. Do not alert the Charr in the camp to your presence.
Run in and steal the plans while Vael keeps the Charr busy.
Take the plans back to Captain Langmar.
Don't forget the plans! (If the plans are dropped.)
If zoning in with a party member who has never spoken to Vael:
Vael is not ready to undertake the covert mission. He has still not made himself known to one of your party members.
If zoning in with a party member who has spoken to Vael but has not completed Be Very, Very Quiet...:

Vael is not ready to undertake the covert mission. He is busy following a suspicious looking Charr. Help your party member discover what that Charr is up to, and then Vael will be ready to raid the Charr camp for plans.

quests/quest:gww:69323/sections/walkthro.text: After speaking with Vael, the party waits on a bluff close by while he runs to the Charr camp and lures them away. A large group will follow Vael once he challenges them, wait a few seconds and a lingering group of four or more Charr will run out after them. Once the Charr have left, the Battle Plans are easily attainable. Return them to Captain Langmar for the reward.
Note that the Battle Plans are a bundle item, and that you will not be able to map travel back to Longeye's Ledge without losing it. Also, don't wait too long, because those Charr do come back.

quests/quest:gww:69323/sections/notes-1/.text: Avoid lingering in the camp too long as the Charr will return shortly.
There is usually a Locked Chest in the camp near the plans.
The Battle Plans can be carried while in Siege Devourer form, but the Devourer's standard ranged spacebar attack cannot be used.

Vael will sometimes get stuck, and not lure the Charr as the quest suggests. If this occurs, simply zone in and out of nearby Sacnoth Valley and try talking to him again. You may receive a "QUEST FAILED" message upon retrieving the plans. The quest reward can still be collected upon returning them to Captain Langmar

quests/quest:gww:278625/sections/objecti.text: Clear the Pockmark Flats in Ascalon of all enemies in hard mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:278625/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 50 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:278625/sections/instruc.text: "Clear the Pockmark Flats in Ascalon of all enemies in hard mode."

quests/quest:gww:278625/sections/target-.text: Several secondary quests of the Ascalon region lead here. This area is located south of the Eastern Frontier and due east of Serenity Temple.
There is a resurrection point just inside the small walled area near the Serenity Temple portal, but no visible shrine.
Complete exploration of this area contributes approximately 1.6% to the Tyrian Cartographer title.
These quests will affect the spawns in this area:
Vanquishing: 135–234 foes. There are numerous Devourer pop-ups throughout the zone, with a large number in the northern valley surrounding the Searing Crystal.
The Geomancer's Test will significantly increase the number of foes, and Replacement Healers will add Devona as an ally.
There appear to be three variations of spawns in the crater valley; you should be able to tell which shortly after exiting Serenity Temple:

Riders: Patrols of Storm Riders swirl around crevices, and then circle the valley counter-clockwise around the crystal; there is a separate group that stays near the center. When vanquishing, move clockwise to avoid missing any. (Rough estimate: 80% of visits.)
Elementals: The crater contains patrols of Stone Elementals instead. (Roughly 10% of visits.)
Gargoyles: The spawns are gargoyles and there appear to be fewer devourer pop-ups. (Roughly 10% of visits.)
The collector Nicanor Gannel does not always appear; his presence might be tied to the type of spawns in the crystal valley.

quests/quest:gww:275616/sections/objecti.text: *BONUS* Complete the mission in Hard Mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:275616/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 30 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the first *BONUS* Objective for an additional 45 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the second *BONUS* Objective for an additional 75 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:275616/sections/walkthr.text: As per the Pogahn Passage mission.

quests/quest:gww:275616/sections/notes-1.text: The quest reward is greater than that of other Zaishen quests from the region.

quests/quest:gww:278835/sections/objecti.text: Clear the Poisoned Outcrops in the Desolation of all enemies in hard mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:278835/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 250 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:278835/sections/instruc.text: "Clear the Poisoned Outcrops in the Desolation of all enemies in hard mode."

quests/quest:gww:278835/sections/target-.text: Head out the northeastern exit of either the Lair of the Forgotten or the Ruptured Heart.
This is the only area in the Desolation where Junundu are not available.
Complete exploration of this area contributes approximately 2.4% to the Elonian Cartographer title track.
There's a small group of hidden insects at the end of the northern path just out of the Lair of the Forgotten. They can be avoided simply by not using that short central path.

The boss group of Droajam, Mage of the Sands is, by far, the most difficult group to take down. It consists of the boss itself plus 4 other elementals (Sandstorm Crag and Shambling Mesa, usually more of the former). The sheer damage that they can dish out at once can wipe even a well-prepared party several times. Focusing on one at a time and spreading out wide is essential to taking them down. Alternatively, a well-timed Pain Inverter will also usually kill the boss and Sandstorm Crags in one Sandstorm, especially if using spirits/minions/pets (which can also act as a decoy).

Just west of the Lair of the Forgotten are several very closely placed groups of undead, possibly overlapping with a Margonite group as well. Carefully pull each group into the narrow path before fully engaging them. The boss group containing Nehjab the Parched may be difficult to take down; it depends on the number of Awakened Acolytes and Awakened Cavaliers there are. Consider skills like Frozen Soil.
Both the Hallowed Point and the Growing Threat quests will significantly increase the number of Margonite spawns, although the latter also provides some allies.

quests/quest:gww:25368/sections/requirem.text: Enter Sorrow's Furnace without To Sorrow's Furnace sub quests.

quests/quest:gww:25368/sections/objectiv.text: Find and slay 6 more Stone Summit leaders.
See Tharn Stonerift for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25368/sections/walkthro.text: Find and kill six bosses within Sorrow's Furnace. The quickest way to complete the quest is to kill the two bosses in the same chamber as Tharn Stonerift (Sorrow's Belly), take the southwestern path to the Stone Basilica and kill the two bosses there, and then return to Sorrow's Belly, take the east path, and turn south at the fork to clear out the Iron Arch and its two bosses.
Turning north at the fork and following the sparsely-populated crescent passage (the Gap) leads to another two bosses, which may be a preferable alternative to clearing the more enemy-dense Basilica.

quests/quest:gww:25368/sections/notes-1/.text: This quest requires killing exactly half of the bosses in Sorrow's Furnace.
Any bosses killed before you accept the quest are retroactively counted towards the objective, potentially allowing the reward to be claimed immediately.
If a boss is resurrected (e.g. by a Priest of Sorrows), killing him again will not affect the counter.
The northwestern boss can sometimes wander into the crushers, providing a free kill.

Like many monk NPCs, Tharn can sometimes travel long distances with the party to provide healing, particularly if there is a minion master present. However, this may do more harm than good, since Tharn will also heal and cleanse conditions on enemies, including his supposed rivals.
This quest can easily be completed alongside Tasca's Reprise or Subversive Ideas, since both require exploring most of the dungeon.
As with other quests offered inside Sorrow's Furnace, this quest is automatically abandoned if you leave the zone.

quests/quest:gww:67930/sections/objectiv.text: Defeat Blarp in a game of Polymock at Gadd's Encampment.
See Hoff [Polymock Master] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:67930/sections/walkthro.text: Blarp's pieces and their unique skills are as follows:
Earth Elemental: Polymock Stone Daggers, Polymock Obsidian Flame, Polymock Earthquake
Ice Elemental: Polymock Ice Spear, Polymock Frozen Armor, Polymock Glyph Freeze
Fire Elemental: Polymock Flare, Polymock Fireball, Polymock Rodgort's Invocation
The following pieces are good counters:
Kappa Polymock piece vs. Earth Elemental Polymock piece
Fire Imp Polymock piece vs. Ice Elemental Polymock piece
Skale Polymock piece vs. Fire Elemental Polymock piece
Skale Polymock piece vs. Earth Elemental Polymock piece
Gargoyle Polymock piece vs. Ice Elemental Polymock piece
Kappa Polymock piece vs. Fire Elemental Polymock piece

Blarp can be quite difficult to defeat as he uses three Uncommon pieces (and you're likely to only have one, the Kappa). Be sure to Block/Drain the two most important skills of each piece. The latter is more powerful.
These are the skills to watch out for:
Earth Elemental: Earthquake (650 damage, 6 energy, 1 activation, 20 recharge), Obsidian flame (800 damage, 6 energy, 1 activation, 20 recharge)
Ice Elemental: Frozen Armor (+1000 Health for 30 seconds, 2 energy, 2 activation, 20 recharge), Glyph Freeze (600 damage, 6 energy, 1 activation, 20 recharge
Fire Elemental: Fireball (800 damage, 6energy, 1activation, 20recharge), Rodgort's Invocation (200 damage, 10 degeneration for 15 seconds, 2energy, 2activation, 20recharge)
Keep in mind that by strafing (walking from side to side) you can avoid getting hit by projectiles such as Polymock Stone Daggers, Ice Spear, Flare and Fireball.

quests/quest:gww:67930/sections/support-.text: Before you can participate in Polymock matches, you must first obtain three starter pieces from Hoff in Rata Sum and then register them with Denn. Each registration removes the Polymock piece from your inventory and is permanently tied to your character (as opposed to your account). Do not register the piece if you plan on trading it to another character.
Rules

Once you have the three starter pieces, you can do the quest chain which starts from Polymock: Defeat Yulma. The objective of a Polymock match is to kill all three of your opponent's pieces before they kill yours.

After defeating the designated opponent (i.e. completed the quest and accepted the reward), you can return to those you have defeated and challenge them to a match under tournament rules. The one difference is that you are required to choose your Polymock pieces from all three rarities (white, purple, gold). If you did not register at least one Polymock piece for each rarity, you cannot challenge opponents using tournament rules. Winning such Polymock matches will earn you from 40 to 90 Asuran reputation points, depending on who you challenged.
Polymock takes place in several special explorable areas, depending on which region the opponent is found in:
Polymock Coliseum in the Tarnished Coast.
Polymock Glacier in the Far Shiverpeaks.
Polymock Crossing in the Charr Homelands.
Tournament Rules

After completing all polymock quests, you must play by tournament rules. The game is played with 3 pieces of different rarities polymock. To play, you must have 1 common piece, 1 uncommon piece and 1 rare piece.
You win 90 Asuran reputation points for defeating Fonk, Volumandus, Teardrinker, Silverfist or Hoff, 80 points for defeating Blarp, 60 points for Plurgg and 40 points for Yulma.
For maxing the Asuran title
1 Win 90 points. 1 match lasts 5 minutes.

It will take approximately 74 hours to reach tier 8 of the Asuran title if Asuran reputation points are gained exclusively using Polymock matches. No points are awarded past tier 8 therefore it is impossible to max the Asuran title by Polymock exclusively.
Preparation

Talk to Wokk to choose the three Polymock pieces that you want to use. After selecting your three pieces, you are then asked to select which of the three to start with. You are allowed to examine your skill bar before each round begins. Note that the platforms your piece and your opponent's piece are standing on are close to each other and that it is impossible to move out of range (although strafing to dodge projectiles is possible). Your character is replaced by the Polymock piece that you have chosen. Any enchantments or summons you have are removed. Your weapon and armor bonuses do not apply to Polymock skills.

When you use a white (common) Polymock piece, your maximum health is 3000 and your energy is 30. Purple (uncommon) pieces give a maximum health of 4000 and a maximum energy of 35. Gold (rare) pieces give you 5000 maximum health and 40 energy.
Skill use and effects during the match are similar to normal PvE, the only difference being conditions like Burning, Bleeding, and Disease always cause full -10 health degeneration.
Fight

When you are done reviewing your skills, you can tell Wokk to start the match. A 10-second countdown timer will begin, counting down to the start of the duel, at which point the opponent's Polymock piece turns hostile.

A round ends when one or both Polymock pieces loses all health. The loser is required to select another Polymock piece from the remaining two to start the next round. The winner retains its current level of health and energy, and all skills continue their recharge duration (i.e. the skills are not automatically recharged). Once the loser selects the next piece and starts the next round, the 10-second countdown will start again. If your opponent (i.e. the NPC) lost the previous round, the countdown timer starts almost immediately, since the winner is not prompted to start the next round.
This continues until one side's three Polymock pieces have all been defeated. Win or lose, you will be returned to the previous location.

A good opening piece when you still need to use common pieces is the Skale because it does 150 damage with its spammable attack to enemies > 50% health and has two damage skills, both of which do a great deal of damage but take time to activate and thus benefit from facing a healthy opponent.

When the opponent begins a round with a new piece, they will always start off with Polymock Glyph of Concentration, followed by either their most damaging spell or sometimes the light damage spell. Using the 2-second spell here risks taking their high damage spell without being able to get Polymock Block off in time, so using your 1-second spell then Blocking instead may be preferred. Be careful to wait at least 30 seconds for your opponent's skills to recharge before beginning with your new piece so they will have the Polymock Glyph of Concentration available, otherwise they'll start the round in an unpredictable manner.

Always watch your health and energy levels. When you're below 50% health, do not neglect the bonus damage offered by Polymock Glyph of Power. But do not activate it blindly, as the enemy will Polymock Power Drain your attempts to use the Glyph. Be aware of whether you have enough energy to pull it off, because the Glyph works very well with your spammable skill.

Do not forget to use Polymock Ether Signet the moment you reach zero energy. Trying to cast spells without energy wastes valuable time. If you or your opponent is weak, don't hesitate to waste a Polymock Power Drain or Polymock Block to use up your energy so that you can use the Ether Signet and hit them with a higher damage ability.

Try to use Polymock Power Drain and Polymock Block wisely. Try to save them for highly damaging spells and time their recharge. Polymock Glyph of Power is a good interrupt target as well. Be aware of what type of spells can be blocked and what type can be interrupted but not blocked.

Polymock Block can be used as an alternative to Polymock Glyph of Concentration if you use a 1 second spell right after it. Frequently the enemy won't react right away after having a spell blocked, giving plenty of time for your spell to complete. They will often be able to interrupt a 2 second spell after being blocked though, but if you can use the block while they're not casting then it will work for longer spells as well. If you have neither available, you can also slip a 1 second spell in right as the enemy is activating one of their spammable attacks to get it through uninterrupted.
Opponents

Yulma (1) - uses the three starter pieces - see Polymock: Defeat Yulma
Plurgg (2) - uses Fire Imp, Ice Imp, and Kappa - see Polymock: Defeat Plurgg
Blarp (3) - uses Earth Elemental, Ice Elemental, and Fire Elemental - see Polymock: Defeat Blarp
Fonk (4) - uses Kappa, Aloe, and Wind Rider - see Polymock: Defeat Fonk
Dune Teardrinker (5a) - uses Charr Shaman, Charr Flamecaller, Titan - see Polymock: Defeat Dune Teardrinker
Grulhammer Silverfist (5b) - uses Dredge, Dolyak, Dwarf - see Polymock: Defeat Grulhammer Silverfist
Necromancer Volumandus (5c) - uses Skeleton, Wraith, Dragon - see Polymock: Defeat Necromancer Volumandus
Hoff (8) - uses random pieces - see Polymock: Defeat Master Hoff

Begin the fight with your highest damage 1 second cast spell. This will hit your enemy while they are using their Polymock Glyph of Concentration. Optionally, if you cast your other high-priority spell right in the beginning, your opponent will not be able to interrupt it.
Use Polymock Block to interrupt your enemy's high powered spell.
Use Polymock Glyph of Concentration followed by your other high-priority spell.
Be ready to interrupt their 2 second cast or other high damage spell which is almost always used soon after.
Advanced starting attack chain
Use Polymock Block instantly and start casting your 2-second spell. Usually, when the enemy finishes Concentration and tries to interrupt you, the Block will still be in effect.

Use Polymock Glyph of Concentration followed by your highest damage spell.

Survivors beware that losing all three battles will on rare occasion count as a death.

Use the Earth Elemental Polymock Piece against Dolyak Rider Form
Use the Ice Elemental Polymock Piece (or Ice Imp Polymock Piece if you haven't got the Ice Elemental piece yet) against Dwarven Arcanist Form
