quests/quest:gww:68715/sections/support-.text: Before you can participate in Polymock matches, you must first obtain three starter pieces from Hoff in Rata Sum and then register them with Denn. Each registration removes the Polymock piece from your inventory and is permanently tied to your character (as opposed to your account). Do not register the piece if you plan on trading it to another character.
Rules

Once you have the three starter pieces, you can do the quest chain which starts from Polymock: Defeat Yulma. The objective of a Polymock match is to kill all three of your opponent's pieces before they kill yours.

After defeating the designated opponent (i.e. completed the quest and accepted the reward), you can return to those you have defeated and challenge them to a match under tournament rules. The one difference is that you are required to choose your Polymock pieces from all three rarities (white, purple, gold). If you did not register at least one Polymock piece for each rarity, you cannot challenge opponents using tournament rules. Winning such Polymock matches will earn you from 40 to 90 Asuran reputation points, depending on who you challenged.
Polymock takes place in several special explorable areas, depending on which region the opponent is found in:
Polymock Coliseum in the Tarnished Coast.
Polymock Glacier in the Far Shiverpeaks.
Polymock Crossing in the Charr Homelands.
Tournament Rules

After completing all polymock quests, you must play by tournament rules. The game is played with 3 pieces of different rarities polymock. To play, you must have 1 common piece, 1 uncommon piece and 1 rare piece.
You win 90 Asuran reputation points for defeating Fonk, Volumandus, Teardrinker, Silverfist or Hoff, 80 points for defeating Blarp, 60 points for Plurgg and 40 points for Yulma.
For maxing the Asuran title
1 Win 90 points. 1 match lasts 5 minutes.

It will take approximately 74 hours to reach tier 8 of the Asuran title if Asuran reputation points are gained exclusively using Polymock matches. No points are awarded past tier 8 therefore it is impossible to max the Asuran title by Polymock exclusively.
Preparation

Talk to Wokk to choose the three Polymock pieces that you want to use. After selecting your three pieces, you are then asked to select which of the three to start with. You are allowed to examine your skill bar before each round begins. Note that the platforms your piece and your opponent's piece are standing on are close to each other and that it is impossible to move out of range (although strafing to dodge projectiles is possible). Your character is replaced by the Polymock piece that you have chosen. Any enchantments or summons you have are removed. Your weapon and armor bonuses do not apply to Polymock skills.

When you use a white (common) Polymock piece, your maximum health is 3000 and your energy is 30. Purple (uncommon) pieces give a maximum health of 4000 and a maximum energy of 35. Gold (rare) pieces give you 5000 maximum health and 40 energy.
Skill use and effects during the match are similar to normal PvE, the only difference being conditions like Burning, Bleeding, and Disease always cause full -10 health degeneration.
Fight

When you are done reviewing your skills, you can tell Wokk to start the match. A 10-second countdown timer will begin, counting down to the start of the duel, at which point the opponent's Polymock piece turns hostile.

A round ends when one or both Polymock pieces loses all health. The loser is required to select another Polymock piece from the remaining two to start the next round. The winner retains its current level of health and energy, and all skills continue their recharge duration (i.e. the skills are not automatically recharged). Once the loser selects the next piece and starts the next round, the 10-second countdown will start again. If your opponent (i.e. the NPC) lost the previous round, the countdown timer starts almost immediately, since the winner is not prompted to start the next round.
This continues until one side's three Polymock pieces have all been defeated. Win or lose, you will be returned to the previous location.

A good opening piece when you still need to use common pieces is the Skale because it does 150 damage with its spammable attack to enemies > 50% health and has two damage skills, both of which do a great deal of damage but take time to activate and thus benefit from facing a healthy opponent.

When the opponent begins a round with a new piece, they will always start off with Polymock Glyph of Concentration, followed by either their most damaging spell or sometimes the light damage spell. This can be taken advantage of by using your 2-second spells right from the start. Even if your opponent attempts Polymock Power Drain after the glyph, you will almost always get your spell off. Using the 2-second spell here risks taking their high damage spell without being able to get Polymock Block off in time, so using your 1-second spell then Blocking instead may be preferred. Be careful to wait at least 30 seconds for your opponent's skills to recharge before beginning with your new piece so they will have the Polymock Glyph of Concentration available, otherwise they'll start the round in an unpredictable manner.

Always watch your health and energy levels. When you're below 50% health, do not neglect the bonus damage offered by Polymock Glyph of Power. But do not activate it blindly, as the enemy will Polymock Power Drain your attempts to use the Glyph. Be aware of whether you have enough energy to pull it off, because the Glyph works very well with your spammable skill.

Do not forget to use Polymock Ether Signet the moment you reach zero energy. Trying to cast spells without energy wastes valuable time. If you or your opponent is weak, don't hesitate to waste a Polymock Power Drain or Polymock Block to use up your energy so that you can use the Ether Signet and hit them with a higher damage ability.

Try to use Polymock Power Drain and Polymock Block wisely. Try to save them for highly damaging spells and time their recharge. Polymock Glyph of Power is a good interrupt target as well. Be aware of what type of spells can be blocked and what type can be interrupted but not blocked.

Polymock Block can be used as an alternative to Polymock Glyph of Concentration if you use a 1 second spell right after it. Frequently the enemy won't react right away after having a spell blocked, giving plenty of time for your spell to complete. They will often be able to interrupt a 2 second spell after being blocked though, but if you can use the block while they're not casting then it will work for longer spells as well. If you have neither available, you can also slip a 1 second spell in right as the enemy is activating one of their spammable attacks to get it through uninterrupted.
Opponents
The following opponents are listed in the order the quest chain introduces them:
Yulma (1) - uses the three starter pieces - see Polymock: Defeat Yulma
Plurgg (2) - uses Fire Imp, Ice Imp, and Kappa - see Polymock: Defeat Plurgg
Blarp (3) - uses Earth Elemental, Ice Elemental, and Fire Elemental - see Polymock: Defeat Blarp
Fonk (4) - uses Kappa, Aloe, and Wind Rider - see Polymock: Defeat Fonk
Dune Teardrinker (5a) - uses Charr Shaman, Charr Flamecaller, Titan - see Polymock: Defeat Dune Teardrinker
Grulhammer Silverfist (5b) - uses Dredge, Dolyak, Dwarf - see Polymock: Defeat Grulhammer Silverfist
Necromancer Volumandus (5c) - uses Skeleton, Wraith, Dragon - see Polymock: Defeat Necromancer Volumandus
Hoff (8) - uses random pieces - see Polymock: Defeat Master Hoff
General starting attack chain

Begin the fight with your highest damage 1 second cast spell. This will hit your enemy while they are using their Polymock Glyph of Concentration. Optionally, if you cast your other high-priority spell right in the beginning, your opponent will not be able to interrupt it.
Use Polymock Block to interrupt your enemy's high powered spell.
Use Polymock Glyph of Concentration followed by your other high-priority spell.
Be ready to interrupt their 2 second cast or other high damage spell which is almost always used soon after.
Advanced starting attack chain
Use Polymock Block instantly and start casting your 2-second spell. Usually, when the enemy finishes Concentration and tries to interrupt you, the Block will still be in effect.
Use Polymock Power Drain to interrupt their high-powered spell which they generally try to cast now, but whose Concentration effect was wasted on trying to interrupt you.
Use Polymock Glyph of Concentration followed by your highest damage spell.
Universal followup strategy

After opening with one of the above two starting attack chains, spam your primary low-damage spell continuously. It breaks the opponent's Block rapidly, and it delivers continual damage while you wait for skills to recycle, targets to interrupt, or while you think of tactics or are moving your mouse with the other hand. It is a very important default action requiring no thought.
While spamming and attacking with other spells, use the fast Polymock Block and Polymock Power Drain between them.

Cast Polymock Block whenever it is ready for use. Because of its fast cycle time (12s), don't delay using it, except when a high-damage spell will be ready for casting soon and Polymock Glyph of Concentration is not yet available.

Cast Polymock Power Drain tactically, don't waste it. Hover your mouse over the skill while you wait for something good to interrupt, meanwhile spamming away with your primary low-damage spell and casting Polymock Block periodically.
Always use Polymock Glyph of Concentration before casting your high-damage spell to reduce the chance of it being wasted.

When your energy is at 5 or below, focus almost exclusively on getting it to zero fast so that Polymock Ether Signet can be used. If you're down to energy 6 but your 6-energy high-damage spell is not yet available, forget it, focus on losing all your energy. Your main spam skill (cost 1e), Polymock Glyph of Power (1e) and Polymock Block (2e) are best for shedding your energy. Polymock Power Drain (3e) could be used, but it is such an important skill that it is best left for its primary role of interrupting tactically.

Throughout all of the above, always use Polymock Glyph of Power if you are under 50% health. By adding 200 damage, it makes your primary low-damage spell a real powerhouse, and should be used at every opportunity.
Using the above strategy, all the main quest opponents can be defeated very easily and almost automatically.

You can map travel out to abandon a match. This makes it faster to restart a match if it goes badly or if you've made a mistake selecting your pieces. Using /resign will let you teleport to the outpost without having to locate it on the world map.
Survivors beware that losing all three battles will on rare occasion count as a death.

When you are outside of your Polymock piece, you will be subject to all active Polymock effects. For example, if the match has ended and a projectile is already mid flight, it will still deal damage to you once it hits. Another example is an area damage over time skill such as Polymock Savannah Heat. Because of the high amounts of Polymock skill damage (most Polymock skills deal over 500 damage), you will die but you will be resurrected instantly without any animation. You might not notice your death mid-match, even if you actually defeat your opponent in the Polymock battle.
After defeating an opponent Polymock piece, there's a short time window that allows you to activate another skill with an activation time of 1 second or less, such as Polymock Glyph of Power.

To make future runs easier, avoid registering the Ice Elemental, Aloe Seed, and Mirage Iboga pieces as you get them, and just complete the quest sequence with the Earth Elemental, Fire Elemental, and Kappa. Then pass the three unregistered pieces off to new characters that need to go through, and return them after completion. Note that this will prevent you from participating in Tournament Mode until you register a Rare piece.

Be aware of whether you have enough energy to pull it off, because the Glyph works very well with your spammable skill.

Do not forget to use Polymock Ether Signet the moment you reach zero energy. Trying to cast spells without energy wastes valuable time. If you or your opponent is weak, don't hesitate to waste a Polymock Power Drain or Polymock Block to use up your energy so that you can use the Ether Signet and hit them with a higher damage ability.

Try to use Polymock Power Drain and Polymock Block wisely. Try to save them for highly damaging spells and time their recharge. Polymock Glyph of Power is a good interrupt target as well. Be aware of what type of spells can be blocked and what type can be interrupted but not blocked.

Polymock Block can be used as an alternative to Polymock Glyph of Concentration if you use a 1 second spell right after it. Frequently the enemy won't react right away after having a spell blocked, giving plenty of time for your spell to complete. They will often be able to interrupt a 2 second spell after being blocked though, but if you can use the block while they're not casting then it will work for longer spells as well. If you have neither available, you can also slip a 1 second spell in right as the enemy is activating one of their spammable attacks to get it through uninterrupted.

Grulhammer Silverfist (5b) - uses Dredge, Dolyak, Dwarf - see Polymock: Defeat Grulhammer Silverfist
Necromancer Volumandus (5c) - uses Skeleton, Wraith, Dragon - see Polymock: Defeat Necromancer Volumandus
Hoff (8) - uses random pieces - see Polymock: Defeat Master Hoff

Yulma is fairly easy to beat. You can freely use any of the pieces you have against her in any order, although leaving the Gargoyle piece for last might be a good idea as it's your most damaging piece and you can use it to regain ground if you've lost your first two pieces.

This can make her somewhat difficult to predict (and therefore interrupt/block). In general, a good offense is the best way to deal with Yulma; it is possible to simply spam your offensive skills at her until she loses.

You can map travel out to abandon a match. This makes it faster to restart a match if it goes badly or if you've made a mistake selecting your pieces. Using /resign will let you teleport to the outpost without having to locate it on the world map.
Survivors beware that losing all three battles will on rare occasion count as a death.

When you are outside of your Polymock piece, you will be subject to all active Polymock effects. For example, if the match has ended and a projectile is already mid flight, it will still deal damage to you once it hits. Another example is an area damage over time skill such as Polymock Savannah Heat. Because of the high amounts of Polymock skill damage (most Polymock skills deal over 500 damage), you will die but you will be resurrected instantly without any animation. You might not notice your death mid-match, even if you actually defeat your opponent in the Polymock battle.
After defeating an opponent Polymock piece, there's a short time window that allows you to activate another skill with an activation time of 1 second or less, such as Polymock Glyph of Power.

To make future runs easier, avoid registering the Ice Elemental, Aloe Seed, and Mirage Iboga pieces as you get them, and just complete the quest sequence with the Earth Elemental, Fire Elemental, and Kappa. Then pass the three unregistered pieces off to new characters that need to go through, and return them after completion. Note that this will prevent you from participating in Tournament Mode until you register a Rare piece.

quests/quest:gww:277150/sections/objecti.text: Clear Pongmei Valley near Kaineng City of all enemies in hard mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:277150/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 150 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:277150/sections/instruc.text: "Clear Pongmei Valley near Kaineng City of all enemies in hard mode."

quests/quest:gww:277150/sections/target-.text: The Count's Daughter quest will lead characters through here. The first time characters enter here will be from Maatu Keep or Sunjiang District.
These quests will affect the spawns in this area:
The Convocation (Both Master Togo and Headmaster Greico will travel with you, but only the former will fight, while the latter won't and will body block allies.)
The Yeti in this area charm the elder pets when you get into compass range. If you stay out of compass range and let heroes and henchmen kill the Yeti, you can tame an Elder Crane or Tiger.

As you approach Xuekao, the Deceptive, use caution to avoid getting surrounded. Groups of Am Fah and Jade Brotherhood will spawn and fight each other; you can either join the brawl or let them fight it out and dispose of what remains.
Foes that only appear in Echovald Forest (e.g. Stone Scale Kirins) or the Jade Sea (e.g. Yeti) with the exception of Pongmei Valley will drop:
Kurzick Keys or Luxon Keys in normal mode, respectively, even though only Canthan Chests spawn in this area.
Weapons that typically only drop in Echovald Forest (e.g. Amber weapons) or the Jade Sea (e.g. Jade weapons), respectively.
Complete exploration of this area contributes approximately 2.58% to the Canthan Cartographer title.

You will not gain a faction bonus for vanquishing this area. However, you can acquire blessings to gain points while killing foes from the Luxon Priest near Boreas Seabed or the Luxon/Kurzick Priest near Tanglewood Copse.
You can skip fighting Meynsang the Sadistic by avoiding his spawn point.

If you trigger the Jade Brotherhood and Am Fah groups near Xuekao, the Deceptive, but leave the area without fighting them, it can save ~14 kills. This is easiest done by flagging a hero while most of the party stays near compass range.
Some Canthan Guards will fight the enemies on the map, and get killed by them.

quests/quest:gww:14356/sections/objectiv.text: Follow the road southwest from town to Ashford. Find Miller Upton and ask him to help Namar.
Use the honeycomb to lure the three bee swarms across the bridge.
Return to Miller Upton for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:14356/sections/walkthro.text: Head down the southwest road from Ascalon City to Ashford and speak with Miller Upton. Before he can help Namar, you'll need to handle a bee problem for him. Pick up the Massive Honeycomb and approach the three bee swarms to grab their attention. Lead the swarms across the bridge until the quest updates, drop the honeycomb, and return to Upton for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:14356/sections/notes-1/.text: This quest introduces players to Bundle items.
The path you take to bring the Massive Honeycomb across the bridge affects the quest getting updated.

The bee swarms might get stuck during the quest and stop moving. The easiest way to get around this issue is to lead the bees underneath the bridge just within range of the quest marker to achieve quest completion.

quests/quest:gww:25613/sections/objectiv.text: Glean information about the harpies from Captain Jafahni.
Scavenge the wilderness for Screecher and Scratcher. Kill them to reduce harpy morale.
See Prince Ahmtur the Mighty for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25613/sections/environm.text: Captain Jafahni and the "Elder Skree" harpies in Wilderness of Bahdza (Elder Skree Griffins, Elder Skree Raiders, Elder Skree Singers, and Elder Skree Trackers) will no longer spawn after this quest is completed.

quests/quest:gww:25613/sections/walkthro.text: Start out from Dzagonur Bastion, and meet Captain Jafahni in the Wilderness of Bahdza (just to the east of the outpost). From here, follow your quest pointer deep into the wilderness to hunt down and slay the two harpy leaders: Screecher and Scratcher.

Each leader will be accompanied by 3 other skree harpies, usually Trackers and Raiders. After defeating each leader's group, a 2nd group of skree will pop up and attempt to run away, towards the portal with Resplendent Makuun (without attacking the party); chasing them down or letting them run away does not affect the quest.

Alternately, one can zone into the Wilderness of Bahdza from the Resplendent Makuun entrance. Screecher and Scratcher are both relatively near the portal, and once they have been slain, you will receive credit for completion.
Once the two skree leaders have been killed, return to Prince Ahmtur in the north-west corner of the Wilderness (or map back to Dzagonur Bastion and take a short walk into the Citadel).

quests/quest:gww:25613/sections/notes-1/.text: The additional Skree popup group at the second leader, Scratcher, sometimes gets stuck on the shrine nearby when they try to run away.
The group of Skrees near Scratcher will attack you when you begin to fight with him, but occasionally if you inflict enough damage they will run away through the portal into Resplendent Makuun.

quests/quest:gww:25424/sections/objectiv.text: See Headmaster Quin for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25424/sections/walkthro.text: Leave from Tsumei Village and head south to talk to Jaikmo, then head south again and kill the Unbound Spirit.

quests/quest:gww:215466/sections/objecti.text: Travel to Jaga Moraine and find the bottomless pit.
See Olaf Olafson for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:215466/sections/walkthr.text: Travel to the northeastern corner of Jaga Moraine to find the bottomless pit, and defeat Ssissth the Leviathan.

quests/quest:gww:215466/sections/notes-1.text: You can save time by combining this quest with A Hunter's Pride, Krak's Cavalry, and Anything You Can Do.
This quest cannot be repeated after an Extreme Makeover Credit (sex change) because the boss will not be there.

*BONUS* Kill the Priest of Menzies in Hard Mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:201359/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 30 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the *BONUS* Objective for an additional 75 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:201359/sections/walkthr.text: As per Army of Darkness walkthrough.

quests/quest:gww:201359/sections/notes-1.text: Consider completing this quest at the same time as the Dragon Lich Zaishen quest, since that quest is available from the Zaishen Bounty signpost on the eighth day after this quest (based on the Zaishen Bounty cycle) and both targets are found in the same location at the Great Battle Field.

quests/quest:gww:205973/sections/objecti.text: Kill 3 Prismatic Oozes in the Depths of Tyria. Lists the region instead of the dungeon name
*BONUS* Kill 3 Prismatic Oozes in Hard Mode.

quests/quest:gww:205973/sections/walkthr.text: As per the Watch it Jiggle quest. At least one party member must have the quest in order to get past the locked gate in the dungeon.

quests/quest:gww:9626/sections/walkthrou.text: This quest takes place entirely in Wajjun Bazaar and requires little (if any) fighting. Due to the sequence of events, it does require a significant amount of "backtracking" to complete, since Guardsman Pah is located between Paomu and Officer Chitaro, and Budo is located beyond both of them (along the path to The Marketplace). Once you have spoken to Paomu, Officer Chitaro and Guardsman Pah (in that order), you can map travel to The Marketplace to meet Budo, before returning to Paomu for the reward. If you have access to Nahpui Quarter then map traveling there after meeting Budo shortens the amount of time to complete this quest.

quests/quest:gww:14880/sections/objectiv.text: Meet Poturi on the Plains of Jarin.
Retrieve the sword from the injured Corsair.
Speak to Poturi for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:14880/sections/walkthro.text: [Incomplete source section] Exit the Sunspear Great Hall into the Plains of Jarin with Poturi and travel to where the Wounded Corsair is. There's a surprisingly large group of corsairs around him, so if you're still a low level you may wish to try pulling the groups of four, one by one. Defeat the Wounded Corsair and then interact with the Corsair Chest to receive the Notched Sword. No key is required. Speak with Poturi afterward for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:278866/sections/objecti.text: Clear Prophet's Path in the Crystal Desert of all enemies in hard mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:278866/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 250 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:278866/sections/instruc.text: "Clear Prophet's Path in the Crystal Desert of all enemies in hard mode."

quests/quest:gww:278866/sections/target-.text: These quests will affect the spawns in this area:
Complete exploration of this area contributes approximately 1.72% to the Tyrian Cartographer title.
There are lots of hidden scarabs and devourers, with several Sand Wurms and Salving Cactuses. The Salving Cactuses may burrow similar to wurms for a short time.

The area around Kepkhet Marrowfeast is likely the most difficult, as there are several Scarab Nest Builders that cannot be pulled away (but you can pull the boss). Ranged damage is best because the Scarab Nest Builders litter the area with traps. Consider clearing out the patrols around the boss before engaging. The patrols are hostile to non-scarab foes.
The foes here use conditions liberally. Condition removal skills can be brought, but since they are reapplied very quickly, it is best to bring skills to counter health degeneration.
The hydra boss (random profession) patrols a long route west of Augury Rock and might be missed.

Even if the player waits on the hydra boss route, the hydra may not approach the player on its own. Various groups of patrolling minotaurs are hostile to all foes, including other minotaurs. If you start from Augury Rock, Heroes' Audience, or Vulture Drifts and kill all the foes south of the green oasis belt, sometimes the area is considered vanquished, even if there are still foes north of the line of greenery (the area outside of the Amnoon Oasis).

quests/quest:gww:10072/sections/objectiv.text: Protect the Halcyon from Outcast raiders. You have 7..0 groups remaining.
See Captain Lexis for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:10072/sections/walkthro.text: This quest simply requires you to fight off several waves of attacking Outcasts. This is most easily accomplished with ranged attacks or spells. A warrior (or minion master) can tank the Outcasts as they head inside and move upwards to your position.
After obtaining the quest, travel to Zos Shivros Channel and head out the northern gate into the Boreas Seabed. The Halcyon is the large ship just to the north of your starting location.

The ship is hollow with several levels of walkways inside. Rion is located up the first ramp, on the tiny first level. Talking to him immediately starts the waves of attackers. Head up the ramp to the second level and attack from here. This level is within casting range of the NPCs in the area (who have Word of Healing) and attacking range of the Outcasts on the ground.

Targeting opponents requires moving along the walkways rather than moving to ground level. Be careful of this when targeting the next opponent. Whether using the keyboard or the mouse to target opponents, game mechanics will move you downward rather than along the walkway to a viable shooting location.

quests/quest:gww:10072/sections/notes-1/.text: If somebody in your group has the Quest "The Halcyon Job" active, the assault will not start and your quest log states that you have 7 groups remaining.

quests/quest:gww:21972/sections/objectiv.text: Alert the scholars about the assault on the Halls of Chokhin. You have spoken to 0...8 of 8 scholars.
Protect the scholars from the advancing Margonite forces. At least 4 scholars must survive. 8...0 of 8 scholars are still alive.
Eliminate the groups of Margonites attacking Chokhin. 12...0 of 12 groups remain.
See Library Envoy Chukeht for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:21972/sections/walkthro.text: When this quest is active, there appear to be "hidden" triggers in the Halls of Chokhin which set off each wave of Margonite groups, however, these triggers only become active after the party has spoken to all 8 scholars. When the scholars are spoken to, they will run to the shrine of Lyssa at the north-west side of the halls. For this reason, it is best to start talking to the scholars furthest from the shrine, then work your way in to speak to the closest scholars last.

Once all the scholars have been spoken to and have congregated at the shrine, the party can start to trigger the Margonite groups. This is best done by carefully moving forward on one side while holding the Show Targets key (Left Ctrl by default) until you can see a Margonite group, and then moving enough to trigger make them head towards the scholars. At this point, hold your position to head them off, or retreat to a suitable ambush/blocking point.

Even with this careful approach, you will likely find that the Margonites attack in waves of 3 groups (so 2 waves on each of the north and south sides to make the total 12 groups). Do note that there are 4 different kinds of groups. The first group at the east are mostly rangers. The 2nd at the east side are melee. The 2 groups on the west side are both casters and melee.
When you have cleared the 6 groups on one side in this fashion, switch to the other and repeat.

The terrain here benefits a smart party: make use of height advantage by standing at the top of stairs and use ranged attacks to increase damage; use body blocking at corners to hold groups and nuke them together; wells and wards can help the party or hinder foes (minion masters or other corpse users will have plenty of material); since the Margonites will have to cross bridges or climb narrow stairways, placing traps in their path before you trigger each wave can be of great help too. Casting Death Nova on minions to spread poison is also useful.
For more tips and tactics for this mission, see this article's Talk page

quests/quest:gww:25278/sections/objectiv.text: Find Paulus the Monk in Regent Valley
Search Paulus's body for any personal effects.
Return the holy symbol to Grazden the Protector.

quests/quest:gww:25278/sections/walkthro.text: Go into Regent Valley to look for Paulus. If you're having trouble finding the path to the portal, follow the creek bed in the direction of Ascalon City a short distance until you can climb a hill on your right. Once through the portal it's a fairly straight path; just follow the quest arrow. Alternatively start from Fort Ranik and walk alongside the aqueduct. This not only is extremely easy to find but also much shorter.

You'll find that you are too late to save him. You'll need to click on his body to obtain his holy symbol to take back to Grazden. Beware, though. Party members will become poisoned by the spot. Return the symbol to Grazden.

quests/quest:gww:25278/sections/notes-1/.text: The poison inflicted by interacting with Paulus's body suggests that he fell to a similar environment effect to the one monk players had to protect him from in pre-Searing.

quests/quest:gww:25504/sections/objectiv.text: Meet Farrah Cappo in Lakeside County.
Keep Farrah alive while she hunts down the infamous Alain.
Return to Grazden the Protector for your reward.
Grazden will give you the following skills upon taking the quest:

quests/quest:gww:25504/sections/walkthro.text: After accepting the quest from Grazden the Protector, leave Green Hills County to Lakeside County. There you will find Farrah Cappo waiting for you. She will start running to fight the groups of bandits. Follow her and make sure she doesn't die. You can help her fight if you want but the main objective of the quest is to keep her alive. Once she fights off four groups she will run into Alain. Keep Farrah alive at all costs. Once he is dead run back to Green Hills County to talk to Grazden the Protector for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25504/sections/notes-1/.text: If Alain kills you but Farrah still manages to kill him, you will get credit for completing the quest

Alternatively, if you kill Alain before the escort (which only starts when you approach Farrah at the Green Hills County zone portal), the quest will be marked complete once Farrah reaches Alain's location safely.

quests/quest:gww:63346/sections/objectiv.text: Speak to Kilroy to start your brawling training.
Defeat the Norn brawlers using your new skills.
See Kilroy Stonekin for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:63346/sections/walkthro.text: Accepting Kilroy's quest offer will not place the Brass Knuckles in your inventory yet, but you will have it once you enter the arena and will need to equip it in your weapon slot. Your skills will be replaced with the Brawling build. The Norn Brawlers will become hostile in order. First, two single brawlers will face you, then a pair and finally the last three. Your health is partially refilled any time you defeat a brawler, and the next set does not turn hostile until you have defeated all the previous group.

Although the pair and trio of Norn Brawlers move to the center of the arena as if they were a group, they actually are not together as a team and using a longbow/flatbow or slowly moving towards them from the side can help you pull just one at a time.

quests/quest:gww:14893/sections/objectiv.text: Seek the meaning of the ancient parchment.

quests/quest:gww:14893/sections/walkthro.text: Map travel to Tihark Orchard, then head out into the western Forum Highlands, and speak to Seborhin Protector Zuor to gain entrance to the Garden of Seborhin. Once in the garden, make your way to Hedge Wizard Mabai located in the middle area of the east side. Speak to Mabai and show him the ancient parchment to complete the quest.
You can only complete this quest if you have completed the Nightfall campaign, or if you have Tahlkora in your party (before the garden becomes Nightfallen).

quests/quest:gww:14893/sections/notes-1/.text: The garden is not always accessible. See Garden of Seborhin for details.

quests/quest:gww:204218/sections/objecti.text: Kill Pywatt the Swift in Alcazia Tangle.
*BONUS* Kill Pywatt the Swift in Hard Mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:204218/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 20 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the *BONUS* Objective for an additional 50 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:204218/sections/walkthr.text: The simplest way to reach Pywatt is to leave from Rata Sum via Magus Stones. Use the southeast portal to travel to Alcazia Tangle; Pywatt is just south of the portal in Alcazia Tangle.

quests/quest:gww:204218/sections/notes-1.text: Goes well with the quest Turning the Page.

quests/quest:gww:18809/sections/objectiv.text: Deliver the custom sword to Castellan Puuba at the Sunspear Great Hall.
Meet up with Castellan Puuba on the Plains of Jarin.
Fight beside Castellan Puuba as he tries out his new, customized sword. You have slain x of 10 creatures.

quests/quest:gww:18809/sections/walkthro.text: If you don't have the Sunspear Great Hall on your map yet you can combine this quest with Armored Transport, which will take you there. If you haven't entered the Sunpspear Great Hall after that quest you have to go there now and enter the outpost. Once in the Sunspear Great Hall, find Castellan Puuba (you can use the "Alt" key to find NPCs inside a town/outpost). When you talk to him he will ask you to go outside into Plains of Jarin to test his new blade.

Enter the area and after taking the Insect Hunt Bounty at the resurrection shrine, approach Castellan Puuba. He will now be added to your party as a ally. Straight ahead from the entrance there is a colony of Stalking Nephila. Lead the Castellan there and he will start to attack them; and, as a good ally, he will even change his target to whatever target you are attacking. After slaying the required 10 creatures, the Castellan will thank you for your help and you can return to Kamadan to collect your reward.

quests/quest:gww:18809/sections/notes-1/.text: Puuba doesn't personally have to slay a beast to make it count.
Combines well with Armored Transport, Proof of Courage, and Map-Travel Inventor.
The word Castellan is a Title, not part of the NPC's Name.
Unlike most other quests when you give an item to an NPC, there doesn't appear to be a text notification that Puuba takes his sword.

quests/quest:gww:203752/sections/objecti.text: Kill Quansong Spiritspeak in Tahnnakai Temple.
*BONUS* Kill Quansong Spiritspeak in Hard Mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:203752/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 20 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the *BONUS* Objective for an additional 50 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:203752/sections/walkthr.text: Head north through the Tahnnakai Temple explorable area from Zin Ku Corridor. Be prepared for area of effect fire damage from the Temple Guardians around him. If you follow the path in the the map posted on the right, you will only encounter Temple Guardians on your way to Quansong Spiritspeak.
You will not encounter any physical attackers, so skills that block, cause misses, or inflict the blind condition are less effective here; however, Temple Guardians have Stun on Critical Hit.
Quansong Spiritspeak and Temple Guardians are not fleshy creatures, so skills that exploit corpses and inflict bleeding, disease, or poison are ineffective against them.

You will only encounter spellcaster mobs, so consider bringing anti-caster skills and/or various Ranger nature rituals that can benefit your party but cannot benefit the Temple Guardians (such as Favorable Winds, Infuriating Heat, and Winnowing).

Temple Guardians have less armor rating against cold damage, so consider bringing Winter or skills that deal cold damage. Consider bringing Water Magic hex spells that snare and deal cold damage (i.e. Deep Freeze, Ice Spikes, Mind Freeze, and Shard Storm), which will slow their movement speed and can help in preventing them from reaching your midline/backline and dealing point blank area of effect damage from Temple Guardians' Double Dragon and Quansong Spiritspeak's Ancestors' Rage.
Temple Guardians have less armor rating against blunt damage, so consider using a weapon that deals blunt damage.

quests/quest:gww:25673/sections/objectiv.text: Speak to Miner Tonabanza at the Cliffs of Dohjok and tell him you will stand guard while he continues mining.
Protect the miner if he gets attacked.
See Quarrymaster Bohanna for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25673/sections/walkthro.text: Speak with Miner Tonabanza to start him walking towards the cliff wall. When he starts to work, a group of three mandragors will spawn near him. Kill the mandragors and keep them off the miner. Once the mandragors are dead, talk to the Tonabanza again and then return to Quarrymaster Bohanna for the reward.

quests/quest:gww:25674/sections/objectiv.text: Meet the Sunspear squad at the Cliffs of Dohjok
Kill all the mandragor in the quarry
See Quarrymaster Bohanna for your reward

quests/quest:gww:25674/sections/walkthro.text: After talking to Quarrymaster Bohanna, exit the outpost onto the Cliffs of Dohjok. Talk to Captain Vahndah to have the Sunspear squad follow you to the quarry. At its west end, you will find a group of stoneflesh, slitherers, and imp mandragor guarding the Queen. After killing all of them, return to the Quarrymaster for your reward.

As an alternative (if you've already been there), Map travel to Blacktide Den. This will give you a shorter route with fewer monsters, and a party of 8, at the cost of not gaining the level 10 allies from outside Champion's Dawn.

quests/quest:gww:25674/sections/notes-1/.text: Can be used for farming Sunspear Promotion Points in Cliffs of Dohjok.

quests/quest:gww:25447/sections/objectiv.text: Assault the Crimson Skull Guild Hall and defeat Captain Quimang. Find reinforcements along the way
See The Emperor's Blade for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25447/sections/walkthro.text: You have to find recruits who are guards and go to Captain Quimang. The guards are necessary as Quimang has a lot of Crimson Skull protecting him in all directions.

Best if using Henchmen to start in Ran Musu Gardens, that way your henchmen will be level 10 where as starting in Tsumei Village your Henchmen will be level 6. Start in Ran Musu Gardens, go down through Kinya Province to Panjiang Peninsula to keep henchmen at level 10. Kill Tahkayun Tsi to give your party a morale boost, as he is right outside of the exit from Ran Musu Gardens. Head down towards Port Kaimu where Captain Quimang is, killing the groups on both sides of where the Captain is, but staying away from contact with him. Then head to the farming village (Kaitan Village) just outside Tsumei Village starting from as far south as you can go working north and you'll end up with 9 level 10 guards to help you with the final group and Captain Quimang.

quests/quest:gww:25447/sections/notes-1/.text: If one of the partymembers has the quest Togo's Ultimatum, you cannot do this quest as Captain Quimang will not be hostile.
There are groups of Crimson Skull all over the area. The best way to collect the help described above is to take on and kill these groups.

The gathered reinforcements will be useless if playing a ranged character. This is is because their aggro range is quite short and being under attack (or attacking) will not cause them to engage the enemy.

quests/quest:gww:8054/sections/objective.text: Speak to the first Sunspear Recruit.
Speak to the second Sunspear Recruit.
Speak to the third Sunspear Recruit.
See First Spear Jahdugar for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:8054/sections/walkthrou.text: Speak to the three Sunspear Recruits and return to First Spear Jahdugar for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:8054/sections/notes-1/b.text: This is marked as a Primary Quest but is not required to proceed.

quests/quest:gww:295339/sections/objecti.text: Speak with Guardsman Qao Lin when you are ready for combat.
Position the Imperial Guards in defensive positions. There is only a short time before they reach the gates!
Do not allow the gangs to breach the gate to the palace.
Defeat Reisen the Phoenix and Apep, Unending Night
See Guardsman Qao Lin for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:295339/sections/shared-.text: You can talk to the guards to have them follow you. Talk to them again to have them wait at a suitable position.

Soon, the Main Gate will be broken. Defeat all incoming attackers. After a while, the Dock Gate is breached as well. With attackers from both sides, you can either split your forces or take a stand near the Palace Gate. If you stay at the gate, let all the guards follow you, this keeps them from going too far away from your position to defend the main Gate.
Note that all three gates cannot be healed or otherwise repaired. Be sure to intercept your foes early. (e.g. you could use the central courtyard and pull from both sides)
If your party wipes, you will be resurrected at the Palace Gate. Dead Canthan Guards will self-resurrect between waves.
When Reisen the Phoenix arrives, it is recommended to target him first since he has very high damage.
Make the guards follow you at the start, and stay by the main gate.
Bring Pain Inverter and target elementalists and bosses with it.
Bring area of effect (AoE) skills. The staircases can serve as choke points.

Flag heroes quickly out of Chaos Storm or Churning Earth when enemies cast it; otherwise, sit back and enjoy the show while the guards serve as a never-ending meat shield for your party and your AoE skills wreak havoc on the incoming mobs.
A Soul Twisting (Shelter and Union) hero is recommended for defense.
Because there will be many foes and allies, considering bringing a minion master (or even two) and Ebon Battle Standard of Honor, respectively.
Sometimes the incoming waves of enemies will not spawn. Instead, only a few waves will spawn in the Main Gate, and no other enemies will spawn afterwards.

Then, drop as many IFTs as you can along the paths. Spread out any heroes and pop any defensive spirits they might have available before the Tengu arrive. During the battle, you can keep grabbing explosives and tossing them at the balled-up foes.

quests/quest:gww:25628/sections/objectiv.text: Escort Hareh to the ancient graveyard in the Sulfurous Wastes.
Visit gravesites and help Hareh summon the undead. You have visited 0 of 5 gravesites.
Protect Hareh while he performs the ritual to raise the undead.
See Infantryman Hareh for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25628/sections/walkthro.text: Follow the quest marker to come to a spot with five gravesites located near each other. Infantryman Hareh will follow you (he is undead, so don't worry about him not being inside a Junundu). The quest marker will point you successively to all five of the gravesites. At each gravesite, Infantryman Hareh will use the skill Rise From Your Grave! to animate two level 18 Undead Soldiers (they look like Flesh Golems). You do not need to click on the gravesites. Just get Hareh to follow you close enough to trigger his use of that skill.

After Hareh animates each pair of his minions (unlike normal minions, these will not have inherent health degeneration), a group of about 6 Margonites will attack your position. Being inside Junundu will make the fight easy, but note this will prevent you from using healing skills on Infantryman Hareh, so consider having a monk outside of the wurm if you have trouble keeping him alive. Don't worry about the Undead Soldiers dying. Once Hareh has activated his skill for the fifth time, the quest is considered complete and you can claim the quest from him before the fifth group of Margonites arrives.

quests/quest:gww:199793/sections/objecti.text: *BONUS* Complete the mission in under 20 minutes (26 minutes in Hard Mode).
*BONUS* Complete the mission in Hard Mode.

quests/quest:gww:277355/sections/instruc.text: "Clear Raisu Palace in Kaineng City of all enemies in hard mode."

quests/quest:gww:277355/sections/target-.text: This explorable area can only be entered from the Imperial Sanctum outpost, and is therefore only accessible after completion of the Raisu Palace mission.

There are globes of light scattered throughout the area. Those near a boss will spawn Shiro'ken if you approach too closely when fighting. To avoid this, pull the boss away from the globe. (The Ranger Boss does not have a globe in its vicinity.)
The progress bar in the vanquish counter drastically overestimates progress, as most foes in the instance are not included in the total count until they enter compass range.
The portal near the Imperial Sanctum outpost can be used, even though the gate sometimes appears to be closed.

quests/quest:gww:216404/sections/objecti.text: Kill Rand Stormweaver and accompanying foes in Slavers' Exile.
*BONUS* Kill Rand Stormweaver and accompanying foes in Hard Mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:216404/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 40 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the *BONUS* Objective for an additional 100 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:216404/sections/walkthr.text: As per Justiciar Thommis' level. Both Rand Stormweaver and the small group directly around him must be killed.

quests/quest:gww:25416/sections/objectiv.text: Complete the Advanced Defense Techniques course.
See Headmaster Greico for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25416/sections/walkthro.text: This quest requires the completion of four sub-quests given also by Instructor Ng. The order of completion is entirely optional.

quests/quest:gww:17644/sections/objectiv.text: Take Rastin's request to Artisan Daved in Old Ascalon.
Deliver the Scribe's supplies to Witness Rastin in Old Ascalon.

quests/quest:gww:17644/sections/walkthro.text: Head south from Witness Rastin along the main road. You'll encounter some Gargoyles, a Hulking Stone Elemental or two, some Devourers, and a couple Grawl. After you crest the top of the hill, turn southwest and speak with Artisan Daved to get the necessary items. Head back to Rastin and give him the supplies to get your reward.

quests/quest:gww:17644/sections/notes-1/.text: This quest can be completed in conjunction with Gargoyle Trouble and Counting the Fallen, as they take place in roughly the same area.
You may have to speak with Artisan Daved twice. If you speak with him and the green arrow over his head is still present, speak with him again to get the supplies.

quests/quest:gww:63909/sections/notes-1/.text: If you do not have the required quest, the closed door by the Inscribed Stone will not let you leave the first room.
Completion of this dungeon will fill in page #8 of the Master Dungeon Guide storybook.
Be careful of the ice traps.
East from the Dungeon Key, a lone Ancient Vaettir roams at the end of the corridor. When approached, it will "push" three ice boulders that roll down and kill any creature in their path.
Allies such as minions and Dwarven Heroes will attempt to attack these boulders and may die as a result.
The Vaettir may also die to these boulders.
Light the braziers near the north bridge to lower the bridges.
To get the dungeon key to drop, you must kill the Reaper of Destruction and the group of hidden destroyers at the Reaper's initial location.
Near the portal to Level 3, the Chromatic Drakes and the Destroyers will fight against each other.
There is an area beyond the traps that is not shown on the map. There is nothing of value.

There appears to be an unreachable area beyond the south west corner of level 2 which does not appear on the minimap, within which a Whirling Wisp may occasionally be seen. The final Destroyers may be friendly, making the dungeon impossible to complete.

quests/quest:gww:63909/sections/shared-q.text: Captain Sargen's unit is located within Level 3 of the Raven's Point dungeon.

There are many places throughout the levels where there are flame braziers, which must be lit to open the doors. One is always lit. A chest will spawn after defeating an Ancient Vaettir, and spawns a torch that you can light the other braziers with. Keep in mind that any torch can be used and thus carrying just one torch through the level is sufficient.

In the first level, you need to defeat the Reaper of Destruction, which is a dervish boss, and several Destroyers that will spawn around it to get the dungeon key. You must kill all the Destroyers (including the ones that have not spawned behind the boss yet, if the boss is lured) for the dungeon key to drop. You also can summon a Dwarven Ghost if you have Light of Deldrimor close to where you pick up the area map. There are two hidden treasures in the exit area with the drakes.

At the second level, the dungeon key is located in the western portion. When you pick up the key, several Destroyers will spawn between your party and the dungeon gate. There is a potentially frustrating section on this level that requires you to light a torch, run past a gauntlet of ice-jet traps, and then light another pair of braziers (in order to make a bridge appear). It is possible to do this without a speed boost skill, but it is advised to bring one. With or without, you may have to try this several times before you succeed. This can be accomplished simply by running between the ice wall and the ice-jet traps (behind them). There is enough space to run behind them when they are on and down the middle of the chamber when they turn off.

The third level is very short. You will notice a group of Dwarves, and they will be attacked by several waves of Destroyers coming from all sides. Survive the waves, and the end boss, the Plague of Destruction will show up at the end of it. Kill it to clear the dungeon, and pick up your reward from the Destroyer Chest. Note that surviving the waves of Destroyers is generally harder than defeating the Plague of Destruction.
A speed boost can make it easier to run torches (especially on level 2), but you can manage without one.
You generally can drop the Unlit Torches after opening a passageway as there are several chests containing new unlit torches that you can find along the way.
Once you kill the Reaper of Destruction on level 2, your route to the exit will fill with spawns of destroyers.
If you are having trouble, you can run away from the destroyers and wait for nearby ice traps or remaining foes to weaken the groups enough for you to finish off the rest.
Destroyers are resistant to fire damage and immune to Burning. Several foes here (Elementals and Nightmares) are not fleshy.
If you save the northeastern group of Dwarves then they will patrol towards Captain Sargen's unit - potentially helping your group engage with the Destroyers.
The quest log could update itself as "Completed" after killing the waves of Destroyers but not the Plague of Destruction.

quests/quest:gww:10147/sections/objectiv.text: Find Junior Minister Jejiang. Convince him to call off the destruction of "The Roost."
Collect 2 platinum to bribe Junior Minister Jejiang.
See Quill Songfeather for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:10147/sections/walkthro.text: The quest itself is straight forward, simply travel between the quest giver and the Minister, and then back.

quests/quest:gww:10147/sections/notes-1/.text: You can complete the quest without spending any money: with at least 2 platinum in your inventory, speak to Junior Minister Jejiang and follow the dialogue until the "Accept" and "Decline" options appear. Drop all your money and Accept the reward. (Remember to pick up your cash before zoning out.)

quests/quest:gww:25676/sections/objectiv.text: Find Rojis on Issnur Isles and convince him to rejoin the Sunspears.
Find the nest of mandragor destroying Rojis' field and eliminate them.
Tell Rojis the Mandragor are dead.
See Castellan Puuba for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25676/sections/walkthro.text: Enter Issnur Isles from Kodlonu Hamlet and follow the quest marker to find Rojis. He will ask you to kill five level 11 Mandragors located to the south-west of Rojis' position, in the midst of several groups of skale. When you have killed all five mandragors, speak to Rojis again, and then return to Castellan Puuba.

quests/quest:gww:25676/sections/notes-1/.text: Rojis will appear outside Kamadan with the group of Sunspears during the quest War Preparations (Recruit Training) even if this quest is not completed.

Completing this quest requires completing the first step in Isle of the Dead; curiously, however, Rojis is part of the Sunspear squad met during that quest in Cliffs of Dohjok, despite being recruited back into the Sunspears in this quest.

quests/quest:gww:21966/sections/objectiv.text: Meet Lieutenant Murunda and her soldiers in the Mirror of Lyss.
Kill the demons infesting the Sebelkeh Basilica. 7...0 of 7 groups remain.
See Lieutenant Murunda for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:21966/sections/walkthro.text: Start from Dzagonur Bastion, and meet Lieutenant Murunda just outside in the Mirror of Lyss. After speaking to Murunda, a Vabbi Guard Captain and 4 Vabbi Guards will join your party as allies.

From here, it's a simple search and destroy type quest, as you follow the quest pointer to each group of Margonites and defeat them. Be aware that the usual spawns for The Mirror of Lyss will also be present along the way.

quests/quest:gww:21966/sections/notes-1/.text: If the Margonite groups are killed out of order, the Vabbi Guard's dialogue appear in a different order as well. Each quote is tied to a specific group.

The Guards will follow you until the quest is finished, which makes Vanquishing this area much easier. While the quest does add the Margonite groups, it also removes most of the Kournan spawns, for only a small overall increase in foes to be vanquished.

quests/quest:gww:25292/sections/requirem.text: The Great Northern Wall mission completed

quests/quest:gww:25292/sections/objectiv.text: Go from town to Old Ascalon and find the Army Recruits.
Lead all three recruits west along the wall to the far gate and present them to Gate Guard Hollis.
Speak to Gate Guard Hollis for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25292/sections/walkthro.text: Start from Ascalon City. Outside you will meet three Army Recruits, who will follow you automatically. The recruits tend to lag behind the party, and all three must survive to complete the quest, so take care while escorting them. Head to the entrance to The Breach, where Gate Guard Hollis stands, but do not go through. The quest will be updated when the three recruits have arrived.

quests/quest:gww:25292/sections/notes-1/.text: The recruits will stop moving during combat and do not fight back if attacked.

quests/quest:gww:25428/sections/objectiv.text: Speak to Guardsman Pah about filling out the ministry's scrollwork.

quests/quest:gww:25428/sections/walkthro.text: This quest is quite easy, all it requires is for you to retrace your path taken in the previous quest back to Guardsman Pah.
Alternatively, map travel to Nahpui Quarter and return into Wajjun Bazaar to Guardsman Pah.

quests/quest:gww:25428/sections/notes-1/.text: This quest appears to be mutually exclusive with the Imperial Assistance quest.

quests/quest:gww:295210/sections/objecti.text: Talk to Yayoi of the Orders.
Talk to Chow Zhong the Inferno.
Talk to Gao Han of the Rings.
Talk to Disciple of Shadow Feung Zhu.
Talk to Min the Dragon's Claw.
Defeat the Ministry of Purity forces.
See Lei Jeng for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:295210/sections/environ.text: While this quest is active, the Shiro'ken bosses in Sunjiang District do not spawn.

quests/quest:gww:295210/sections/walkthr.text: Start from Zin Ku Corridor and head out a short distance to meet up with Zenmai, who is having a conversation with Daisuke Crimson Edge. The Ministry of Purity will approach soon; kill them and Zenmai will join as an ally.

Your task now is to lead Zenmai to find her friends in the Am Fah. Keep an eye on her as she has a tendency to get stuck on chests and be left behind. The Ministry of Purity are hostile to Am Fah groups, so try to take advantage of this. The mobs are spaced out enough that you mostly do not need to worry about over-aggro.

Refer to the map for the shortest path to reach all of Zenmai's friends. She must get within range before the quest update will trigger. Each of her friends will turn hostile at end of a dialogue. Four of them, when defeated, will turn into allies. Of particular note is Chow Zhong the Inferno - spread out your group before his dialogue ends because he uses PBAoE skills.
After Chow Zhong, you will run into two groups of Ministry, led by the ranger and assassin bosses.

At the last point on the map, where Min the Dragon's Claw is located, the dialogue will trigger the spawning of two large groups of Ministry, led by the remaining two bosses. Right before they turn hostile, friendly Am Fah will show up. You can either let the Am Fah weaken the Ministry for you first, or just join in the fray. Once all hostiles are dead, the quest is complete.

quests/quest:gww:295210/sections/notes-1.text: For players without Guild Wars Nightfall, the Sunspear that Zenmai mentions in her opening dialogue refers to a prominent NPC in the Nightfall campaign.

If any of the Am Fah allies recruited in this quest die in combat, their "death" will count as a morale boost, and you will be able to capture their skills. They will still self-resurrect after a period of time.

quests/quest:gww:295212/sections/objecti.text: Talk to Yayoi of the Orders.
Talk to Chow Zhong the Inferno.
Talk to Gao Han of the Rings.
Talk to Disciple of Shadow Feung Zhu.
Talk to Min the Dragon's Claw.
Defeat the Ministry of Purity forces.
See Lei Jeng for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:295212/sections/walkthr.text: As per the normal mode version, refer to the map for the locations of the quest NPCs. Take note that their locations are different compared to normal mode.

Another difference is that as Zenmai approaches each quest NPC, the moment the dialog triggers, a group of Am Fah will spawn near the boss. They turn hostile the moment the boss turns hostile. Consider placing spirits and flagging heroes apart before letting Zenmai trigger the dialogue.

The ambush at the end of the quest, although in a different location, is the same. It is best to quickly move away from the Min's location, where the Ministry will converge. Let Daisuke's Am Fah take the brunt of the attack before joining in.

quests/quest:gww:295212/sections/notes-1.text: The locations of the quest NPCs are different compared to the normal mode version.
The first time each boss ally dies, the party gains a morale boost.
Including enemies defeated during the quest, there are 223-227 enemies to vanquish in this area while the quest is active.

quests/quest:gww:279270/sections/objecti.text: Clear Reed Bog in the Maguuma Jungle of all enemies in hard mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:279270/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 50 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:279270/sections/instruc.text: "Clear Reed Bog in the Maguuma Jungle of all enemies in hard mode."

quests/quest:gww:279270/sections/target-.text: Start from Ventari's Refuge and travel south through Ettin's Back. The secondary quest Dropping Eaves given outside Ventari's Refuge will lead here.
Complete exploration of this area contributes approximately 0.6% to the Tyrian Cartographer title.
Minion masters should be aware that the Moss Scarabs will steal minions using Verata's Gaze.
Most foes in the area are hidden.
The northern path has many hidden Moss Scarabs.
The southern path has many hidden Maguuma Spiders and Life Pods.
With great patience, it is possible to bring a party of 8 from the Temple of the Ages.

quests/quest:gww:33702/sections/objectiv.text: Defeat Primeval King Jahnus and his royal guards.
Find Myrish, the leader of the slave spirits, and tell him of King Jahnus' demise.

quests/quest:gww:33702/sections/walkthro.text: Right after taking the quest, King Jahnus and his guards will turn hostile. You just need to kill the king to get the first objective. It's a relatively easy fight.

quests/quest:gww:33702/sections/notes-1/.text: Both this quest and its sister quest, Destroy the Ungrateful Slaves, give the same rewards.
Immediately after accepting this quest, the king and his guards will become hostile.

quests/quest:gww:25430/sections/objectiv.text: Bring the Chalice of Corruption to the Imperial Agent Hanjo.

quests/quest:gww:25430/sections/walkthro.text: Just speak with Imperial Agent Hanjo in Kaineng Center.

quests/quest:gww:25430/sections/notes-1/.text: Accepting this quest will turn all the surrounding Am Fah hostile.
When the Am Fah become hostile, you can just map travel to Kaineng Center to see Imperial Agent Hanjo for your reward.
Once this quest is completed, your character can no longer complete the Drink from the Chalice of Corruption quest.
Upon turning hostile, many of the Am Fah, especially the Marksmen will fall victim to the numerous traps they set while friendly.

quests/quest:gww:279573/sections/objecti.text: Clear the Regent Valley in Ascalon of all enemies in hard mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:279573/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 50 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:279573/sections/instruc.text: "Clear the Regent Valley in Ascalon of all enemies in hard mode."

quests/quest:gww:279573/sections/target-.text: There are many secondary quests that will lead to this area. It lies to the southeast of Old Ascalon and leads to Fort Ranik in its northeastern corner.
If entering from Fort Ranik, a small group of soldiers can be seen engaging either the renegades or a group of Charr.
You can obtain a Moa Egg (required to hatch a Black Moa Chick) in the southeastern section, near a large number of Moas.
Complete exploration of this area contributes approximately 1.6% to the Tyrian Cartographer title.
Vanquishing: 129–178 foes. There are many hidden Devourers in this area.
The Renegade Elementalists have Mind Burn in hard mode, a powerful area of effect spell.
The fog in the northwest corner of the map does not uncover for an unknown reason, so it will not look like it is explored on the map; exploring this part will still add to your Cartographer title.
At the exit to Pockmark Flats the shrine on the other side looks destroyed with both arches incomplete but when changing the area the shrine is complete and working.

quests/quest:gww:10457/sections/requirem.text: The Great Northern Wall mission completed

quests/quest:gww:10457/sections/objectiv.text: See Lord Darrin for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:10457/sections/walkthro.text: After obtaining the quest from Sergeant Brannen just outside Fort Ranik, head to King's Watch in Regent Valley. A group of four Charr will be waiting at the marked location, but they do not need to be killed. The quest will update upon reaching the quest marker, and you can map travel back to Fort Ranik for the reward.

quests/quest:gww:10457/sections/notes-1/.text: This quest combines well with Cities of Ascalon and The Red-Cloaked Deserter as all three require traveling to King's Watch.

quests/quest:gww:16562/sections/objectiv.text: Start from Lost Soul [Challenge Mission Starter] located in Remains of Sahlahja.
Evade angry ghosts and cleanse the tombs by killing the insects that have infested the area.
Evade the ghosts of the primeval kings.
Kill greater infestations to earn points and gain the temporary ability to harm ghosts.
Destroy lost souls to free their spirits and earn points.
Earn 15 points to unlock access to each section of the tombs.

quests/quest:gww:16562/sections/rewards-.text: Scoring in this mission rewards experience and gold base on the formulas below. Values are rounded down. An additional bonus is given for achieving daily best, monthly best, or quarterly best.

For every Maddened Spirit that you kill, you have a chance of acquiring an Ancient Armor Remnant (each of these allows you to upgrade the visual appearance of hero armor; you can add statues of heroes with upgraded armor to the Hall of Monuments).

quests/quest:gww:16562/sections/walkthro.text: During the mission, you will suffer from Corrupted Lands, which causes a constant Health degeneration of 1 pip. This can be hard to mitigate because your ability to heal is limited by spending most of the mission riding a Junundu. There are 5 different areas in this challenge. You start out in the center and have 4 locked doors to the other areas at the beginning. For every 15 points you earn you unlock a new section. You earn points by defeating various enemies during the mission

The Maddened Spirits deal 700 damage and are invincible unless you are enchanted with Spirit Form, which lasts for a short period after killing a Greater Infestation while within a Junundu. You get the most points for defeating Lost Souls, which spawn at random locations on the map.

The Paragon skill, "Can't Touch This!", will protect you from the Maddened Spirit's Maddened Strike (but you can only kill a Maddened Spirit while inside a wurm — and you can enter a wurm while being attacked by Maddened Spirit, unlike with any other creature).

The best method to get Armor Remnants is to camp near a Greater Infestation and keep it near death as you kill Infestations. Keep an eye on your radar and watch for a moving red dot, then as the Maddened Spirit gets near you kill the Greater Infestation. You should then be able to kill the spirit and move on to camp the next Greater Infestation.

The best method for gaining points is seeking and killing Lost Souls. Kill the first few Maddened Spirits until you have unlocked two areas. Then, start running in your wurm through the areas. There are three spawn points in the northwestern corner (one on rocky ground), three in the northeastern corner, one in the southeastern corner (on rocky ground) and two in the southwestern corner. When you start running, go through each area methodically, scanning for lost souls. Do not fight the Spirits. Let them chase you and use your tunnel skill to keep ahead of them. When you find a lost soul, make sure you have some space between you and the spirits before you kill it. Then, tunnel quickly away. This will take a while, but done effectively you can rack up many points.

For souls on rocky ground, have at least 2 aggro circles' distance between you and the spirits before having the wurm spit you out. You will need a running skill (perhaps two) and enough damage to kill the soul quickly.

To heal you can either build up your adrenaline and use Junundu Smash to KD a mob then use Junundu Bite (given that the first attack doesn't kill your target) to heal for 500 hp. You can also use Junundu Tunnel then use Junundu Bite to knock down and heal for 500 hp. You can also use Junundu Wail to heal for 500 hp if there are no enemies near you. The best way to heal is to exit your wurm and get a new wurm, but you are very vulnerable while doing this so make sure you have at least two aggro circles' distance between you and the spirits before you try this.

To offset the effects of health degeneration you can use Bowl of Skalefin Soup or War Supplies, which will cancel the effects of the health degeneration and allow the Junundu's natural regeneration to take over.

You may want to equip a few speed stances, because Lost Souls may spawn on rocky terrain where your wurm cannot go to. In these cases you'll have to build sufficient distance between you and the Maddened Spirits to get out your wurm without being caught. Once you are out of the wurm use your speed boosts to stay ahead of the Spirits and run to the nearest wurm spoor after killing the Lost Soul.

quests/quest:gww:16562/sections/notes-1/.text: During this mission you will be under the effects of Corrupted Lands.
As with most other challenge missions, foes do not drop loot.

The section at the start contributes about 0.5%.
After unlocking a single gate, you can uncover just under 0.4% more.
You can indefinitely avoid the maddened spirits (while still killing infestations) by using a consumable providing a speed boost (e.g. using Rock Candy, Cupcake or Empowering Feast)

You can recover health with either a health regeneration buff (e.g. Bowl of Skalefin Soup, War Supplies or Empowering Feast) or using your junundus skills (in particular the Junundu Tunnel>Junundu Bite combo)
A video guide for the mission can be found here.

quests/quest:gww:16673/sections/walkthro.text: Completing this quest will require you to travel the whole Underworld, killing groups of three Terrorweb Dryders at the six other monuments of Grenth. Upon accepting the quest one group of Terrorwebs will spawn next to each of the monuments. When your party kills one of the groups the corresponding Reaper is spawned next to the monument.

Pay extra caution at the monuments of Forgotten Vale, Twin Serpent Mountains and Spawning Pools. Kill the surrounding monsters before the Terrorweb Dryders, because otherwise they might attack the Reaper and cause your party to be taken back to the outpost from which you entered the Underworld.

As the quest suggests, once a Reaper is freed, you will be able to speak to him and he can teleport you to any other Reaper that you have freed. The Reapers also have quests to offer, but be aware that taking any quests without consulting the party is unwise as they tend to spawn dangerous groups and might cause a party wipe if the party isn't prepared.

Note: Although it is very tempting to take the quest immediately after completing the preceding quest or soon after clearing one or two nearby areas due to the offered teleportation possibility, it might be wise to clear the furthermost problematic monuments before accepting the quest to avoid having to fight against the Terrorwebs and the other enemies surrounding the monuments at the same time.

Bringing disruption skills or even better Frozen Soil can severely speed up this quest because of the number of resurrection skills the undead groups have.

Once this group of Tengu has been slain, claim your reward from Wulk Cragfist.

quests/quest:gww:25450/sections/notes-1/.text: Since he is a tall creature, the quest markers will not be visible

You can make this quest a little easier by taking Yijo Tahn (Study Buddy quest) along with you.

quests/quest:gww:10451/sections/objectiv.text: Head to Scoundrel's Rise east of North Kryta Province. Find the cause of the undead's westward movement.
Lord Timot is the source of the undead movement. Destroy him.
Return to Captain Greywind [Skills] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:10451/sections/walkthro.text: Head east along the beach of North Kryta Province and enter Scoundrel's Rise. Just as you enter you will see Settlement Scout Drew (if he dies you cannot complete the quest until you zone somewhere, luckily he stands right next to a portal). He will point you in the direction of Lord Timot, a zombie boss who you must kill to complete the quest. Proceed east until you can travel south into a dead-end swamp where the boss will be located. The route is guarded by 4 Executioners who may prove difficult to take down if faced all at once. Timot himself can be found at the bottom of the path together with some Smoke Phantoms.

When you enter the dead-end swamp, Lord Timot and the Executioners will begin moving out towards you, leaving the rest of the undead behind. The Executioners move much more slowly than their Lord, passing them at the swamp's entrance, so you can wait for them to separate in order to kill Timot without his guardsmen. Once outside, Lord Timot will turn southeast and march towards the Gates of Kryta, eventually becoming unreachable when he moves beyond the portal. Consider pre-clearing the large clump of enemies just east of the swamp entrance to make sure you can safely catch up with Lord Timot if you intend to let him move away from the Executioners before engaging him.
Once he is defeated, return to Captain Greywind for your reward.

If you have War in Kryta content active, Lord Timot will spawn close to Joh the Hostile and his group, who will fight and kill Lord Timot if he comes too close, rendering you unable to complete the quest until you zone. You are advised to move to the area quickly to prevent this from happening.

quests/quest:gww:10451/sections/notes-1/.text: The reward focus item has the Stone Chakram skin, not Jeweled Chalice.

This is the earliest opportunity to obtain the skills Desecrate Enchantments, Animate Bone Fiend and Barbs in the Prophecies campaign, so consider bringing three Signets of Capture if you are a Necromancer.
Eventually, Timot will leave Scoundrel's Rise into Gates of Kryta, making the quest impossible to finish in the current instance.

quests/quest:gww:277488/sections/target-.text: Rhea's Crater can be reached via the eastern exit of Seafarer's Rest, or through the Gyala Hatchery explorable area from the Leviathan Pits.
There are 7 hidden Oni groups (each consisting of 3 to 5 of them):
Southwest of Grenth's shrine, at the southern end of the curving path at the western edge.
In the inlet bordering the landmass west of Grenth's shrine.
Short distance from the Gyala Hatchery exit, near the shrine.
In a nook at the northeastern corner.
At the end of the eastern path that leads away from the Aurios Mines.
At both ends of the bridge just north of the petrified leviathan marked on the area map as a dark green square (see map), these ones have a chance to drop Ungues of the Oni.
Outcasts are hostile to other enemies - you can save ~22 kills if you let them fight it out.
Arius, Dark Apostle - depending on how fast you can reach her location - may already have been killed by other mobs.
Talous the Mad may also get in a fight with the sea life of the area, but will most likely emerge victorious. She and Wavecrest Stonebreak will fight each other when their patrol paths intersect.
The eastern side of the central area contains actual water - a rarely seen thing in the Jade Sea region.
This area has one boss of each profession available in Guild Wars Factions.

quests/quest:gww:269415/sections/walkthr.text: When the mission begins, you will be in the town of Beetletun. White Mantle soldiers will threaten villagers on the east side of the mission map. Position Miku close to them during their speech and when they become hostile, kill them as quickly as possible. Keep using Nature's Blessing to heal the villagers; all survivors will assist you in the battles that follow. Following the initial fight, Keiran will receive an additional shout, "There's Nothing to Fear!"; use it often on both sides of the village to increase the durability of your allies.

Six waves of enemies will then attack alternating sides of the village: waves 1 and 3 come from the Nebo side; waves 2 and 4 come from the Watchtower side; and waves 5 and 6 come nearly simultaneously from both sides. Avoid the front lines, so that you can cover as many villagers as possible with Keiran's shout and stance. Use interrupts frequently, and watch out for minion-producing necromancers that hide outside the village.
Just before the final wave, Miku will announce, "looks like the big one".

quests/quest:gww:269415/sections/notes-1.text: "There's Nothing to Fear!" is added to Thackeray's skillbar after he shouts "There's nothing to fear!" (shortly after the Initial Confrontation).
"Find Their Weakness!" and "There's Nothing to Fear!" benefit from his high Expertise, reducing their energy costs.

You must equip Keiran's Bow to start this mission. However, you can switch it out for another weapon, including a long- or flatbow for pulling and especially one that has weapon upgrades appropriate to Keiran's skills. However, you cannot increase his maximum health, energy, or total attributes using weapon or armor upgrades.
As with other missions, you can still receive credit for completing Rise even after you die, as long as all enemies are killed. To get your rewards, wait for the quest to update before mapping out.
Crossing the portals will teleport you to the middle of the village; you can take advantage of this to jump quickly from one battlefront to the other.

Some consider this a good farming option for Ebon Vanguard reputation points, War Supplies, or sweet points because it can be completed in under 8 minutes, i.e. in an hour, approximately 37,000 experience, 38 supplies/sweet points, and 9,400 EV points.

quests/quest:gww:25702/sections/walkthro.text: Throughout the campaign there are resurrection shrines. An NPC can be found at each shrine who can grant a bounty for hunting certain creatures. The bounty normally provides extra experience and, more importantly for this quest, it includes Sunspear promotion points. Gather 100 points to achieve the Master Sergeant level. You can see your progress in your Hero panel; press H to open it, and select the "Titles" tab. As soon as you reach the rank of Master Sergeant your quest log will update and you can go to Runduk to collect your reward.
