quests/quest:gww:18605/sections/objectiv.text: Talk to three potential recruits in Zehlon Reach and convince them to join the Sunspears.
Talk to Morik in Zehlon Reach and ask him to join the Sunspears.
Talk to Dahni about Morik's dilemma.
Tell Morik that Dahni is leaving to join the Sunspears.
Talk to Ando and ask him to join the Sunspears.
Kill the beast threatening Ando's family.
Tell Ando that the threat is gone.
See Castellan Puuba for your reward

quests/quest:gww:18605/sections/walkthro.text: The first potential recruit, Morik, can be found on a pier in the center of the north coast in Zehlon Reach. Speak to him to find out he doesn't have confidence in himself and would rather stay with Dahni. Speak to Dahni, who can be found a little south on the same pier. She is the second recruit and has already decided to join the Sunspears. She asks you to tell Morik that she is leaving. Talk to Morik and he will join the Sunspears. The third recruit, Ando, can be found southwest in a small village. Speak to him to find out he can't leave the village until he is certain that it will be safe without him protecting it. Head a little south and kill the group of five Irontooth Drakes that is threatening his village. Tell Ando that the threat is gone and he will join. Return to the Sunspear Great Hall and speak to Castellan Puuba to collect your reward.

quests/quest:gww:18605/sections/notes-1/.text: This quest appears to have been added after the November 30th, 2006 update.
To significantly decrease the quest time, use Charge or a similar team running skill and set your heroes to avoid combat. Leave from Jokanur Diggings and run North past all enemies.

quests/quest:gww:21974/sections/objectiv.text: Light candles on all four braziers in the catacombs to appease the angry spirits.
Return to Necromancer Munne for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:21974/sections/environm.text: Upon completing the quest, the braziers will no longer spawn. Neither will the Restless Spirits, resulting in a higher presence of Restless Corpses in the swamp water, as they will no longer be thinned out by the spirits.

quests/quest:gww:21974/sections/walkthro.text: Talk to Necromancer Munne and take the 4 Votive Candles. Proceed through the Catacombs and place a candle on each of the four Remembrance Braziers in the order shown on the mission map.

Since some of the braziers are located in Swamp Water, which causes constant health degeneration, you need to monitor your health drop. Be careful about drawing aggro from nearby foes at the same time.
Any healing skill, such as Orison of Healing or Troll Unguent, to counter with the swamp water effects.
Life stealing skills like Vampiric Touch can be useful too, though there are few foes to use them against in the swamp water.

quests/quest:gww:21974/sections/notes-1/.text: If you die, you will lose the candles. Just go back to Necromancer Munne for more candles. She will take any extra back when you go to get your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25417/sections/objectiv.text: Complete the Advanced Defense Techniques course.
See Headmaster Quin for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25417/sections/walkthro.text: This quest requires the completion of four sub-quests given also by Instructor Ng. The order of completion is entirely optional.

Completing the Condition Removal quest should be relatively easy. Before entering the dojo, set all of your attribute points in Restoration Magic. Before you start the course, use Generous Was Tsungrai to increase your maximum health, and be ready to drop the ashes when you need a quick burst of healing or just before the spell ends. Keep Resilient Weapon up as soon as you're first hit with a condition; it should deal with any damage you take as long as you're not bleeding. You can also train Soothing Memories if you want to be extra sure of survival. As the warrior attacking you uses self-knockdown skills, kiting can be very effective too.
You should use the same tactics as the ones for Condition Removal, however you should train Soothing Memories if you didn't already as you will be losing health much faster.

You can also create spirits and back up. They will focus their attack the spirits. Just remember to keep creating spirits when the current ones are about to die. You can then choose to wait it out or try to deplete their health.

The Disruption quest is slightly harder; you should mix your attributes between Communing and Spawning Power for this quest. It also helps to have taken a secondary profession with strong interrupts. You should bring Pain as well as Dissonance, and any secondary profession skills that can interrupt. Essentially your goal here is to reduce the instructor to 50% health, while they try to use skills against you with very long casting times. If you have any interrupts that cast quickly, save them to counter Meteor.

Skill Chaining is the hard part of this quest and you may want to level up before attempting it. It should be very easy by the time you reach level 10. Simply put all of your attribute points into Channeling Magic and bring Cruel Was Daoshen, Channeled Strike, Spirit Rift, and Spirit Boon Strike. Before they start attacking use Cruel Was Daoshen. When they start attacking use Channeled Strike then drop Cruel. Next use Spirit Rift and Spirit Boon Strike. Repeat if necessary.

quests/quest:gww:276380/sections/objecti.text: Clear Riven Earth in the Tarnished Coast of all enemies in hard mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:276380/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 250 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:276380/sections/instruc.text: "Clear Riven Earth in the Tarnished Coast of all enemies in hard mode."

quests/quest:gww:276380/sections/target-.text: This area is to the east of Rata Sum. To get here for the first time, start from Vlox's Falls and head west across Arbor Bay.
After completing Genius Operated Living Enchanted Manifestation, speak with Sokka to obtain an Asuran Beacon, which can be dropped to create a G.O.L.E.M. 1.0 to aid your party.
This is a popular spot for farming Asura reputation due to the large concentration of Raptor Nestlings in a cave close to the entrance.
Discounting quest influences, it has been reported to range from 260 to 299.
These Quests influence the spawns in this area: The Asura Trap, The Cipher of Dwayna
Keep spread out when engaging dinosaurs (especially Ceratadons); their area damage can easily kill bunched up heroes and henchmen.
Keep away from the forested area west of the Golem Foundry, to avoid triggering the hidden spider groups there (but do find the Simians in the clearing north of it).
There are also hidden spider groups right before reaching Gallow Nooseknitter.
After completion of the Eye of the North storyline, the small number of Destroyers in the north are actually separated into two hostile groups that will fight each other.

This area comprises approximately 6% of the mappable area in Eye of the North; you can uncover most of it during the G.O.L.E.M. mission by killing the originally spawning Destroyers and before activating the kilns.

quests/quest:gww:201251/sections/notes-1.text: It is significantly easier and faster to complete the mission in hard mode and then do the first bonus in normal mode (assuming you don't need the hard mode bonus for the Guardian of Tyria title).

quests/quest:gww:63658/sections/objectiv.text: Enter the tournament and defeat your first round opponent.

quests/quest:gww:63658/sections/rewards-.text: You gain 5 Norn reputation points for killing your foe (unless Norn rank 8 or above)
You gain a quest reward after beating all 6 rounds, see Final Round: Fight! (first time completion) or Final Round, Championship Edition: Fight! (for repeated victories)

quests/quest:gww:63658/sections/notes-1/.text: Talk to Gellir Frostshield to start the tournament. A fee of 100gold is automatically deducted from your character upon confirmation.
Round one opponents may be Kilroy, Kisai, Little Thom, Lo Sha, Sogolon, or the Great Zehtuka. Please refer to the Norn Fighting Tournament article for details on their skill sets.
This quest is automatically completed upon defeating the round 1 opponent. The follow-up quest Round 2: Fight! is automatically accepted (that is, if you win round 1.)

As your character progresses through the quest chain (i.e. tournament rounds), should your character lose, your quest log will again show this quest as not completed, allowing you to talk to Gellir Frostshield to start again without needing to re-acquire this quest from Magni the Bison.
For the detail of spectators' quotes, see talk page.
You can use Heart of the Norn to gain extra health depending on the title rank for an extra boost.

quests/quest:gww:63658/sections/support-.text: Your character must have the quest Round 1: Fight! in order to enter the tournament. Obtain the quest from Magni the Bison if this is the first time your character is entering the tournament or is re-entering the tournament after previously winning the tournament. Losing the tournament will keep that quest in your quest log. Talk to Gellir Frostshield to start the tournament. A fee of 100gold is automatically deducted from your character upon confirmation.
Rules

There are six consecutive rounds that you must win in total to be considered the winner of the tournament. In the first five rounds, an opponent is randomly selected from a subset of those listed below, i.e. each opponent can appear in only a particular round so that each round has a different set of potential foes. In the sixth round, your opponent will be Magni the Bison (although, in extremely rare cases, you might face Palawa Joko during Final Round, Championship Edition: Fight!).

The tournament takes place in a small explorable area designed as an arena. Each of the 6 rounds of battle (5 random opponents and the final round) takes place in a different instance of the area. Your character starts each round in a side room. The door to the battle chamber is locked for 10 seconds; when the timer ends, the door opens and your previously neutral opponent turns hostile. However, you will not aggro your foe until you step out of the side-door, giving you extra time to cast enchantments or preparations. When you leave the side room, the door will close behind you and you must kill or be killed.
Rewards
Upon winning the final round for the first time, you receive:
150 Norn Reputation Points
A Touch of Guile
"Dodge This!"
"Finish Him!"
The Bison Cup
Repeated completions of the tournament reward one Bison Championship Token each.
Winning the first five rounds award Norn reputation points to characters with a Norn rank of less than eight: 5 → 10 → 15 → 20 → 25 (for a total of 75 points).
One-time rewards
Defeating Xandra and Kahmu will unlock them as heroes.
After defeating Zho for the first time, you will receive Zho's Journal, which is required to obtain the Black Moa Chick.
The first time you defeat the Great Zehtuka with Zehtuka's Great Horn in your inventory, he will replace it with Zehtuka's Horn; the new item will be customized to your current character.
Skill recommendations
Guide to the Norn Fighting Tournament
Enchantment removal, to counter the monk opponents.
Condition removal to remove blindness.
Self heal.
A spirit spammer with sufficient damage (e.g. Signet of Spirits) and self-healing (e.g. Vampirism) or protection (e.g. Union).
Counters to Magni:
snares to keep out of melee range, e.g. "You Move Like A Dwarf!".
Skills that cause Blind to nerf his attacks.
Interrupts, to prevent him from using his Bear Form.
The tournament cannot be fought in Hard mode; the game will always switch to Normal mode upon entering.
Opponents do not drop loot; however, their companions can drop seasonal items if they die before you win the round.

Spirits placed in the starting room will not have line of sight to the main battle; spirits placed in the starting room's doorway will. Alternatively, you can move the spirits into the main room just before the gate shuts.
A "You were not worthy." message appears if you die during the tournament.

snares to keep out of melee range, e.g. "You Move Like A Dwarf!".

You will earn 3,000 Ebon Vanguard reputation points upon your first completion of this dungeon on normal mode, and 1,500 for subsequent completions. 4,500 Vanguard reputation points are awarded for completing this dungeon for the first time in hard mode, and 2,250 for subsequent completions in hard mode.
Feeding a "Blobby" will cause it to join your party as an ally.
Rragar and Hidesplitter do not regenerate their health.
When fighting Rragar and Hidesplitter, it is useful to kill Rragar first, because he carries Resurrection Chant.

quests/quest:gww:67860/sections/shared-q.text: Leave from Doomlore Shrine and go southwest through Dalada Uplands, to Grothmar Wardowns, and then southeast into Sacnoth Valley. Head south to the southwest corner, as this is where the entrance to Rragar's Menagerie is found.
Level 1

Talk to the Beacon of Droknar to gain Dwarven Raider. Head north past Blobby (a neutral Ooze). Just after, some Fleshreavers will appear. Save any Fleshreaver Morsels that they might drop; you can use them to tame Blobby and have him follow you. Throughout the first level, the Charr and Fleshreavers are hostile; you can leave them to kill each other off and mop up the remains.
To get the optional dungeon map, take the north-east passage. Proceed carefully to avoid aggroing too many of the Charr patrols along the way.

On your way back to the western passage, pick up a Dwarven Powder Keg (bundle) or clear out the group of Charr near the weakened wall and then return for it. Your next goal is to acquire the dungeon key to advance to the next level. Crack the wall to your right and ignore the cracked wall in the chamber you enter. Take the right passageway that will lead to a group of Charr (led by a boss). After finishing them off, continue down the passage to meet Rragar Maneater and still more Charr. You can pull about half of them without aggroing Rragar. As you kill off the group, Rragar will take off leaving behind the key. Return back to the wall you've cracked open. Head north-west. Magma Blisters will appear in the piles of magma, which can cause Burning when stepped on. After killing the blisters, turn left (west) and go down the ramp (the first ramp is a dead end the second is a tunnel; can be easy to miss if your screen is dark.

As you enter the next chamber, Fleshreavers will pop up; an Ooze group will pop-up right at the shrine - be careful not to aggro the charr and ooze at the same time. After finishing these foes, you will notice a Keg Station near a Beacon of Droknar. Grab a keg and head north to find more Charr and Blisters. Blow up the cracked wall you find. Do not enter immediately to allow the Fleshreavers and Charr to fight; move in and finish them off. Avoid any remaining Charr on your way to Level 2.
Level 2

As you enter and head left, a group of Charr will run away, unleashing two Boulders and closing a large gate. You have three options: run quickly to the right and follow them out the gate (so it does not lock you in); snare them (so that you can kill them before they exit); or allow them to lock the gate. The fight is easier using the first two options, but you end up in the same place regardless.

This hallway has several spots where there are rockslides. You will eventually encounter a sizable group of Charr. You can easily pick up the dungeon map for this level if you head into the left chamber from where you encountered the Charr group. After handling these, you will enter an area with a body of water you will have to walk through, Ooze pop-ups will occur. Turn right after handling the pop-ups and head north through the entrance. Turn left after going through this entrance. Keep heading south-west, killing a group of Fleshreavers a few Charr groups.

It is easy to miss the boss key on this floor. You will reach a Beacon of Droknar. West of this beacon is Rragar Maneater, again, with Charr around him. You can pull the Charr without Rragar to make the battle easier. Get the Key.
Start heading south-east to reach the entrance to the last level. You will fight through Fleshreavers, Charr, and Ooze to get there.
If you kill the Charr group at the beginning of the level before they close the gate on you and pick up the key they drop, then use the Dungeon Lock, the gate will close.
Level 3

Head to the south passage. After you kill the Fleshreavers blocking the way, head west. Charr and Fleshreavers will start appearing in hybrid groups. Head south-west when possible. You will reach a chamber with a Beacon of Droknar and another Keg Station; as you approach, the wall nearby will be blown up by an incoming Charr group. Head directly south down this now-opened passage and retrieve the boss key, after killing a sizable group of Fleshreavers with a boss type amongst them.

Start heading north-west when possible now. You may fight through several Fleshreaver groups. However, if you are careful and watch the patrols, you can avoid all but one or two. Use the Boss Key to open the gate.
Rragar and Hidesplitter

Most players concentrate on killing Rragar first; if Hidesplitter dies first, Rragar will resurrect him. Hidesplitter, on the other hand, goes into a rage when Rragar dies, but if you got this far, you should not have any trouble surviving anything he tries to throw at you.
Skill recommendations
There are plenty of exploitable corpses for minion masters; however, Fleshreaver Hounds deal holy damage, Ominous Oozes have Verata's Aura, and Shimmering Oozes have Spiritual Pain.
Shadow Form is a poor skill for tanking; Fleshreaver Hounds can cause substantial melee-range damage through it.
On the first level, Charr and Fleshreavers are hostile to each other; however, they are allied with each other on the second and third levels.

The key to an easy victory is by bringing down the health of one boss to a minimum and then attack the other boss. If Rragar Maneater is killed first, then Hidesplitter will enter an aggressive stance and deals more damage. If Hidesplitter gets killed, Rragar Maneater will try to resurrect his companion using Resurrection Chant.
On the first level, near the door to Level 2, beware of the popup Ooze group. Try to pull the Charr away from that spot to avoid being overwhelmed.

On the first level, in the far southwest corner there is hidden treasure. There are also 2 other hidden treasures in the same chamber to the north. On the first level, to the southeast of the northern Dwarven Powder Keg Station there is a secret switch which opens a secret tunnel. There is a hidden treasure and a Dwarven Ghost down that secret tunnel. There are 2 hidden treasures by the exit from the first level.
On the second level there is a Dwarven Ghost next to the Beacon near the Boss Key and there is a hidden treasure next to the Boss Key. There is a hidden chest to the northeast of the boss door.

On the third level, south of the entrance there is a secret switch for a secret chamber. In the secret chamber there are five hidden treasures and one Dwarven Ghost. In the four alcoves near where the boss key is obtained there is a hidden treasure in each alcove.

The charr stronghold is inaccessible if any party member has not completed Assault on the Stronghold. It is possible to have completed Assault on the Stronghold without having completed the other charr missions in the same mode (by alternating Normal and Hard mode), in which case the stronghold will also be inaccessible.
If any party member has Forbidden Fruit active, the western back entrance will be open.
If any party member has Single Ugly Grawl Seeks Same for Mindless Destruction in Ascalon active, the southern path leading into the stronghold will be accessible.
Players can still enter the stronghold by exploiting Dismount Siege Devourer right at the front gate, facing away from it.
The southeastern area is teeming with Burning Spirits and Flowstone Elementals, making it arguably the most dangerous part due to the high number of spells dealing AoE fire damage.
Keep an eye out for patrolling groups of Burning Spirits, especially the one including Borrguus Blisterbark; they move quickly along a circular route and can quickly overwhelm your party.

Bring skills for party-wide damage mitigation and/or elemental resistance such as Ward Against Harm. Party-wide caster shutdown tactics, especially Daze (e.g. using Technobabble) and interrupt (e.g. using Complicate) are also advised to counter Searing Flames, Fire Storm and Savannah Heat.
A single well-placed Pain Inverter there is usually a guaranteed kill.

There are four bosses in the Charr stronghold (after completion of Assault on the Stronghold), which makes it worth saving until you have a Boss Bounty. Approach from the west or south, to avoid the well-defended eastern entrance (Charr Seekers stand atop the ridge, making it hard to get close without taking significant damage).
Fozzy Yeoryios is in a group with a lot of potent healing; it can be difficult to kill them without the proper counters.
As with any area in the Charr Homelands, if at least two player characters are in the party, several Siege Devourer can be mounted which can make vanquishing much easier.
For a complete Vanquish all worms in the southwest corner have to be killed.

The flaming spirits surrounding Borrguus Blisterbark will shout phrases normally attributed to the Charr, e.g. "For the warband!". After extended periods of time, the animation of the fire in the burning forest will freeze and will not resume until you have exited and restarted the game. At certain times, the Stronghold will be closed to all players. This requires a full reset from a outpost.

Wind Riders chain Cry of Frustration interrupting initial skill usage efficiently. Use the Fount Of Maguuma environmental effect to gain an advantage.
There's a large number of hidden foes, more than the visible ones.
Devourers hide by the dry paths, especially in the south.
Maguuma Spiders spawn near the bamboo-like growths.

Moss Scarabs sometimes spawn with spiders but mostly along verdant paths, especially in the north. They use Verata's Gaze to steal minions and Vampiric Touch can be deadly if too many spike a single ally.
Some of the popup groups may stagger their appearance, spawning some after you've already engaged the first enemies. Be aware of this and be sure to check in case any didn't aggro.

It is sometimes possible to vanquish this area without killing all of the non-popup scarabs and devourers along the path to/from Skyward Reach.

Many of the foes in this area, particularly the Storm Kin and Hydra, travel quickly along long routes, making them easy to miss. Placing numerous spirits will help to slow or kill many of these patrolling foes.

quests/quest:gww:18001/sections/objectiv.text: Meet Zerai the Learner on the Cliffs of Dohjok.
Collect 12 Iboga blossoms by slaying Beautiful Iboga. You have collected [0...12] of 12 Iboga blossoms.

quests/quest:gww:18001/sections/walkthro.text: After entering the area go to Zerai and talk to him, he will now start following you. You don't have to worry much about him since he will not be attacked. Now follow the road westwards. you will find the Beautiful Iboga along the path.

The Beautiful Iboga are level 10 and are in groups of 3 each. Make sure you can kill them fast since they are of the Mesmer profession. More healing does not work too well against Mesmers, faster killing is most of the time the key in beating them. A skill to remove Hexes is a good thing to have in your skillbar while doing this quest.
Make sure to take the most Northern path westwards.

If Zerai gets stuck along the way, just go back and move around him for a bit he will get unstuck again and follow once more. When you arrive at the portal of Jokanur Diggings, make sure to wait for the Quest log to update before going through the portal (the game is prone to not registering this part, make sure you res any dead party members before walking up to the gate of the diggings!). Last but not least, collect your reward from Midauha.

If you get to the entrance to Jokanur Diggings and you don't have all 12 blossoms, you can still take Zerai there and then enter Jokanur Diggings. The quest will update that you have escorted him. Now all you need are the other blossoms and you can simply re-enter the Cliffs of Dohjok, find enough blossoms, then map to Jokanur Diggings for the reward.

quests/quest:gww:18001/sections/notes-1/.text: You can easily complete this quest while working on Leaving a Legacy and Identity Theft in the Cliffs of Dohjok.

If you keep the quest active, the 4 groups of Beautiful Iboga can be farmed for Iboga Petals and Sentient Seeds. At low levels, they can also be farmed for experience with the Fire Imp and Dunkoro as an ally from the quest Leaving a Legacy.
If Zerai the Learner is left too far behind, it will cause him to stop moving. The only way to make him follow you again is to get within range of where he stopped.

Heirlooms of the Mad King (Halloween quest)

Without active quests, your party will only encounter Gargoyles and Skales:
None of them can inflict conditions on your party, so condition removal skills are unnecessary.
They do not rely on attacks to deal damage, so skills that block, cause misses, or inflict the blind condition are less effective here.
Each of them use at least two hexes, so consider bringing additional hex removal skills.
They have additional armor rating against cold damage and Mergoyles use Mantra of Lightning, so consider not bringing skills nor equip weapons that deal cold nor lightning damage.

They are all spellcasters, so consider bringing anti-caster skills and/or various Ranger nature rituals that can benefit your party but cannot benefit them (such as Favorable Winds, Infuriating Heat, Toxicity since Bog Skale Blighters use Chilblains, and Winnowing).

At point 3, in addition to the group of Kurzicks, you will also find several groups of Yeti. Arrahhsh Mountainclub is among one of the groups. Defeat him and you can pick up the Golden Lantern to complete Return of the Yeti. You can then either go back to Magistrate Kin immediately for your reward or finish Scout the Coast and then go back to Magistrate Kin later.

quests/quest:gww:13110/sections/walkthro.text: Obtain the quest from Scoutmaster Theron just outside of Eredon Terrace. You will need to defeat four Kurzick scout groups. There are seven possible locations where these groups will appear (marked with an "X" on the quest map). Follow the quest marker to each location in the Maishang Hills. A Kurzick Scout and a random group of Kurzicks will spawn at each location. Only killing the Kurzick Scout is necessary to update the quest log, so pulling and killing the Kurzick Scout and not killing the rest of the group can save time.

After defeating the Kurzicks at each of the four locations, return to Scoutmaster Theron to collect your reward. Remember that you should not map travel to Eredon Terrace before collecting your reward, since leaving Maishang Hills area will automatically abandon this quest.

quests/quest:gww:67787/sections/walkthro.text: Beware of the Ooze! They multiply and can wipe an unprepared party with PBAoE damage spam.
Level 1

On the first level, you need to take out a number of groups of Needling Lavastriders and Lifeweavers. If you kill the Lifeweaver first, the rest of each group is much easier. The Oozes should be pulled carefully or avoided if possible since they tend to swarm the party quickly with high amounts of AoE damage. There are plenty of pop ups throughout the dungeon, so try to aggro mobs one by one.

To the south of the start point there is a dungeon map guarded by spiders. Following the map, you will find an Asura Flame Staff bundle among the dead asura, which must be used to light up the nearby spider web blocking the path. (You do not need to keep the first staff, but keeping hold of the second one you obtain later will save time.) Continue until you reach the next Beacon of Droknar - where a ranger boss will appear.

There are a lot of spiders and poison traps in the next room, so pick a wall and keep close to it to avoid spawning too many spiders. Head for the northwest gate, pickup the staff and burn the web. (Keep this staff.) Keep close to the right hand wall and you can avoid many of the Elementals and Forge Masters in this room, but be wary of the Fire Bombs that Lok sends down the passage. Exit the room by the next web, and kill the plant popups in the next room. Pass the narrow passage with more Painweavers and poison jets.

Clear the spiders out from around the Spider Eggs. It is useful to the party if you light the eggs one at a time to prevent the party being overwhelmed by the popups. Also on the fourth group of eggs, the spawn of spiders is delayed. After lighting all the eggs, a Spider Matriarch will appear.
Repeat this process on the eastern bunch of Spider Eggs. Once complete, the Dungeon Key will appear on the ground in front of the last Spider Web gate.

If a party misses the first matriarch by running straight past the eggs, then the key will not drop at the matriarch near the entrance to the next level. The party must run back to the first matriarch and kill it. This will cause the key to spawn in the location of the matriarch near the entrance to level 2, this had been mistaken for a bug but can be avoided by simply killing the first matriarch as you pass the eggs.
Level 2

Head east as soon as you enter the level to retrieve the asura flame staff, then back-track to the start and head southwest. Ignore the tunnel with the Spider Web gate in front of it and head up the stairs past the Fire Darts. If the Fire Darts are difficult to deal with, they can be disabled by killing a Flame Guardian off the direct path to the south of the entrance; a safer route to the Guardian can be opened at the Area Map using a Secret Switch that can be revealed using Light of Deldrimor within compass range of the entrance.

Head west across the waterlogged next room and to the Beacon of Droknar. Ignore the skelk-infested passage and head northwest to the large room with the Spider Web gate in front of it. From here there is only one route to the end of the dungeon, with large numbers of spiders and a few popups of plants.

In the final room there are many spiders, from Level 14 Spiders to Lifeweavers of Level 24, and it is recommended to kill all of the spiders before starting to burn the eggs because of the pop ups. There are ten clutches of eggs to burn, in two groups of five on either side of the chamber. Burning all five clutches on one side causes a large group of spiders including a Spider Matriarch to spawn, and after you've burned the last clutch of eggs, Arachni spawns with another large group. You have to kill the matriarch and Arachni to complete the quest and reveal Arachni's Spoils; it doesn't matter which one you kill first.
Killing Arachni

Blinding skills, or skills such as Price of Failure and Spiteful Spirit make the final boss battle much easier. The damage from Arachni comes from Barrage and Whirling Defense. If you use Diversion to stop Barrage then Arachni will simply stop attacking.
Whirling Defense can be turned to your advantage with Pain Inverter.
Skill recommendations

Minion Masters are extremely useful, as they are very efficient in killing the many weaker mobs. There are enough corpses to easily support two Minion Masters. Ebon Battle Standard of Honor can boost the damage output considerably.
AoE damage is extremely useful against the large groups of low level spiders.

Because of the large number of Ranger and Paragon enemies in this dungeon, consider taking a skill like "Shields Up!" or Winds to reduce the damage you and your party takes. The henchman Talon Silverwing uses "Shields Up!".

When trying to do this dungeon, remember that your NPC allies are warriors as primary, and they'll rush to attack anything crossing their aggro bubble. This can be extremely dangerous when trying to pull the oozes on level 1, because the NPCs following you will attack your target and aggro all the others. For this reason, it's highly recommended to bring along with you at least one running skill to break NPCs' aggro on foes.

quests/quest:gww:25655/sections/objectiv.text: Speak with Misela Wahmeh to learn if she is worthy of her father's inheritance.
Escort Misela Wahme while she gathers Mosu Reeds to make a cure for the swamp fever.
See Healer Zenwa for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25655/sections/walkthro.text: Talk to Misela and then follow the compass point to find the mosu reeds. Kill the skale that are there and walk past the mosu reeds to get Misela to find them.

quests/quest:gww:66578/sections/requirem.text: To get to the Secret Lair of the Snowmen, get the quest Lost Treasure of King Hundar from Koris Deeprunner in Umbral Grotto. You must have already given him all of the map pieces first. Subsequent runs do not need additional map pieces.

quests/quest:gww:66578/sections/notes-1/.text: It is only possible to enter this dungeon via dialogue in the required quest.

You do not gain experience for defeating the 165-180 foes in this dungeon; however you can gain reputation points if you take the bounty from the Beacon of Droknar when you enter. This typically results in earning approximately 1,500 points per run (2,000 in hard mode).
These snowmen have no apparent weakness to fire or resistance to cold. All but the Angry Snowman are fleshy.
Killing the Angry Snowman disables the 4 ice dart towers and the ice geysers in front of his spawn.
The snowmen in this dungeon deal cold damage with their normal attacks.
Consider bringing Shield of Absorption on a monk, as the damage can not be mitigated by block or Protective Spirit as you will most likely not take enough damage in a single shot for it to matter.
Completion of this dungeon will fill in page #17 of the Master Dungeon Guide storybook.

If Koris Deeprunner dies at Freezie and does not self-resurrect, the dungeon chest might not spawn. Similarly, if he gets stuck (e.g. on a bridge or locked chest), he will not reach the final room and you will not be able to complete the dungeon. If that happens, flag any heroes or henchmen out of the way and then maneuver around the NPC to guide him around the obstruction and back to the final room.
The Snowmen near the second shrine sometimes spawn inside a wall; they can be ignored or killed using ranged, non-projectile attacks.
Koris Deeprunner can spawn without his bow. However, he will still attack as if he has it, and hit enemies but does 0 damage.

quests/quest:gww:66578/sections/shared-q.text: Upon entry, you can take Dwarven Raider from the Beacon of Droknar. The destination is all the way South. You will encounter massive numbers of fragile Snowmens which pose little threat. There are Ice Darts and Ice Spouts spread through the area, avoid them as much as you can.

After a short walk inside, a Mischievous Snowman will send two Ice Boulders your way, dodge them or your party will be killed instantly. The Area Map can be found at the second Beacon of Droknar, but the quest is pretty straight forward and it is not of much use.

At the third Beacon of Droknar, turn east to get the Dungeon Key which drops after defeating the Angry Snowman at the very back of that little room. Procede slowly in there, many Snowmen and Ice Darts stand inside. The darts will deactivate after killing the key holder. Unlock the Dungeon Gate and fight the group immediatly behind it.

Head east, and battle Freezie and its large Snowmen army. This boss will drop the Boss Key, which opens the door right behind. Enter this chamber to trigger the final dialogue which spawns the Chest of Wintersday Past to collect your rewards.
Mid-way through the quest, you will find Wintersday Moa along the western side of the cave before the dungeon gate.

This is probably the best place to farm Deldrimor points. Large amounts of points can be farmed from here, as there are 170 enemies in a relatively small area. The mobs are also level 15 and relatively easy to kill.
To repeat the quest, you must zone out then back again after accepting the quest reward. For instance, changing districts after receiving the reward.

In normal mode, a typical run takes 10-15 minutes, and yields approximately 1000 Dwarven Reputation points. In hard mode, a typical run takes slightly longer, and yields approximately 50% more Dwarven Reputation points.
Sometimes Koris Deeprunner will get stuck at a locked chest, making the quest impossible to complete.

quests/quest:gww:18046/sections/objectiv.text: Help Hatuk kill the Great Fire Flower and pass his rite of passage into manhood.

quests/quest:gww:18046/sections/environm.text: Once this quest is completed, Hatuk will no longer spawn in Zehlon Reach.

quests/quest:gww:18046/sections/walkthro.text: Obtain the quest by entering Zehlon Reach from The Astralarium and heading west along the northern path. Once obtained, head further west across the swamp. The Great Fire Flower is not a boss, and should not pose a problem even for solo players of the same level as the foe. The foe is not in the same group as any of the surrounding plants, so you may wish to kill those separately first.

quests/quest:gww:18046/sections/notes-1/.text: If you come from Champion's Dawn when obtaining this quest, you might want to head south first, to swing by the Resurrection Shrine near the entrance to the Cliffs of Dohjok to obtain the plants bounty.
The pre-quest offer dialogue will always get initiated for non-Nightfall characters despite the fact that non-Nightfall characters will not be offered this quest.

quests/quest:gww:25442/sections/objectiv.text: Go to the first checkpoint and make certain that it is secure. Kill any Luxon invaders you find.
Go to the second checkpoint and make certain that it is secure. Kill any Luxon invaders you find.
Go to the third checkpoint and make certain that it is secure. Kill any Luxon invaders you find.
Go to the fourth checkpoint and make certain that it is secure. Kill any Luxon invaders you find.
See Scoutmaster Arne for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25442/sections/walkthro.text: Simply visit each of the four checkpoints. A Luxon raiding party will spawn at all four locations, which you must kill in order to progress. Each Luxon raiding party spawns in two groups, each consisting of three to five Luxons. After the first group is eliminated, the second group immediately spawns. Once your party has cleared all four checkpoints, return to Scoutmaster Arne for your reward.
Unlike previously, the checkpoints are now random, with the possible options indicated in the maps on the right.

quests/quest:gww:25442/sections/notes-1/.text: This quest was used for Kurzick fast faction farming prior to the November 13th 2008 update, which added the requirement of killing the Luxon spawns (and moved the 4 spawn locations), significantly increasing the time required to complete the quest.
Like all Factions repeatable quests, if you leave the instance in the middle of the quest, even before accepting the reward, the quest will automatically be abandoned.
This quest is listed under the "Melandru's Hope" heading in the quest log.
You can combine this quest with Charting the Forests since one of the objectives is to get to 5 points in Melandru's Hope.

quests/quest:gww:25309/sections/objectiv.text: Proceed to the first patrol point in Traveler's Vale.
Proceed to the second patrol point in Traveler's Vale.
Proceed to the third patrol point in Traveler's Vale.
Return to Van the Warrior for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25309/sections/walkthro.text: Proceed to each patrol point, potentially clearing enemies along the way to avoid overaggro. Once all three points have been visited, return to Van the Warrior.

quests/quest:gww:25309/sections/notes-1/.text: Despite the warning of enemy encounters, there is no need to fight any targets during this quest, and no additional enemies are spawned.
Because of this, the quest combines well with other quests in Traveler's Vale, particularly Shiverpeak Stragglers, The Way is Blocked, and The Road to Borlis Pass.
It is possible to start from Borlis Pass and complete the objective for the second patrol point before the first.
It is impossible to complete the third patrol point objective prior to the other two.

It is possible to encounter Devona near the third patrol point. She will be running into the Vale from the Ascalon Foothills and engage in combat throughout the area. There is no need to keep her alive or assist her during this quest.

quests/quest:gww:10659/sections/environm.text: While this quest is active, all the Am Fah in Wajjun Bazaar will be allies. This also means that they will not ambush parties out near the areas closer to Nahpui Quarter. Because of this, it may be advantageous to hold off on completing this until you finish your quests in The Undercity and/or vanquish Wajjun Bazaar. The exceptions to this are the quests Captured, The Xunlai Agent, Deactivating P.O.X., and Street Justice. The Am Fah in the immediate area will still be hostile.

After completing this quest, all the Am Fah will be allies until you take either Refuse to Drink or Drink from the Chalice of Corruption. You can use this advantage and keep the Chalice of Corruption in the inventory for some time, while doing other quests in Wajjun Bazaar and nearby areas.

quests/quest:gww:10659/sections/walkthro.text: Just speak with Brother Tosai. You can find him near the entrance to The Undercity surrounded by legions of Am Fah.

quests/quest:gww:10659/sections/notes-1/.text: If you take the Refuse to Drink quest that follows, you will immediately be attacked by the Am Fah there, and Brother Tosai.

As mentioned above, leaving this quest in the Quest Log without finishing it, allows to do other quests in the zone without enemies, since the Am Fah foes are allies. This is a good way to grind experience to level up since there are many quests in that zone that give 3,000 XP rewards. It also makes vanquishing easier.
Sometimes this quest does not show in the quest log.

quests/quest:gww:9624/sections/objective.text: Speak to Guardsman Pongtu in Xaquang Skyway.
Locate Imperial Guardsman Tingjo in the Shenzun Tunnels. Obtain a shelter pass from him.

quests/quest:gww:9624/sections/walkthrou.text: After obtaining the quest, speak to Camp Guard/Guardsman Pongtu who is a few steps away from Yikaro. Imperial Guardsman Tingjo can be found outside of Maatu Keep in Shenzun Tunnels. When you go near Tingjo, several groups of Afflicted will approach Tingjo and attack; however, the quest doesn't require you to defend Tingjo from the Afflicted, so you can speak to him before the Afflicted arrive to receive the shelter pass and map travel to Senji's Corner to collect your reward.

quests/quest:gww:9624/sections/notes-1/b.text: The shelter pass is not an actual quest item as it doesn't appear in your inventory when you receive it from Tingjo.
Camp Guard Pongtu is incorrectly identified as Guardsman Pongtu in the quest log.

quests/quest:gww:205732/sections/objecti.text: Kill Selvetarm and accompanying foes in Slavers' Exile.
*BONUS* Kill Selvetarm and accompanying foes in Hard Mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:205732/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 40 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the *BONUS* Objective for an additional 100 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:205732/sections/walkthr.text: As per the Selvetarm portion of The Last Hierophant quest.

quests/quest:gww:14617/sections/requirem.text: Miller Quang, a resident of the area, has been keeping a treasure chest of his on a near-by small island. Since the increase of the local Naga population, he has been chased off of the island, and has grown increasingly uncomfortable with leaving his chest there.

quests/quest:gww:14617/sections/objectiv.text: Find Miller Quang's chest on Yuroso Island.
Return the chest to Miller Quang.
See Miller Quang for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:14617/sections/walkthro.text: Head to the beach north of Zen Daijun and you will see a small island surrounded by Naga. The chest is on this island, at the top of a small ledge. Grab the chest, and kill the Naga if you want; killing the Naga is not required, but is recommended, as they will be attacking you. Return to Miller Quang to get your reward.

quests/quest:gww:14617/sections/notes-1/.text: On your attempt to retrieve the chest you will probably run into the Naga boss Tin Dao Kaineng, so go prepared for a challenge.
If you have completed Winds of Change, no Naga will spawn. However, many groups of stronger enemies (level 24 scavengers) will be present.

quests/quest:gww:63756/sections/notes-1/.text: If you do not have the required quest, you cannot leave the first room due to the closed Gates of Strength.

For the Anything You Can Do quest, you must kill the Fragment of Antiquities on Level 1. However, there is a bug where killing the Remnants of Antiquity will sometimes also fulfill the quest requirement.
Completion of this dungeon will fill in page #7 of the Master Dungeon Guide storybook.

quests/quest:gww:63756/sections/shared-q.text: The first floor consists of several gates which indirectly lead to the second floor, which contains the boss. To open each gate, you need to step on a proof within the dungeon, of the same name. For example, stepping on Proof of Strength will open the Gates of Strength, and so on. The dungeon includes rooms with several posts which fire Ice Darts and Ice Jets. The streams are easy to avoid; however, the darts can be very annoying and potentially deadly. A party entering a room full of dart posts and foes should be wary. It is usually safer to pull enemies out of the rooms to avoid being hit by the darts.

In general, players should avoid fighting large mobs of monsters and getting trapped in places where they are constantly taking damage. This strategy will make for a relatively straightforward run. When players arrive at the boss area, they will see Remnant of Antiquities and two other ice elementalist creatures. It is recommended to dispatch the non-boss creatures first, as they cast dangerous AoE spells.

Defeating the Remnant of Antiquities can be a very difficult and grueling experience, especially if the party has no reliable interrupts or dazing. The boss casts the monster-only AoE spell Diamondshard Mist, a type of ward which causes bleeding and heavy damage to those within its boundaries at its expiration.

If you are unable to prevent the spell, it is essential to keep moving in order to stay out of the Diamondshard Mist. The party should spread out so that multiple party members avoid taking heavy damage simultaneously. If the entire party dies, there is a nearby resurrection shrine, so you can return to the assault before the boss can recover completely. A persistent party can defeat the Remnant regardless of Death Penalty.
Bring hex removal as the dryders and elementals in this dungeon use a lot of hexes.

Careful pulling and avoiding bunching up will make this dungeon a relatively easy run. Also, because the traps can deal a lot of damage, it's advised to lure the enemies to a location where the traps can't hit you.

Bringing the following skills will make this dungeon much easier: Ward Against Elements, Mantra of Frost, Light of Deliverance, Extinguish (for the final boss), and interrupts such as Savage Shot, Distracting Shot, or anything causing Daze.

There are not many fleshy creatures, so skills that inflict Bleeding, Disease or Poison, or require corpses are less effective here. Plus, the Whirling Wisps carry Banishing Strike, destroying minions quickly.
Cold damage is less effective here, since several foes have additional armor rating against cold damage.
The henchwoman Zho uses Broad Head Arrow, making her the henchman of choice for this dungeon if you don't have a hero with a daze skill yourself.
When facing the boss, spreading your party so his Deep Freeze won't hit all of them at the same time is very helpful.
Or you can bring Pain Inverter and a party with spirits and minions so the boss kills itself.

quests/quest:gww:25515/sections/objectiv.text: Defend King Frozenwind while he summons new Ice Elementals.
Return to the Reaper of the Ice Wastes for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25515/sections/walkthro.text: Once this quest is activated, groups of enemies will start spawning northeast. Each wave consists of separate groups of two yellow Terrorweb Dryders, one or two silver Terrorweb Dryders, and one Skeleton of Dhuum. One group will head towards King Frozenwind, while the other heads toward the Reaper of the Ice Wastes (see the map). A total of three waves will spawn within a short span of time. King Frozenwind has four level 28 Ice Elementals to assist him, but they will fall quickly to the fire spells of the dryders. You must protect both King Frozenwind and the Reaper. If either of them dies, your party is taken back to the outpost from which you entered the Underworld. You can either split your team into two groups which take one group of foes at a time or you can take all foes as a whole group if you aggro them at their spawn-point. Note that the following waves spawn quickly, so you will need to take them down quickly.

King Frozenwind and his allies can take down a group of 4 Terrorweb Dryders, thanks to his Ward Against Harm. This can lighten the load on your team if you position yourselves to primarily defend the Reaper, who is practically defenseless.

quests/quest:gww:25515/sections/notes-1/.text: Consider bringing Winter to convert the Dryder's fire damage to cold damage, against which the Ice Elementals have a higher resistance.
If capturing a spider from this location, it should be noted that the spider spawns and the quest is completed after the first wave is destroyed, even though more waves will continue to come.
Due to the rapid spawn times of the Dryders, the fact that they are spawned in separate places, and they spawn with Skeletons of Dhuum this quest is now considered the hardest of The Underworld.

quests/quest:gww:63659/sections/objectiv.text: Speak to Artificer Mullenix when you are ready to defend the Eye of the North.

references.title: Service: In Defense of the Eye

quests/quest:gww:63659/sections/objectiv.text: Fight alongside the Eye's support personnel. Defend the Eye of the North from the attacking Shiverpeak Centaurs.

references.title: Service: In Defense of the Eye

quests/quest:gww:63659/sections/objectiv.text: See Artificer Mullenix for your reward.

references.title: Service: In Defense of the Eye
Service: In Defense of the Eye
Service: In Defense of the Eye
Service: In Defense of the Eye

quests/quest:gww:63659/sections/walkthro.text: After talking to Artificer Mullenix, you will be taken just outside the entrance of Eye of the North to the Service: In Defense of the Eye zone, which shares a map with Ice Cliff Chasms. There, you will be attacked by several waves of Shiverpeak and Modniir Centaurs.

references.title: Service: In Defense of the Eye

quests/quest:gww:63659/sections/walkthro.text: The easiest way to complete this quest is to retreat up the ramp. Rangers and spirit spammers then have plenty of time to lay/summon their spirits/traps without the attacking centaurs being aggroed (beware spirits too far down attacking the centaurs). Players can then aggro the centaurs causing them to move up the ramp to attack. Once your enemies are grouped together on the ramp unleash a barrage of area of effect damage, this will quickly destroy the level 8 Shiverpeaks Centaurs leaving only the level 20 Modniir Centaurs. Take notice of the Modniir Centaur's skill Trample as it can cause havoc if you're not prepared.

references.title: Service: In Defense of the Eye

quests/quest:gww:63659/sections/walkthro.text: An alternate strategy calls for running directly to the left at the beginning of the mission. Simply allow the centaurs to reach the front of the Eye, then pull them into smaller groups. This tactic allows players to avoid the mobs of Centaurs (which ultimately requires less firepower), but requires more time in return.

references.title: Service: In Defense of the Eye

quests/quest:gww:63659/sections/walkthro.text: Another strategy is to retreat far back on the ramp and stay there, pull one group of foes at a time on the ramp by using a ranged attack such as a longbow. This strategy puts fewer demands on group composition, though inclusion of two elementalists, two healers and two warriors is recommended (not counting the three allies that join you on this mission).

references.title: Service: In Defense of the Eye

quests/quest:gww:63659/sections/walkthro.text: Consider bringing along Disease as it will spread between the centaurs but your party will remain safe from it (provided you do not bring Zhed Shadowhoof). This tactic is much better when combined with Toxicity.

references.title: Service: In Defense of the Eye

quests/quest:gww:63659/sections/walkthro.text: There are enough centaur bodies to support two minion masters which will greatly help.

references.title: Service: In Defense of the Eye

quests/quest:gww:63659/sections/walkthro.text: The centaurs arrive in 3 waves which will attack whether or not the previous wave has been defeated. The first wave consists solely of warriors. The second is solely rangers so the newly acquired spirit Winds is useful against this wave. The third and final wave contains warriors, rangers, monks, and a boss. Beware of the Ice Boulders that roll across the frozen lake, as they will kill anyone they roll over, including the Centaurs themselves.

references.title: Service: In Defense of the Eye

quests/quest:gww:63659/sections/walkthro.text: Edge of Extinction is also very useful here, again provided that you do not bring Zhed Shadowhoof.

references.title: Service: In Defense of the Eye

quests/quest:gww:63659/sections/notes-1/.text: This quest provides an opportunity to map Ice Cliff Chasms for Master of the North: equip your heroes with speed boosts (especially "Charge!", "Fall Back!", and "Incoming!") and move away from the portal to the EotN outpost. The remainder of the area will be free of foes, giving you plenty of time to scrape.

references.title: Service: In Defense of the Eye

quests/quest:gww:63659/sections/notes-1/.text: Several exits are blocked by closed doors. Those that are open (the portals to Boreal Station and Norrhart Domains) lead back to the EotN outpost. This is also true for the exit to The Battledepths, even though it appears blocked (you can walk through the doors).

references.title: Service: In Defense of the Eye

quests/quest:gww:63659/sections/notes-1/.text: When you resign, you get the usual, message that "Your party was defeated". However, you remain alive and centaurs continue to attack you until you're returned to the outpost.

references.title: Service: In Defense of the Eye

quests/quest:gww:63659/sections/notes-1/.text: If you kill the boss too far from the main battle (the base of the stairs), your three allies will start celebrating at the location where the boss died; they will not return with you to the stairs to kill any remaining foes.

references.title: Service: In Defense of the Eye

quests/quest:gww:63660/sections/objectiv.text: Tell Artificer Mullenix when you are ready to start the training session.
Help train the service staff by leading them into combat. Destroy 20 practice dummies in 3 minutes.
See Artificer Mullenix for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:63660/sections/walkthro.text: When you start the quest, you are brought to an instance of the Eye of the North outpost along with the three service staff. After the twenty training dummies pop up, you must help the NPCs destroy them. The NPCs will attack the closest dummy and continue around the circle until all twenty are destroyed. The dummies don't attack or use skills, so healing skills and interrupts are not needed.
As the dummies leave exploitable corpses, a minion master with damage skills.
Signet of Spirits build and Great Dwarf Weapon works exceptionally well.

To complete the quest as quickly as possible, resign when you first arrive at the site, before the timer begins. Type the /resign command before entering the mission, and simply hit enter as soon as possible after the loading screen disappears. The log will say you have failed, but it will also say you killed all twenty dummies. In about five seconds, you will be returned to the Eye of the North, and you can claim your reward.
Even if you miss this opportunity, the quest itself should be easy.

quests/quest:gww:63660/sections/notes-1/.text: The dummies actually count as Charr according to the title Rebel Yell so when you kill/destroy one you will gain 2 energy.
The instance inside the Eye of the North outpost used for this quest is labeled Mano a Norn-o.
Resigning while the timer is up will mark the quest as completed.

quests/quest:gww:277646/sections/objecti.text: Clear Shadow's Passage in Kaineng City of all enemies in hard mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:277646/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 50 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:277646/sections/instruc.text: "Clear Shadow's Passage in Kaineng City of all enemies in hard mode."

quests/quest:gww:277646/sections/target-.text: Exit from Dragon's Throat, or travel through Bukdek Byway
These quests will affect the spawns in this area:
This area always contains one chest. When entering the area from Bukdek Byway, the chest most often spawns near Afflicted, otherwise you'll find it near Jade Brotherhood.

If starting from Dragon's Throat it is possible to vanquish only the Afflicted groups, The Afflicted Ako and one small spawn before him, by pulling them closer so you are never within range for the Jade Brotherhood to spawn. This will decrease the number of foes to vanquish to approximately 8.

quests/quest:gww:269408/sections/objecti.text: Find information about the White Mantle's plans.

quests/quest:gww:269408/sections/walkthr.text: Follow the main path from Aurora Glade until you reach the area with the Henge Portal, killing foes along the way. Find and read the White Mantle Missive deep in the camp to finish the quest.
As in other Hearts of the North mini-missions:
Use Keiran's Sniper Shot against targets called out by Miku, which causes over 900 points of damage if it hits (unless Miku's Promise of Death is removed).
If she dies, Miku will self-resurrect after a short period of time.

quests/quest:gww:269408/sections/notes-1.text: "Find Their Weakness!" is added to Thackeray's skillbar after he shouts "Find Their Weakness".
The skill benefits from his high Expertise, reducing its energy costs.
If you have rearranged your skills so that your 7th skill slot is taken, "Find Their Weakness!" will replace the skill on this slot.

While you must equip Keiran's Bow to access this mission, you can switch it out for another weapon, including a long or flatbow for pulling and especially one that has weapon upgrades appropriate to Keiran's skills. However, you cannot increase his maximum health, energy, or total attributes using weapon or armor upgrades.

quests/quest:gww:63661/sections/objectiv.text: Travel to Raven's Point to begin the hunt.
See Hogni Truthseeker for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:63661/sections/walkthro.text: Start from Olafstead and head north-west to the entrance of Raven's Point dungeon. Head inside, where you will find the Shadow Spawn surrounded by mobs of Shadow Vaettir, Mist Vaettir and Stormcloud Incubus.
The Vaettir and Incubus can easily be pulled away from the Shadow Spawn and defeated before taking it on. Once the creature is defeated, return to Hogni Truthseeker.

Do not talk to Olaf (at Olafstead), since he will redirect your party to a different primary quest in the same dungeon. Olrun Olafdottir, at the entrance to this dungeon, offers an additional secondary quest, which does not interfere with this quest.

quests/quest:gww:25260/sections/objectiv.text: Go to the Breach and kill Charr Fire Callers to obtain a bottle of fiery unguent.
Return to Shalev the Hermit for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25260/sections/walkthro.text: Find Shalev in a cave on the western border of Old Ascalon, west-northwest of Sardelac Sanitarium. Map travel or navigate to Piken Square. Cross the small valley to the west and climb the path to the right (watching for Charr patrols) to find up to three Charr Fire Callers. When defeated, one will drop a bottle of fiery unguent. Bring it back to Shalev for the reward.

quests/quest:gww:66402/sections/requirem.text: From Vlox's Falls head south. You will also pass through this dungeon as part of Finding Gadd. If you have access, you can start directly from Gadd's Encampment (however, if your goal is completing Lost Souls, you will need to visit the other entrance to find Crewmember Shandra; only she can open the door required for the quest).

quests/quest:gww:66402/sections/notes-1/.text: If you do not have the required quest, you cannot pass the door to the southeast by the Scrap of Parchment. It is still possible to navigate between the exits to Arbor Bay and Gadd's Encampment.
Completion of this dungeon rewards 1,500 Asuran points in normal mode and 2,250 in hard mode. Completing the dungeon for the first time in each mode rewards twice that.
To complete the dungeon, you must destroy the Soul of Fendi Nin.
Although Shandra cannot be killed, she does not attack or use skills in the dungeon. On the contrary, she often body blocks allies trying to maneuver.
On the second floor, the Northernmost room with three interlinking traps allows an entire party to walk behind the traps against the wall, bypassing them entirely.
Completion of this dungeon will fill in page #12 of the Master Dungeon Guide storybook.
If Fendi Nin is killed by a flame jet without any interaction from your party, the Soul of Fendi Nin will not appear. Instead, as you approach the jet, Fendi Nin will respawn with full health.

On very rare occasions, Fendi Nin will not spawn. Unfortunately, there is no work-around; you must restart the dungeon. This happens if you have quests for other dungeons. There is an interval of approximately 2 seconds during which Fendi respawns and the soul disappears (these two events do not occur simultaneously - Fendi respawns first). If the soul has been killed before its disappearance and after Fendi's respawn, its death will trigger the chest but will not unspawn Fendi and the archers.

quests/quest:gww:66402/sections/shared-q.text: Level 1

The first level is self explanatory: find the area map, kill the Cursed Brigand that has the dungeon key and proceed to the second level. Take care to not warp to Gadd's Encampment. If you started from Gadd's Encampment, you will have to fight your way towards the Arbor Bay entrance to get Crewmember Shandra or else the door for the dungeon lock will remain closed.
Level 2

Kill the Cursed Brigand to the immediate left of the portal. When it dies, a chest spawns with an unlit torch, which you will need for most of this level. Take down the mob that blocks the way to a lit brazier and then light all the flame braziers in the circular graveyard room. Be ready for a large mob of undead and enchanted that spawn in a random spot within the room after the final one ignites; they must be killed before the exit door will open for you. Next, make your way to the tiled room to light the 2 of 4 unlit flame braziers, spawning yet another mob including a Cursed Brigand. Kill the Brigand to get the dungeon key to exit the level (he can be pulled away from his group). Leave the torch behind and head for the exit to the next level.
Level 3

The third level is similar but with more undead mobs, and careful pulling is recommended here. Once again, you need to light up a series of flame braziers to gain access to the final area. These are farther apart than on the other levels, but can easily be lit without a speed boost if you are careful about clearing any groups of foes in the way.

After entering the level, take out the group of undead and enchanted to your right, blocking the first unlit brazier. Open the nearby chest to get a new torch, light it on the nearby brazier, light the now unblocked brazier, then drop the torch for the moment. There are 2 groups of foes and a patrol along the route to the second unlit canister; pull carefully and take them out one at a time. Recover the torch to light the next set of braziers until you come to the entrance of the large chamber with the final set of containers to be lit.

There are several groups in this chamber, but you only have to take out 3 or 4: a group that spawns near the entryway; a group that spawns near the boss lock; the group that spawns with a Cursed Brigand (who carries the final key); and perhaps one more group. After taking out the group near the entrance, light the two stands to the left and right of the entrance. Then, carefully walk around and between any other mobs to light two braziers up the center of the room and two more in the back. If you have heroes and henchmen, flag them to the back so they do not accidentally aggro any foes and take down the Brigand's group, which has now spawned. From this position, you can also confront the group blocking the boss lock, safely leaving room to maneuver and retreat.

Take the zig-zag corridor protected by Poison Spouts and give your party a chance to heal before killing two Bone Dragons and some undead archers. These are the last of the ordinary groups in the dungeon. The final area contains Fendi Nin and his archer body guards.

Fendi Nin has two forms: as an undead and as a soul. When you kill him in his undead form, a group of Damned Crewmen will replace the Skeleton Archers accompanying him and he will turn into the Soul of Fendi Nin. Keep spread out: the Crewmen will spike clumped party members with Clamor of Souls and Fendi attacks with armor-ignoring area of effect damage; they can quickly wipe an unprepared party, especially in hard mode. Fendi remains in his soul form for approximately half a minute, after which time he will revert back to his undead form and the crewmen will revert back into archers. Repeat the process until the soul form has been destroyed to finish the dungeon.

Note: the Damned Crewmen spawn wherever the Skeleton Archers were, so you can kill the Archers then lure Fendi Nin away from where the Archers were killed and the Crewmen will not aggro when the Soul of Fendi Nin spawns. However, Skeleton Archers spawn on top of Fendi Nin when he reverts to his undead form.
Ward of Stability and Ward Against Melee are very useful, since much of the difficulty of the dungeon comes from the knock downs caused by Skeleton Wizards and Zombie Brutes.
Blind is also prevalent; skills such as Sight Beyond Sight and Antidote Signet can help.
Holy damage is highly effective against the Skeletons and Zombies.
Rising Bile, if placed on the soul form before it reverts, will still proc proving an effective way to do damage to the soul form while dealing with the archers and regular form.
Since Zombies are the only fleshy creatures in the dungeon, skills that inflict Bleeding, Disease or Poison, or require corpses are less effective here.
Remember to keep your party spread out before engaging Skeleton Wizards to mitigate their AOE damage.
Consider clearing rooms and areas of all foes before lighting flame braziers.

Lighting all braziers in the southwest room on 3rd level (where you get the last key) opens a secret passage near the very beginning of the 3rd level (Northeast corner of the map). Consider running back to that secret area to collect hidden treasures.

You may not receive credit in your Dungeon Guide for this quest even after talking to the correct NPCs. Fendi Nin might not spawn at all, making it impossible to finish the quest and forcing the player to resign and restart.

quests/quest:gww:23146/sections/objectiv.text: Collect heket legs to sate Rokel's unending hunger. You have collected [0...10] of 10 heket legs.
See Bonesmith Rokel for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:23146/sections/walkthro.text: While a character has this quest active, all Heket killed will drop a Juicy Heket Leg each until your character holds 10 of it in their inventory. This means that if those collected legs are dropped or moved into storage, the Juicy Heket Legs will start dropping off any Heket again.

Places where a lot of Heket can be found include (but not limited to) northern portion of Barbarous Shore, southern half of Dejarin Estate, the watery areas of the Floodplain of Mahnkelon, and the northwestern corner of Vehjin Mines.

quests/quest:gww:23146/sections/notes-1/.text: Heket killed in the Tarnished Coast locations (Guild Wars Eye of the North) also drop these legs while this quest is active. If available consider combining with the quest Frogstomp.
This quest is easily done with Desperate Measures active. The Skree and the Heket kill each other, leaving the player only needing to pick them up.
This quest doesn't change status to "completed" when you gather all required items.

quests/quest:gww:277903/sections/objecti.text: Clear the Shenzun Tunnels in Kaineng City of all enemies in hard mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:277903/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 150 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:277903/sections/instruc.text: "Clear the Shenzun Tunnels in Kaineng City of all enemies in hard mode."

quests/quest:gww:277903/sections/target-.text: The To Tahnnakai Temple primary quest will lead characters through this area for the first time.
Travel from Senji's Corner via the Nahpui Quarter explorable area or Xaquang Skyway. Alternatively, when available leave directly from Tahnnakai Temple or Sunjiang District.
These quests will affect the spawns in this area:
4 additional Afflicted popup when approaching The Afflicted Kam (besides those already visible).
Similarly, only 4 foes are visible as you approach The Afflicted Li Yun, after which he and several Afflicted popup (see map).
There is an Am Fah group that patrols a long route along the western side and might be missed.
10 Royal Guard allies spawn near Maatu Keep during the quest Battle in the Sewers. However, they are not as intelligent in battle as heroes or henchmen.

Sometimes the vanquish won't be complete even after you kill everything in the area. In this case, run to all the portals. Occasionally a group of foes walks through it to disappear and you can get the reward as you approach the portal.

quests/quest:gww:18493/sections/objectiv.text: Search the road to Ascalon for refugees.
Lead the refugees to Yak's Bend.
Return to Captain Osric [Skills] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:18493/sections/walkthro.text: Make your way to the quest marker on the south side of Traveler's Vale. It is quickest to reach from Borlis Pass, but starting at Yak's Bend allows you to clear foes along the way, making it easier to protect the refugees on the way back.

A short way north of the refugees, on the path from Yak's Bend, you will find about a dozen Stone Summit warriors and mesmers, in four groups of 2-4 dwarves each, gathered close together. Either pull them and kill them there, being wary of overlapping patrols, or bypass them by traveling along the east side of the map.

At the quest marker, you will find Elsa Alston and a handful of Ascalon Refugees. Speak to Elsa and the group will begin following you. If the Stone Summit dwarves spawned by the quest are still alive when a player approaches Elsa, they will run south and spread themselves out over the road, but there is ample time to evade them and return to Yak's Bend along the eastern path. Lead the refugees to Yak's Bend and make sure the quest has updated before entering the outpost and claiming the reward from Captain Osric.
Elsa Alston is the only refugee who is required to survive to complete the quest.

quests/quest:gww:18493/sections/notes-1/.text: While it is tempting to take Captain Osric's other quests, The Way is Blocked and The Road to Borlis Pass, at the same time, the enemies spawned by these three quests overlap substantially, making them significantly easier to complete separately.

If attempting to complete one or both of these quests at the same time, most of the Stone Summit spawned by Shiverpeak Stragglers will move out of the way if you bypass them and speak to Elsa Alston first.
The Ascalon Refugees will shout "Look out! It's the Dwarves!" when you engage any mob, even if they aren't Dwarves. They will also attack, despite Elsa's claim not to be fighters.
The refugees will continue to follow you and fight after leading them to Yak's Bend.
The refugees may be dead by the time you arrive, forcing you to restart the trip to them again.

quests/quest:gww:278028/sections/objecti.text: Clear the Silent Surf in the Jade Sea of all enemies in hard mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:278028/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 150 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:278028/sections/instruc.text: "Clear the Silent Surf in the Jade Sea of all enemies in hard mode."

quests/quest:gww:278028/sections/target-.text: The Journey to the Whirlpool primary quest will lead characters from the Leviathan Pits through this area on their way to Unwaking Waters (Luxon).
Several secondary quests that can be obtained in Leviathan Pits also take place here.
These quests will affect the spawns in this area:
If It Weren't for Bad Luck....
Complete exploration of this area will yield about 2.8% to the Canthan Cartographer title track.
Be wary of groups that move along long overlapping patrol paths, especially the Outcast groups, as some of them move very fast.
There are 5 hidden Oni groups (each consisting of 3 or 4 of them):
Around the southern bend from the Seafarer's Rest exit.
In a corner at the end of the western path heading south away from Leviathan Pits.
In the small nook east of the bridge that connects the eastern island to the larger landmass.
South of Kenrii Sea Sorrow's location, along the cliff face.
On the southernmost island (the path above the pier).

The Afflicted, the Outcasts, and the Jade Sea wildlife are all hostile to one another and will fight each other if two different groups come within aggro range. If you take your time before moving to the more densely-patrolled areas, many of the groups may have already killed each other.
Because so many groups kill each other, it is possible to complete the vanquish by killing only around 175 enemies, despite there being over 240.

quests/quest:gww:279970/sections/objecti.text: Clear Silverwood in the Maguuma Jungle of all enemies in hard mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:279970/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 150 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:279970/sections/instruc.text: "Clear Silverwood in the Maguuma Jungle of all enemies in hard mode."

quests/quest:gww:279970/sections/target-.text: Exit from Quarrel Falls or Bloodstone Fen. Alternatively, the quest Mysterious Message will lead you here from Druid's Overlook.
Complete exploration of this area contributes approximately 1.8% to the Tyrian Cartographer title.
It is possible to walk through the portal leading to Ettin's Back without zoning into that area. Note that this does not yield otherwise non-explorable parts of the map.
There are hidden groups of Moss Scarabs.There are no Life Pods.
There are two groups of three Maguuma Hunters that are easily missed. One group patrols a long route in the northwestern corner of the map, south of Bloodstone Fen. The other patrols in the south.
Mind also the lone Wind Rider that patrols the fountain area in the northeast.
With great patience, it is possible to bring a party of 8 from the Temple of the Ages.
Just outside the entrance to Bloodstone Fen, there is an area that appears to keep "foggy" as if unexplored.

quests/quest:gww:25677/sections/objectiv.text: Seek out Master Engineer Jakumba in Zehlon Reach.
Lure the fierce skale by attacking his brethren by the fishing docks. x of 4 groups remain.
Recover Jakumba's magical compass from the fierce skale.
Return the magical compass to Jakumba.
See Lieutenant Murunda for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25677/sections/environm.text: Once this quest is completed, Hungry Skale will no longer spawn in Zehlon Reach.

quests/quest:gww:25677/sections/walkthro.text: Start from Jokanur Diggings. Head North to find Lieutenant Murunda. She is located next to the resurrection shrine along side some stone pillars and columns.

After taking the quest, you need to talk to Master Engineer Jakumba, who is just outside of compass range to the East along the northern bank of the water. He will send you to the North to hunt down the skale who took his compass. Kill the small groups of Hungry Skale until you find the Fierce Skale who will drop the compass.
Once the compass is retrieved, simply return it to Master Engineer Jakumba, then return to Lieutenant Murunda to turn in the quest.

quests/quest:gww:25677/sections/notes-1/.text: Lieutenant Murunda and the Hungry Skale spawn by default, including for non-Nightfall characters who will not be offered this quest.

quests/quest:gww:40831/sections/objectiv.text: Speak with Sujun again to begin the test.
See Instructor Ng for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:40831/sections/walkthro.text: You will be provided with two skills. Carefully read their descriptions to see how they can interact. Then use them in the right order to gain the synergetic effect. This will make defeating your trainers easy. You may also defeat them using other skills.

quests/quest:gww:40831/sections/notes-1/.text: Since the skills are given upon accepting this quest, you can actually learn all the skills if you wait until you are Weh no Su. Simply take the quest, abandon it, switch secondary professions, then take the quest again. Repeat until your character learns all the skills.

quests/quest:gww:25453/sections/objectiv.text: Go to the north shore and kill the Naga boss Xsshsss Zsss
See Miller Quang for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25453/sections/walkthro.text: The destination (as the crow flies) is North-Northwest from Miller Quang. The best route to take is through Linkei Township and across the map to the North of Teipao Island, then up and around the outcropping of rock. This will help you avoid the extremely large encampment of Crimson Skull located to the North of Hanzing Pier.

quests/quest:gww:25453/sections/notes-1/.text: The Naga 'boss' is accompanied by 6 other Naga, varying from levels 6 to 10.
After completing the Zen Daijun mission, this map area is crawling with Crimson Skull groups.

quests/quest:gww:25653/sections/objectiv.text: Find the skree harpy nests on the Cliffs of Dohjok and destroy the skree hatchlings. You have destroyed [0...26] of 26 hatchlings so far.

quests/quest:gww:25653/sections/walkthro.text: Simply head southwest from Champion's Dawn towards the shrine outside Beknur Harbor. Before you get to the shrine, you will encounter 26 hatchlings to kill. For every 6 or so hatchlings that you kill, a higher level Harpy Mother will spawn, so be careful not to be overrun by harpies.
