quests/quest:gww:4631/sections/requireme.text: Defeat the four Lords of Anguish with Mallyx the Unyielding quest active, then speak with High Priest Zhellix.

quests/quest:gww:4631/sections/objective.text: Protect High Priest Zhellix while he performs the opening ritual on the Ebony Citadel.

quests/quest:gww:4631/sections/rewards-1.text: Chance of receiving Primeval Armor Remnants for party members.
Citadel Chest which gives one of Mallyx's unique items to each party member.
Completion of Mallyx the Unyielding quest and taking its reward.

quests/quest:gww:4631/sections/walkthrou.text: Defending Zhellix
The first step of the mission is to protect Zhellix while he performs the opening ritual. Nineteen (19) groups of monsters either spawn or arrive at the area of the priest:
Margonites
Titans
Torment creatures
Stygian Veil creatures.
The waves come in the following order (pay close attention to when each group spawns as some groups will spawn on the death of certain foes and not others):
From the south and west: 1 Margonite Anur Ki, 1 Margonite Anur Su, 1 Margonite Anur Kaya, 1 Margonite Anur Tuk, 1 Margonite Anur Vu and 1 Margonite Anur Rund.
From the east: Shortly after (and regardless of whether any were killed) 1 Misery Titan, 2 Fury Titans, 1 Tortureweb Dryder and 1 Greater Dream Rider.
From the west: As soon as all original members of group 2 die (Titan spawns do not count, group 1 does not matter). 2 Anguish Titans and 1 Tortureweb Dryder.
From the west: As soon as original members of group 3 die. 1 Heart Tormentor, 1 Mind Tormentor, 1 Water Tormentor, 1 Soul Tormentor and 1 Flesh Tormentor

From the south: As soon as original members of group 4 die (spawns from Call to the Torment do not count). 1 Mind Tormentor, 1 Earth Tormentor, 1 Flesh Tormentor, 1 Sanity Tormentor and 1 Spirit Tormentor
Center (just south of priest): As soon as original members of group 5 die. 1 Stygian Fiend, 1 Stygian Brute, 1 Stygian Horror, 1 Stygian Hunger, 1 Stygian Golem
Center (just south of priest): As soon as group 6 dies. 1 Stygian Fiend, 1 Stygian Brute, 1 Stygian Golem, 1 Stygian Hunger, 1 Stygian Golem
From the south: As soon as group 7 dies. 5 Greater Dream Riders.
From the west: As soon as group 7 dies (they spawn at the same time as group 8). 2 Tortureweb Dryders, 1 Rage Titan, 1 Despair Titan.
From the south: As soon as group 8 dies (even if group 9 did not). 1 Heart Tormentor, 1 Soul Tormentor, 1 Margonite Anur Vu, 1 Margonite Anur Tuk, 1 Flesh Tormentor
Center: As soon as group 10 dies. 1 Heart Tormentor, 1 Water Tormentor, 1 Stygian Horror, 1 Stygian Brute, 1 Stygian Golem
Center (just south of priest): As soon as group 11 dies. 6 Dementia Titans.
From the east: As soon as group 12 dies. 2 Misery Titans, 2 Anguish Titans.
From the South: As soon as original members of group 13 die. 1 Margonite Anur Ki, 1 Margonite Anur Ruk, 1 Margonite Anur Su, 1 Margonite Anur Tuk, 1 Margonite Anur Vu
Center (slightly west): As soon as group 14 dies. 2 Rage Titans, 2 Despair Titans, 2 Dementia Titans (these Titans do NOT spawn other Titans).
Center (slightly east): As soon as group 15 dies. 5 Stygian Fiends.
From the west: As soon as group 16 dies. 1 Heart Tormentor, 1 Mind Tormentor, 1 Flesh Tormentor, 1 Water Tormentor, 1 Soul Tormentor.

and 19, final mobs after group 17 dies: From the east: Misery Titan, Greater Dream Rider, Tortureweb Dryder, Heart Tormentor, Water Tormentor and Spirit Tormentor. From the south: Margonite Anur Ki, Margonite Anur Ruk, Margonite Anur Rund, Margonite Anur Su, Margonite Anur Tuk and Margonite Anur Vu.

After the original members of groups 18 and 19 are killed, the door to Mallyx's citadel opens and the priest will be removed from the party list, where he was listed as an ally. As soon as any party member steps past the door, a short cut-scene is played, the whole party is transferred inside the Citadel and the door is closed behind them.

Mallyx will be standing on a pedestal and will not be hostile, as will be four spirits. As soon as any party member comes close enough to Mallyx (about 1.5 times the aggro radius), Mallyx will give a short speech then turn hostile and attack.
Moving the Priest:

A technique that makes fending off the groups much easier is to pull the priest away from the spot where he is performing the ritual (which is the end point for all incoming waves). This can be achieved by having the priest chase a foe down to the gate of the citadel, and then killing that foe. The priest will remain in that spot and will not try to return to his original spot.

The best candidate for this action is one of the two Fury Titans that come as part of group 2. Since they are original members of the group, the following spawns will not trigger until they die. And because they are the smallest titans, they will not spawn any more after their death. Therefore, the party should leave one Fury Titan alive, bring him close to the priest so that the priest starts attacking him and then have his target slowly back up all the way to the Citadel door and wait for the priest to catch up. If done correctly, protecting the priest will not be a factor in defeating these monsters.

Fighting away from the priest: Another tactic to facilitate defending the priest is, once the priest is moved, to actually pull groups up the hill (towards the southwest) and use the big rock at that spot for tanking and nuking. The one draw back of this approach is that there are two groups (group 9 and 17) that spawn at that position. However, the benefit (which strongly outweighs the disadvantage) is that the party can retreat at any time and disengage whenever they feel overwhelmed.
Defeating Mallyx
Anguished Soul Spirits
Four Anguished Soul spirits (6120 health in normal mode) reside behind Mallyx and are responsible for 4 environmental effects in the room (the same as seen across the Domain of Anguish):
Listless Soul causes Repressive Energy: lose 2 energy for each attack or use of a skill
Tormented Soul causes Enduring Torment: lose 10 health for every second of movement
Shrouded Soul causes Shroud of Darkness: all attacks have a 50% chance to miss
Demonic Soul causes Demonic Miasma: take 50 damage for every block, or dodge
Mallyx can revive the nearest dead Anguished Soul by casting Unyielding Anguish.
Mallyx's offense and defense
Mallyx himself uses particularly nasty monster skills:
Summoning Shadows: transports all his foes to him.
Shadow Smash: heavy spike that pushes any surviving foes away from him.
Consume Torment: purges all hexes and conditions and converts them into a strong source of healing.
Banish Enchantment: strips all enchantments from a foe and disables one skill for every party member for every enchantment removed.
Wild Smash: ends stances and disables them.
Unyielding Anguish: revives the nearest environmental spirit.
Huge aggro range. He will start rushing creatures from far away.
If Mallyx isn't hard enough to beat, reinforcements spawn whenever Mallyx's health drops below certain thresholds:
80% Health: 2 groups at the portals on either side of the door, each group includes two random "Anur" Margonites
50% Health: 2 groups of two random Torment Demons
General tips

Ritualists are especially effective because they do not have to depend on hexes or enchantments. Mallyx has no special defenses against Spirits or Weapon Spells. In particular, Displacement and Shelter are very potent in containing Mallyx since his only actual damage comes from his melee attacks and environment effects.
Anti-summon skills are useful: Holy Spear and Spiritual Pain do bonus damage to the Soul spirits; Gaze of Fury destroys them.
Never use enchantments unless you can shutdown his use of Banish Enchantment.
Bring alternatives to hexes, conditions, and enchantments: Wards, Wells, Shouts, Spirits, Weapon Spells, signets, and plain skills.
Mallyx's skills cannot be disabled; skills such as Blackout and Diversion are of no use.
Specific tactics
Mallyx's skills tend to prevent the use of the standard tactic of a frontline of tanks, a midline of ranged attackers/casters, and a backline of healers.

His Shadow Smash ability is always active and will often cause him to retarget different allies, making Tanking extremely difficult. Summoning Shadows similarly makes it difficult to keep out of his aggro range.
Kill the spirits to remove their environmental effects.
Other notes
Examine Mallyx's movement, should he run off: aimless movement means he will return shortly; no movement means he has lost aggro.
Sometimes you need to distract him by leaving 2 or 3 people inside the gate to get him to stay, instead of running off after he kills the puller.
After Mallyx uses Shadow Smash, party members need to kite in order to force him to re-establish aggro on the tank, if using a tank.

Once Mallyx is defeated, a Citadel Chest and Spirit of Truth will spawn. If your party wipes after Mallyx has been killed (or while he is degenerating to death, ie through Well of Suffering), they will not be resurrected to claim the chest. The quest will be considered complete.
Gaze of Fury may sometimes spawn the spirit but leave the Anguished Soul alive.
"Skipway"

If a party member goes through the portal leading to Mallyx's room right after killing the last group of enemies and all 8 party members skip the cut scene quickly, then the entire party can stay in the original room. One person can pull Mallyx back to the original room and the entire fight can take place there to make it significantly easier due to the lack of spawns attacking you & negative spirit effects.

quests/quest:gww:4631/sections/notes-1/b.text: When planning to complete this mission in hard mode, it can be a good idea to first obtain the quest Miniature Companion: The Domain of Anguish from Merrise, Sworn to Seas in Embark Beach. This quest rewards 2025 experience, 2006 gold and the Miniature Greased Lightning.

quests/quest:gww:25488/sections/objectiv.text: Escort Fadden Hathorn into the Devourer devourer cave and keep him safe while he gathers eggs.
Escort Fadden Hathorn back to Duke Gaban.
Return to Duke Gaban for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25488/sections/environm.text: Upon completing this quest, Duke Gaban and Fadden Hathorn will no longer spawn in Lakeside County. They can both be seen again post-Searing, Fadden in Sardelac Sanitarium and Duke Gaban in the Bonus Mission Pack.
Upon completing this quest, the Devourer Nests will no longer be interactive.

quests/quest:gww:25488/sections/walkthro.text: Exit Ascalon City, cross the river to the south, and head slightly uphill to locate Duke Gaban and Fadden Hathorn (hold Alt if you have trouble spotting them). Accept the quest and lead Fadden into the cave.

Fadden will flee from any living devourer, even though most are not hostile. To keep him moving, you must systematically clear the cave. The eight level 1 Carrion and Lash Devourers inside shouldn't pose much of a threat, especially if you pull them one by one.

One level 0 Diseased Devourer will unburrow at the second nest and attack you, and two more will strike at the third. This can trigger nearby devourers to attack as well. Focus down the level 0 ambushers first, as they drop after one or two basic attacks, which quickly brings down the incoming damage.

Once Fadden gathers all three eggs, escort him back to the Duke. Two Lash Devourers will spawn near the cave entrance while you are inside. If you haven't already, clear them out so Fadden can safely exit and you can claim your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25488/sections/notes-1/.text: Upon completing the quest, Duke Gaban will give you two devourer eggs. One can be used in the quest The Worm Problem and the other in The Rogue's Replacement. You can also get eggs by giving Brownlow five skale fins or trading with another player.

Two Hidden Stashes also spawn in the cave. On rare occasions, this might block Fadden's path. To get him to move, try pulling some foes nearby, which should cause him to flee. If that does not work, you will have to rezone and try again.

When you attack a devourer that is trapped behind a rock or egg, your attacks can be obstructed. Reposition yourself so that you can attack from a different angle (or bring skills that can do damage without a line-of-sight).

quests/quest:gww:25502/sections/objectiv.text: Use your Fire Storm spell to defeat the ice beasts that attack Aziure.
Return to Elementalist Aziure for your reward.
Aziure will give you the following skills upon taking the quest:

quests/quest:gww:25502/sections/walkthro.text: Upon accepting the quest, simply wait for the Ice Elemental Shards to spawn. They come periodically in three waves. Since the Ice Elemental Shards take double damage from fire, a single, well-placed Fire Storm will easily kill them even with 0 Fire Magic. Wait until they cluster around you or Aziure, cast the spell once they stop moving, and watch them melt.
Once the final wave is defeated, speak to Aziure to claim your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25502/sections/notes-1/.text: If Aziure is killed you cannot accept the reward for this quest, so kill the Ice Elemental Shards before they can kill her.

Some players may find it worthwhile to repeatedly do the quest for experience and drops, zoning back to Foible's Fair, abandoning the quest and going back to Aziure. However, the Ice Elemental Shards are level 1 (compared to the standard level 3 Ice Elementals) and do not drop Icy Lodestones.

quests/quest:gww:15336/sections/objectiv.text: Go to Prophet's Path and slay the kree minotaur.
Take the kree minotaur hide to Cembrien in Heroes' Audience.

quests/quest:gww:15336/sections/rewards-.text: Elementalist available as a secondary profession.

quests/quest:gww:15336/sections/walkthro.text: If you are a ranged character of some sort, this quest is easy. Go west from Augury Rock to the teleporter near the Kree Minotaur. If you attack the Kree Minotaur from the raised area, it will not be able to reach you, although it will frequently run out of range for a short time. Melee characters will have to make a small detour to the north to get to the lower area that the Kree Minotaur patrols, or use the teleporter to cross the valley and take a shorter detour south. Be sure to pick up the Kree Minotaur Hide before you map travel back to Heroes' Audience to get the reward.

quests/quest:gww:15336/sections/notes-1/.text: This is the only secondary profession quest to require delivering an item instead of just killing a boss.

The Quest Log will update when the Kree Minotaur is killed, instead of when the hide is picked up like in most item delivery quests. Cembrien will not accept a Kree Minotaur Hide that is acquired without killing the Kree Minotaur, but the hide is required to complete the quest.

quests/quest:gww:9628/sections/environme.text: Informant Tahzen will no longer spawn after this quest is completed.

quests/quest:gww:9628/sections/walkthrou.text: Head east in Kaineng Center to the Raisu Pavilion portal. Talk to the Emperor's Hand, and then map travel to the Marketplace. Exit into Wajjun Bazaar and follow the quest marker to Informant Tahzen. After speaking to him, return to Kaineng Center and speak to Guildmaster Luan for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25343/sections/objectiv.text: Clear the Temple of War of enemies!
Seek out the Forgemaster at the temple of War.
See Eternal Forgemaster for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25343/sections/walkthro.text: To spawn the Eternal Weaponsmith to get this quest, clear out the camp on the west side of the Great Battle Field.

The Temple sits atop the large hill in the center of the Fissure, and is guarded by some sizable groups of Shadow Army. It is possible to make them and nearby Skeleton Army groups aggro each other to weaken them. When the groups leading up to the Temple are dead, the gate will open. Inside are groups of Shadow Monks and Shadow Mesmers guarding the ramps to the central altar, with groups of Abyssals and Shadow Beasts patroling between them. Pull the first patrol to the door and away from the monks, then work your way around the Temple taking out one group at a time. Atop the central platform are Shadow Rangers and more Shadow Beasts. Clear these out and the Eternal Forgemaster will spawn with your reward.
Do not take the following quest until your party is ready.

quests/quest:gww:25343/sections/notes-1/.text: Despite the reward dialogue, you still need to do two more quests to craft Obsidian armor, Defend the Temple of War and Restore the Temple of War.
There are spots on the right side of each access ramp of the forge that allows non-tanking players to hide.
Both the north and south ramps provide such narrow access that they are easily body-blocked should the foes attempt to go round the barriers.
Clearing the Eternal Forge area before taking the quest, may sometimes result in the Forgemaster not spawning.

*BONUS* Complete the mission in Hard Mode.

quests/quest:gww:278910/sections/target-.text: Exit from Vasburg Armory or travel north from Amatz Basin via Mourning Veil Falls.
The Wardens and Mantis are hostile to each other. If you let them fight it out, it can save around 17 kills.
Take note that when approaching the seemingly solitary Flower Spiritgarden, at least 8 other Wardens will drop down from the trees behind it.
There are 4 hidden Oni groups (each consisting of 3 of them):
At the southern edge of the area directly south of Vasburg Armory.
Close to the western edge, in an underpass amidst several Warden groups.
A short distance southeast from the Eternal Grove outpost.
In the small lake near the southern edge.
Complete exploration of this area yields approximately 1.9% towards the Canthan Cartography title.

quests/quest:gww:25456/sections/objectiv.text: Bring the spirit essence to Mastersmith Rutger.

quests/quest:gww:25456/sections/walkthro.text: On receiving the quest from Scholar Andrej, a quest item called Spirit Essence will be added to your inventory. The spirit essence must be taken to Mastersmith Rutger, who can be found in the south-west corner of Ferndale, near the Dredge temple. Chat with Rutger to pass along the Spirit Essence quest item and collect your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25456/sections/notes-1/.text: You may wish to also have the quest Melodic Gaki Flute active while performing this quest since both quests take you to the same general area in Ferndale.
Despite what the quest reward dialogue says, Rutger will never craft weapons.

quests/quest:gww:280955/sections/objecti.text: Clear the Falls in the Maguuma Jungle of all enemies in hard mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:280955/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 250 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:280955/sections/instruc.text: "Clear the Falls in the Maguuma Jungle of all enemies in hard mode."

quests/quest:gww:14268/sections/objectiv.text: Defeat Abbot Ramoth and retrieve the Litanies of the Unseen.
Return the Litanies of the Unseen to Brother Mizar.

quests/quest:gww:14268/sections/walkthro.text: Exit the Temple of the Ages and follow the quest marker west to Abbot Ramoth and his retinue of White Mantle Justiciars. You may encounter some Bog Skale Blighters and will likely find some hidden Spined Aloes on the road, which should not be too hard to dispatch by themselves.

You must defeat Abbot Ramoth, whereupon he will drop the Litanies of the Unseen. Ramoth is a skilled protector monk, so engaging him together with his warrior guards may be challenging for an unprepared party, though the party size of 8 available from the Temple of the Ages is a boon. Fortunately, Ramoth can be separated from the Justiciars, and their wide wandering range should make it easy to pull them. If you do end up fighting all of them together, focus on the Abbot; the Justiciars are hardy even without his support, and they do not have to be killed to complete the quest.
Once Ramoth is dead, retrieve the Litanies of the Unseen and return to Brother Mizar for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:14268/sections/notes-1/.text: Abbot Ramoth and his Justiciars drop Leather Belts, which are otherwise unique to the much more challenging Cult of Verata and Galrath's Bandits, instead of the usual White Mantle Emblems and Badges.

quests/quest:gww:25369/sections/objectiv.text: Help Ennis Granitestrider complete his mission inside Sorrow's Furnace.

quests/quest:gww:25369/sections/walkthro.text: This should be a walk in the park by now, since you had to travel to Sorrow's Furnace several times already for the preceding quest To Sorrow's Furnace. Talk to Ennis Granitestrider, who will be waiting patiently on the right when you exit Deldrimor War Camp in the Southern Shiverpeaks. Kill some patrols and just walk into the exit to Sorrow's Furnace.
Here you will receive the quest The Forge Heart. To get past the gates, use the explosives given by Budger Blackpowder.

After completing the quest, walk back to Ennis Granitestrider just inside the entrance gate if necessary to accept the reward. Do not leave the instance until after accepting the reward for The Forge Heart, since if you exit prematurely then The Forge Heart quest is removed from your quest log and you will have to repeat it.
Once The Forge Heart is complete, you can leave and turn in The Final Assault with the Dwarven Prospector.

quests/quest:gww:25369/sections/notes-1/.text: This quest sets up the spawns for The Forge Heart, including the Iron Forgeman, whose attack is required to hatch a Black Moa Chick once the player has acquired and filled an Incubator Kit.
Completion of this quest unlocks the Eternal Conqueror of Sorrow's Furnace statue in the Hall of Monuments.

Sometimes Ennis stops following you on the path to Sorrow's Furnace. Once inside, he will not appear and you have to come back to the starting point. To prevent this, click and talk to Ennis just before entering to ensure he is following.

quests/quest:gww:295333/sections/objecti.text: See Initiate Zei Ri for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:295333/sections/rewards.text: Initiate Zei Ri joins your party. 1
1 - This reward is not listed in the quest log.

quests/quest:gww:295333/sections/shared-.text: Miku stands south of the entrance to Tahnnakai Temple outpost. After initial dialogue, she will take you to the garden where Reiko walks with Ashu, which is the explorable vesion of Shing Jea Arena. After a brief dialogue, Reiko will become hostile. During the fight, she will use three special skills:
Grand Illusion, which creates a vortex of phantoms; its strength is indicated by a purple bar on the screen.
Mirror Echo, which creates images of herself.
Mirror of Darkness, which creates copies of party members and allies; these will have exactly the same skill bar as their parent (including any PvE skills of player characters).

Your goal is to reduce the Grand Illusion bar to zero strength by attacking the real Reiko. During the confrontation, you will be aided by various allies from previous quests while members of the Ministry of Purity will come to her defense.

You can use any team here that successfully met any of the previous challenges. As long as you can keep the party alive, you will outlast Reiko in a war of attrition. Keep spread out, concentrate on one target at a time, and deal with the ministry foes as they come along.
Hex Eater Vortex is used frequently by Reiko (and the many "false images" of herself) to strip enchantments and deal massive AoE damage.

Conditions are effective. Extend Conditions and Plague Signet can be spammed to spread and manage conditions, such as Burning, Cracked Armor, and Deep Wound; the latter of which triggers Miku's Venom Fang.
All phantoms and clones are summoned creatures:

Swap can be used to identify the true Reiko. If she is selected, the skill will report her as an invalid target. Use Swap then immediately cancel so it doesn't cast. You will get the notification whether or not you successfully cast it if it is the real Reiko.
Anti-summon skills are effective. Holy Spear, Spiritual Pain and Consume Soul can be spammed to deliver strong AoE damage, since the false images tend to ball up.
Mantra of Resolve and Power Drain on most, if not all, casters. Power Drain serves as both an interrupt and energy management (to counter the penalty from the stance).
There is an opportunity to map the area before and after the dialogue, which permits access to Shing Jea Arena that would normally be accessible during PvP.
Elite Ministry Captains and Elite Ministry Zealots have their name swapped during this quest.

quests/quest:gww:277211/sections/objecti.text: Clear the Floodplain of Mahnkelon in Kourna of all enemies in hard mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:277211/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 150 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:277211/sections/instruc.text: "Clear the Floodplain of Mahnkelon in Kourna of all enemies in hard mode."

quests/quest:gww:24082/sections/objectiv.text: Settle Zudash's debt with the corsairs.
See Zudash Dejarin for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:24082/sections/walkthro.text: First talk to Zudash Dejarin in Yohlon Haven. Then make the long trek across the Arkjok Ward through Pogahn Passage across the Dejarin Estate to Camp Hojanu and then finally to the Barbarous Shore. Find Ruthless Sevad with a group of corsairs in the Barbarous Shore. After talking to him, the corsairs will become hostile. Defeat them, and return to Zudash to collect your reward.

quests/quest:gww:24082/sections/notes-1/.text: It may be wise to speak with the Wandering Priest at the Resurrection Shrine just behind Sevad's group to obtain a bounty on Corsairs. Sevad's Boys count towards this bounty and will earn you additional Sunspear points.
This quest fits right in with A Fool's Luck since both have you talk with Ruthless Sevad.
Lieutenant Shagu will not appear while this quest is active.

quests/quest:gww:25354/sections/objectiv.text: Destroy all three of the Rage Binders controlling the Iron Forgeman at the same time.
See Ennis Granitestrider for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25354/sections/walkthro.text: After talking to Ennis Granitestrider inside Sorrow's Furnace, Budger Blackpowder will accompany you. He will provide you with explosive Dwarven Powder Kegs, which will be used to blow up sealed doors inside this area (master gears won't work on the doors -- only on the bridge). Budger Blackpowder cannot die, and will not help out in battle. He does tend to stand in the middle of skirmishes, getting in your way, though. If you find he's gone missing, he may be stuck behind the crushing traps; run back and he should begin to follow you again when you're back within range.

You start at the upper left corner of the map, and your objective is to reach the lower right-hand corner. Most of the enemies you encounter along the way are not difficult to kill. Towards the end of the journey, there will be a few groups of enemies together — pull small groups to avoid getting the attention of all of them at once.

You'll find The Iron Forgeman in a walled area surrounded by a number of guards. There are three Rage Binders accompanied by two Furnace Guardians, and one roaming Stone Summit patrol. In addition, while you are inside the walled area, The Iron Forgeman will dump lava on your group and hit you with a wrecking ball if you are stationary.
The easiest method is to take your time, and eliminate each group of Furnace Guardians first, and then the patrol.

There will be three Rage Binders left. When you kill one, it will respawn in about 30-45 seconds. You have to kill all three of them in a short amount of time. With a group of human players, this is fairly easy since you can split up into two teams. With heroes/henchmen only, it will be harder. You may have to race around the circle killing them as fast as you can. A speed boost can be handy, as can interrupt for the Life Siphon that the Rage Binders use.
Don't kill the first one with slow-recharging skills, since there is no hurry killing the first. Your skills can better serve defeating the second.
It may be possible to damage one of the Rage Binders, and then move on to the second. In this way, the first will be killed faster when you come back to it.
Experienced players with heroes/henchmen can flag your heroes around one Rage Binder to keep it killed, while you and the henchmen kill the other 2 Rage Binders.

Alternatively, if using a full party of heroes, you can kill the middle Rage Binder first then flag half of your heroes to one of the remaining Rage Binders and accompany half to the other, if your builds are good enough they should easily kill both in time.
When you have killed all three you will get to see a cut-scene.

There will now be three Flame Djinn in the circle. You most certainly don't want to aggro all of them at the same time, so get back out of the circle quickly to regenerate. Pull one of them at a time outside the circle and interrupt the Consuming Flames skill to kill it faster. Even with a large Death Penalty it shouldn't be too big of a problem to kill one of them.
Pain Inverter is highly effective if used when the Flame Djinn is using Consuming Flames resulting in it losing almost half of its health if 5 party members are next to it.

If there are two Djinn stuck together, keep trying to pull one of them away from the other one. There's a resurrection shrine nearby, so you have all the time in the world. Some parties can probably kill two djinn at the same time, but with a large death penalty it will not work. But even with a full death penalty, a minion master can mitigate a large amount of damage from the djinns.
Now that you've killed all three djinn, talk to Ennis Granitestrider to complete the quest.

quests/quest:gww:25354/sections/notes-1/.text: This quest is only available if the party enters Sorrow's Furnace while accompanied by Budger Blackpowder and Ennis Granitestrider, who will only follow players who have completed To Sorrow's Furnace. This means that a party member who has completed To Sorrow's Furnace and The Final Assault at least once, can make this quest available for other party members who have not.
As with other quests in elite areas, you must claim your quest reward before exiting Sorrow's Furnace.

quests/quest:gww:25352/sections/objectiv.text: Seek out Sariss Yassith in Skyward Reach.

quests/quest:gww:25352/sections/walkthro.text: After obtaining the quest from Annelle Fipps in Destiny's Gorge, you can take one of two paths. You can take the northern exit at Destiny's Gorge and travel south through Skyward Reach. After a while, you will arrive at a teleporter which you will need to activate to continue south and then west where you will find Sariss Yassith. Alternatively you can map travel to Augury Rock, take the northern exit and travel south through Skyward Reach and then east to Sariss Yassith. The alternate route is a bit shorter, but takes you past a few groups of Hydra. Once you arrive at Sariss' location, simply speak to him to receive your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25537/sections/objectiv.text: Fight your way through the entrance chambers to gain entry to the foundry.
Clear the first chamber of enemies.
Clear the second chamber of enemies.
Clear the third chamber of enemies.
Clear the fourth chamber of enemies.

quests/quest:gww:25537/sections/walkthro.text: Clear the four chambers leading to the foundry. After all party members step past the tentacles to enter a chamber, the tentacles will close behind them and the party will be locked inside; this also triggers the initial spawn of foes. The tentacles will not open again until all the monsters in the chamber have been destroyed. In three of the four chambers, additional group(s) spawn after the first group is killed.
Chamber 1: The first group are Margonites; when they are destroyed, they spawn a group of two Despair Titans and two Rage Titans.

Chamber 2: This chamber can be difficult to fight in because its size leaves no room to maneuver. The initial group consists of Margonite Anur mixed with Tortureweb Dryders. After these are destroyed, the new spawns include Tortureweb Dryders mixed with Greater Dream Riders.

Chamber 3: This room has only a single spawn, but it includes four patrols: four Anguish Titans; four Rage Titans; four Misery Titans; and three Tortureweb Dryders with a single Greater Dream Rider. When the titans die, they will spawn lesser titans (Anguish → Despair → Fury; Misery → Rage → Dementia). Each patrol covers the full perimeter of the room, so it is very difficult to pull just a single group unless you stand in the far corner and are very careful. Positioning is extremely important in this room, both to avoid over-aggro, and to minimize the harm from powerful AoE spells. Once the initial enemies are dead, the door to the next room will open.

Chamber 4: This chamber has four successive spawns: Tortureweb Dryders mixed with a Margonite Anur Ki, followed by about 18 Dementia Titans, a mixed group of Despair, Rage, and Dementia Titans, and finally a group with a Greater Dream Rider, a Margonite Anur Ki, a Tortureweb Dryder, a Despair Titan, two regular Fury Titans, and one special Fury Titan (noticeably larger than the rest) which can drop a unique item. When the Despair Titan dies, it spawns two more regular Fury Titans which do not need to be killed to open the door to the Foundry.
After clearing the final chamber, players may advance to the Foundry; Tekliss will be just past the entrance.

quests/quest:gww:25537/sections/notes-1/.text: If you clear the first room before taking the quest and then take the quest the wall will appear again and cannot be removed. This will trap whoever took the quest and anybody else still behind the wall.

quests/quest:gww:25518/sections/requirem.text: Must have Restoring Grenth's Monuments quest active

quests/quest:gww:25518/sections/objectiv.text: Return to Reaper of the Chaos Planes for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25518/sections/walkthro.text: After accepting this quest, the four horsemen begin their approach toward the Reaper from the middle section of the Chaos Planes. The horsemen, accompanied by several Terrorweb Dryders, split into two groups approaching from separate sides. The groups will attempt to eliminate the Reaper, returning the party to the outpost from which they entered the Underworld.
This quest is arguably the most difficult in the underworld, requiring a good strategy to survive.
Spread out around the Reaper and make your stand there. Keep your distance to each other and to the Reaper to mitigate the Dryders' AoE spells - flag your heroes if you brought any.

Your healers' priority should be to keep the Reaper alive. Everyone else must focus on dispatching or disabling the incoming foes. With a sufficiently strong party, you will outlast the waves, completing the quest.
This works well in normal mode and can be done with a 7-hero-team. In hard mode, more elaborate strategies are needed.
Use one or two party members to delay one side while everyone else kills the other.

This strategy needs a dedicated tank to draw aggro and block the foes on one side. A tank with permanent spell targeting prevention should be able to do it alone, otherwise help from a healer may be needed. The tank will last longer with knockdown prevention, Mantra of Flame and anything that boosts armor. The healer must be very careful not to draw aggro, keeping out of range, only approaching the tank when needed.

When the tank is ready, the other party members can accept the quest and intercept all spawns from the other side. Running as far as possible towards the spawns results in earlier kills, reducing the time your tank needs to hold out. On the other hand, staying closer to the reaper allows you to take measures should the tank fall.

quests/quest:gww:203910/sections/objecti.text: Kill the four horsemen; Madruk Dhuum, Thul Za Dhuum, Ghozer Dhuum, Kazhad Dhuum in the Underworld.
*BONUS* Kill the four horsemen in Hard Mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:203910/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 60 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the *BONUS* Objective for an additional 150 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:203910/sections/walkthr.text: As per the The Four Horsemen quest.

quests/quest:gww:205613/sections/objecti.text: Open the Frost Gate in the Northern Shiverpeaks.
*BONUS* Secure the secret siege weapon plans.
*BONUS* Complete the mission in Hard Mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:205613/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 15 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the first *BONUS* Objective for an additional 22 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the second *BONUS* Objective for an additional 37 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:205613/sections/walkthr.text: As per The Frost Gate mission.

quests/quest:gww:284028/sections/objecti.text: Defeat Ganshu the Scribe, and obtain the Jade Brotherhood Text.
See Xan Hei for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:284028/sections/shared-.text: Leave from The Marketplace and head west, fighting through several large groups of Jade Brotherhood. You will receive many allies in the form of members of the Ministry of Purity as well as some regular Canthan Peasants. The Peasants are not very useful, but provide excellent fodder for minion masters. Upon reaching Ganshu the Scribe, his group and one more behind him will initially be friendly; after some brief dialogue they will turn hostile. Defeat Ganshu and pick up the Jade Brotherhood Text to complete the quest.

Alternatively, leave from Nahpui Quarter and head north. This route takes a few more minutes, but it is safer. There will be some regular Am Fah mobs and Mantids along the way, but nothing dangerous. Once you reach the island stronghold, a large brawl will already be going on between some Peasants and Ministry forces; you can either try to save some by rushing in head first, or forget about them and play it safe, pulling the Jade groups apart for easier killing. After this, proceed to Ganshu as normal.

Another option using a party with strong spiking skills and speed boosts is to run west from The Marketplace, ignoring the enemies along the way until you reach the westernmost bridge from the main landmass to the island containing the Jade Brotherhood guild hall. Using this bridge, run north and west past two packs of enemies until you reach a small courtyard with a central dais within compass range just south of Ganshu. Prepare, flag heroes (possibly locking targets for shutdown), precast spirits and protective spells as necessary and then spike down Ganshu. Pick up the text when Ganshu dies and you may freely resign or map out. These tactics work even with small party sizes (where they benefit greatly from accompanying summoned allies).

It is also worth noting that Ganshu does not pull with either of the packs to his immediate west and south. If you lack the means to fight him with his allies, you can pull the west pack first and then pull Ganshu independently for an easy kill.

quests/quest:gww:25242/sections/objectiv.text: Activate all 3 earth shrines by placing Scorched Lodestones upon them.
Return to Kendrick Redstaff for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25242/sections/walkthro.text: If you already have 3 Scorched Lodestones from The Way of the Geomancer or random encounters, skip this paragraph. The area outside of Serenity Temple is brimming with Stone Elementals and Hulking Stone Elementals. Spend some time in the area until you receive the necessary 3 Scorched Lodestones.

Now, travel through the Pockmark Flats to the earth shrines. Be careful of stone elemental patrols, there are a lot of patrols and they seem to converge at the earth shrines. Each earth shrine will look like a stone with an inscription and a bowl on the top. When a Scorched Lodestone is placed in each shrine a yellow sphere will glow above the shrine.

Each earth shrine can be found in relation to the massive crater in the northern part of the Pockmark Flats. The first earth shrine is north of the crater, the second shrine is to the west of the crater, and the third shrine is south of the crater.

After all three shrines have a Scorched Lodestone placed within them the Stone Golem will appear to the southeast of the crater. The Stone Golem spawns by itself, but there are several earth elemental patrols around its position. Stone Golem can be seen from the southern earth shrine.

quests/quest:gww:25242/sections/notes-1/.text: This quest removes a lot of non-elemental foes from the area (primarily the ones that would normally spawn north of the "Pockmark Flats" text label in the World Map), which may or may not make it easier to vanquish.
If you have activated the three shrines and leave the instance, the quest will reset and you will have to start again (and find three more Scorched Lodestones).

quests/quest:gww:63592/sections/objectiv.text: Drink from each of the two ale barrels to get drunk
Move three kegs of ale from the pile to the keg stand
Drink from each of the two ale barrels
Run the slalom. You must pass each flag on the far side or you will be disqualified
Drink from each of the two ale barrels
Herd three pigs into one of the pens
See Olaf Olafson for your reward. (Female quest only)
See Olrun Olafdottir for your reward. (Male quest only)

quests/quest:gww:63592/sections/walkthro.text: You will not have to fight anything, so concentrate your skillbar on moving quickly; aim for a permanent IMS of 33% or more. To start the quest, speak to Sif Shadowhunter who will start the timer. The quest indicator on your compass will help you find your next goal.
Drink from both barrels next to Sif.
Run to the Keg of Ale stack, pick up one, and carry it to the Keg Stand.
Return to the barrels; drink from both again.
Run the slalom by following a zigzag path around the outside of the markers.
Make sure the quest updates as you pass each marker.
Avoid the inner side of the flags; you can get disqualified even if you had passed them earlier from the far side.
Return to the barrels and drink from both one last time.
Follow the quest markers to the pen and push 3 piggies into the pen by bodyblocking them from the opposite direction.
You can speed things up by moving some pigs closer to the pen before starting the challenge.

If you are lucky, you can even herd three pigs into the stable and collect the reward without talking to Sif, allowing you to collect the reward without triggering the timer. However, the pigs are not at all cooperative.
You can bring spirits to help guide the pigs, but that is not guaranteed to work.
Some players have had success by repeatedly rezoning until the pigs are either in or very close to the stable before attempting to herd them.

quests/quest:gww:63592/sections/notes-1/.text: You do not need to touch the Keg Stand; once you bring the keg bundles close enough; they will drop automatically.
The slalom zig-zag path is unforgiving, so give each flag a wide berth (around 5 to 10 steps) as you pass around its far side. Start at the bottom of the hill and head towards the stable.
You must run exactly between the flags, otherwise you fail the quest.
Drunkenness from these kegs does not count towards drunkard title.
Disabling post-process effects makes it easier to navigate, since the display will not wobble.

You can explore past the closed doorways at the various map exits and reveal otherwise unreachable areas. However, you will encounter the usual foes outside the alemoot; bring running skills and/or spirits to use as decoys.
There is a locked chest to the south, in the area where Nulfastu Earthbound normally spawns.

You may postpone the quest reward by map travel from this solo instance to one of outposts and then receive it from corresponding NPC in their usual location. This allows to add to the party other heroes (in particular, below level 20) who will get experience as well.
For various reasons, the quest can be completed without finishing all the activities:

You automatically succeed once three pigs enter the stables. You can use this to your advantage, by body-blocking the pigs into the pen before starting the timer. It takes longer, as the hogs are harder to control, but you have all the time you need this way. Also:
Sometimes three will reach the corral on their own.
Sometimes the game server registers three pigs entering, although you see something different on-screen.
If you have completed up to the slalom, you can retake the challenge and succeed by heading straight for the pigs, who will now be easier to herd.
If you apply an Extreme Makeover Credit to change gender after taking the quest, but before completion, you will have to finish it an extra time before you can proceed to the subsequent quests.
You can see the edge of the world by running into the next zone.
As with any time-dependent tasks, you can fail this quest due to lag. Consider waiting until your ping is low.
Interactive objects
Barrel
Keg of Ale
Keg Stand

quests/quest:gww:213796/sections/objecti.text: Scout the enemy territory north of the Great Northern Wall and assess the strength of the Charr army.
*BONUS* Find and return the four pieces of Kilnn Testibrie's armor to his tomb.
*BONUS* Complete the mission in Hard Mode.

quests/quest:gww:213796/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 15 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:213796/sections/walkthr.text: As per The Great Northern Wall mission.

quests/quest:gww:33051/sections/requirem.text: The Great Zehtuka will only offer this quest after all the Aggressive Lions and Lionesses surrounding him are dead (although you can charm one to become a pet).

quests/quest:gww:33051/sections/objectiv.text: Travel around Jahai Bluffs and visit landmarks commemorating the valiant deeds of the Great Zehtuka.
See the Great Zehtuka for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:33051/sections/walkthro.text: This is basically a tour following Zehtuka around to various points in Jahai Bluffs listening to him blow his own horn about how great a hunter he is. The only possible trouble is the wandering groups of wildlife. You can time your party's movement to avoid many of them.

quests/quest:gww:33051/sections/notes-1/.text: Zehtuka will not wait for your group to keep up, and will travel past the edge of the small square map (at standard size). The best way to catch up with him is keeping this quest active, and follow the stars and/or arrows.

quests/quest:gww:202700/sections/objecti.text: Kill the Greater Darkness in Ravenheart Gloom.
*BONUS* Kill The Unlike the previous objective, 'The' is capitalized here Greater Darkness in Hard Mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:202700/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 60 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the *BONUS* Objective for an additional 150 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:202700/sections/walkthr.text: After completing the repeatable quests To the Rescue!, The Rifts Between Us and Deathbringer Company in Ravenheart Gloom, the Greater Darkness will spawn along with two of the Darknesses. They're easy to kill, but will spawn additional foes on death.
Killing or even surviving the additional foes is not required for this quest, but will progress the quest Mallyx the Unyielding and spawn a reward chest.

quests/quest:gww:25481/sections/objectiv.text: Meet Jehner in the Poisoned Outcrops.
Destroy the soul-eating Margonites. You have X of 5 groups remaining.

quests/quest:gww:25481/sections/walkthro.text: Just follow the markers and kill the Margonite groups. Some groups might be killed for you by the roaming Djinns and Awakened.

quests/quest:gww:25481/sections/notes-1/.text: Jehner and several Freed Souls will join you as allies on this quest. Although quest completion does not require their survival, if you keep Jehner alive, you can avoid the need to return to The Ruptured Heart to claim the reward.

Jehner and the Freed Souls will stop following your party when the quest is completed. If you are using them as meat shields or general allies in a vanquish, it may be advantageous to save one group of Margonite Souleaters for last.
The Margonite Souleaters are hostile to both normal Margonites and the Awakened.

As the Souleaters spawn when you zone into the instance, it is possible to start from Lair of the Forgotten and backtrack to kill the groups without talking to Jehner, effectively making the quest shorter as you don't need to walk from the quest start location to Poisoned Outcrops as well as guaranteeing his survival making claiming the reward easier.

quests/quest:gww:16893/sections/objectiv.text: Speak to Captain Rion of the Halcyon.
See Captain Lexis for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:16893/sections/walkthro.text: [Incomplete source section] Enter Boreas Seabed from Zos Shivros Channel. Go north after speaking to Rion. Most mobs can be avoided. There are popup Oni in a few places. Then head east over the bridge. On the way to Lord Senkai, you will encounter hostile level 10 Canthan Peasants and Canthan Nobles who will turn friendly when reached. Near them you will encounter level 20 Luxon Assassin popups. Head towards Lord Senkai and kill him. This will cause a wave of level 20 Kurzick and Luxon including War Captain Womack and multiple Monks. Killing War Captain Womack completes the quest.

quests/quest:gww:16893/sections/notes-1/.text: Despite his unique name, War Captain Womack is not a boss; however, his death will give a morale boost.
Despite their ongoing conflict, the Luxon and Kurzick will not attack each other.
This quest can be used for farming Bo Staves, Dragon Staves, and many other rare items. Players may choose not to complete this quest in order to use it for farming instead.

quests/quest:gww:25630/sections/objectiv.text: Carry the Staff of the Mists to the Hallowed Point.
Throw the Staff of the Mists into the Hallowed Point.

quests/quest:gww:25630/sections/walkthro.text: Carry the Staff of the Mists northwest to the Hallowed Point. You will encounter additional spawns of Margonites along the way. When the quest log asks the player to "throw" the staff, click on the Hallowed Point. Return to Buuran for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25630/sections/notes-1/.text: Be sure to accept the quest before taking the Staff of the Mists to the Hallowed Point, since clicking on the Hallowed Point will make the staff disappear - requiring you to rezone to start the quest again.
Combines well with Forgotten Retribution, since there are plenty of Margonites along the quest route.

quests/quest:gww:4989/sections/objective.text: Lead Gardener Pohsin safely to the Hanging Gardens of Jahin.
See Gardener Pohsin for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:4989/sections/environme.text: Once this quest is completed, Gardener Pohsin will no longer spawn in Vehtendi Valley.

quests/quest:gww:4989/sections/walkthrou.text: This is a routine escort type quest, simply ensure that the NPC Pohsin stays alive while you take her across Ventendi Valley (point 1 to point 2 on the map). Creatures you're likely to encounter are Kournan soldiers (usually with a margonite), heket and some plant type mobs. The initial quest objective can be approached from either Yahnur Market or the Kodash Bazaar.

quests/quest:gww:4989/sections/notes-1/b.text: This quest can easily be picked up while performing The Role of a Lifetime quest for Norgu, and completed afterwards before leaving Vehtendi Valley.
If Pohsin dies, then the quest fails. You will have to return to an outpost, then return back to the starting point to accompany Pohsin again.
There are many NPCs for Pohsin to get caught on.

quests/quest:gww:320070/sections/walkthr.text: Speak with Devona in Lion's Arch to receive the quest, then again to complete it.

quests/quest:gww:320070/sections/notes-1.text: This quest is available even to characters that have already unlocked Devona as a hero through completion of The Scourge Beneath in pre-Searing Ascalon.

quests/quest:gww:38768/sections/requirem.text: Must have changed secondary profession at least once to another profession (see Notes), either
via a profession changer and a manual change via the Skills and Attributes Panel to first the original secondary profession and then the newly acquired one again, or
by completing one of the following "'s Path" quests:

quests/quest:gww:38768/sections/objectiv.text: Enter the Frozen Forest from Iron Mines of Moladune.1
Return to Vanyi for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:38768/sections/walkthro.text: Enter the Frozen Forest either from Iron Mines of Moladune or Copperhammer Mines and meet Sanyi who will be standing in front of Copperhammer Mines outpost. Follow her while killing Mragga Spawns and finally defeat her. Return to Vanyi.

quests/quest:gww:38768/sections/notes-1/.text: Despite the initial dialogue and the quest objective, it is possible to complete the quest by starting from Copperhammer Mines, which is closer to Sanyi.
It is not necessary to change secondary profession as long as any of the "'s Path" quests have been completed.

If you haven't completed any of the "'s Path" quests, you will need to change from your initial secondary profession to another one once via the Skills and Attributes Panel. Change of secondary from profession changers do not seem to count.
Sometimes Sanyi will get stuck behind the tree stump right before the Stone Summit after crossing the bridge. Talk to her and she will move.

quests/quest:gww:14273/sections/objectiv.text: Return to Vanyi for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:14273/sections/walkthro.text: Map travel back to each of the three outposts in the Crystal Desert, or run to them from Augury Rock if necessary. Once all three have been visited, return to Droknar's Forge and claim the reward from Vanyi.

quests/quest:gww:14273/sections/notes-1/.text: The quest is intended to lead players to the new quests available in the three listed outposts, which unlock the ability to change your secondary profession. Completing those quests is not required to claim the reward for this quest, but will unlock Vanyi's attribute point quest, The Hero's Challenge.
If a character has already visited the outposts and changed professions before talking to Vanyi, it is possible to acquire both quests at the same time.
Having visited those locations previously will not fulfill the objectives, but allows you to do so by simple map travel.
The reward dialogue is the same even if you have completed one of the profession quests and learned how to change your secondary profession.

quests/quest:gww:25492/sections/objectiv.text: Go to Bergen Hot Springs and obtain a written testimony from Andar D'Leod.
Go to Bergen Hot Springs and obtain a written testimony from Dannel Smythe.
Go to Bergen Hot Springs and obtain a written testimony from Penelope Randell.
Go to Bergen Hot Springs and obtain a written testimony from Layman Josef.
Return the written testimonies to Inspector Caleb in Nebo Village.

quests/quest:gww:25492/sections/walkthro.text: To complete the quest, simply follow the quest marker to the outpost Bergen Hot Springs and speak with each witness. Return the testimonies to Inspector Caleb in Nebo Village, then speak with Inquisitor Gilead to receive the reward.

quests/quest:gww:25492/sections/notes-1/.text: Following the quest Mustering a Response, Nebo Village will be cleared of its residents, causing the player to be unable to complete the quest until The War in Kryta is further completed.

quests/quest:gww:25342/sections/objectiv.text: Destroy the Shard Wolves. 7..0 Shard Wolves remain.
Return to Nimros the Hunter for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25342/sections/walkthro.text: When the quest is taken, the seven Shard Wolves will spawn scattered about the Fissure. There will be a Shard Wolf in each of the major areas surrounding the Temple, with the exception of the Lake of Fire. The Shard Wolves can be killed in conjunction with exploring or doing other quests in the Fissure. When the last Shard Wolf is dead, return to Nimros the Hunter for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25342/sections/notes-1/.text: Ensure that all players take the quest before killing the first wolf, or else they can lose the 10,000 xp quest reward (however, they will still get credit for completing The Hunt as one of the eleven mission objectives).
Some players find it easier to start and complete the quest after the area is cleared of foes.
When six wolves have been killed, the quest log reads, "Destroy the Shard Wolves. 1 Shard Wolve remain".

quests/quest:gww:23073/sections/objectiv.text: Purify the hunter's horn in the healing spring in Regent Valley.
Go to the fishing village south of the tower in Wizard's Folly and deliver the purified horn to Aidan.

quests/quest:gww:23073/sections/walkthro.text: After receiving the quest from Chantalle head southeast towards Regent Valley. Once you travel through the portal into Regent Valley start heading south towards the healing spring. This quest has a lot of running across long distances, so make sure your character will survive the journey. At the Healing Spring there are River Skale, Black Bears, Wolves, and all around are Grawl, so when doing the quest make sure you take your time and kill everybody on the way.
Once the area is safe, interact with the Healing Spring with the Hunter's Horn in your inventory. The item icon will brighten, signaling it has become purified.

Follow your updated quest marker west to the entrance to Wizard's Folly. There, travel west along the river until you come to a fishing village, then go south and loop east, where you will find Aidan. Talk to him and get your reward.

quests/quest:gww:23073/sections/notes-1/.text: The spot you purify the horn is close to the area where you are asked to charm an animal during the quest The Ranger's Companion from Master Ranger Nente.

If your character is either a primary or secondary Ranger, you might consider going on to Ivor Trueshot and completing his quest before purifying the horn. You can then go to Aidan with the purified horn, and complete his Ranger quest as well while you are there.

quests/quest:gww:67244/sections/objectiv.text: See Captain Langmar for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:67244/sections/walkthro.text: Enter through the nearby portal into Rragar's Menagerie located in Sacnoth Valley South-West corner. You do not need the quest Veiled Threat that is otherwise needed for the dungeon, as the foes are found in the first room. Pick up the blessing from the Beacon of Droknar and go straight ahead to the mob that you can clearly see with the two melee bosses in. It is a good idea to take out the Flameshielders first as they deal the most damage here. After you have killed the small mob, map travel to Longeye's Ledge and exit into Grothmar Wardowns and speak to Captain Langmar for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:66777/sections/objectiv.text: Defeat the Charr warbands and discover the location of Rend Ragemauler.
See Captain Langmar for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:66777/sections/walkthro.text: Exit from Doomlore Shrine and head south to find Anton (The first marker on the quest map).

The quest updates points that will lead you into the big open field near Molotov Rocktail -- stay on the edge of the clearing if you want to avoid an encounter. Keep in mind that you can activate the resurrection shrines along the way.

In each Charr group there is a Prophet and a Charr Flameshielder. Thus, the easiest way to do this quest, with heroes and henchmen only, is to start from Doomlore Shrine and get control of the Siege Devourer stationed outside the outpost.
After finishing off the fourth group of Charr, map travel to Longeye's Ledge and head outside to speak with Captain Langmar for your reward!

quests/quest:gww:66777/sections/notes-1/.text: Killing the four Charr mobs will complete this quest. You do not need to meet Anton.

quests/quest:gww:25462/sections/objectiv.text: Meet Zenos and the rest of the crew in Gyala Hatchery.
See Po Fang for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25462/sections/walkthro.text: Start from the Leviathan Pits and head north into Gyala Hatchery where Zenos and the crew and waiting just outside. Unfortunately, Zenos can't fulfil any of the crew's requests or requirements before they'll join him, so it's just Zenos and the party going on the monster hunt!
From here, follow your quest pointer to the far north of Gyala Hatchery to find and slay the Impossible Sea Monster.
After slaying the monster, map to Kaineng Center and see Po Fang for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25462/sections/notes-1/.text: It does not matter if Zenos dies before you get to the Impossible Sea Monster, since once you kill it the quest will finish anyway and you will be able to get your reward from Po Fang.
There is no accept/decline dialogue, since this quest is automatically added to your quest log when you receive the preceding quest reward.
This also applies if you abandon this quest after receiving it; it is immediately re-added to your quest log without any dialogue if you talk to Delphinus.
If Zenos dies before the initial dialogue finishes, the quest freezes and you have to rezone to continue.

There is an intermediate dialogue that most players miss, after you have killed the monster with Zenos still alive. The problem is that, as a low level NPC, Zenos almost always dies before you get even close to the monster. One way around this, literally, is to enter Gyala Hatchery from Rhea's Crater and then kill all the enemies between Zenos and the The Impossible Sea Monster, being careful to not kill the monster itself or getting too close to Zenos so he won't follow you. Once everyone is dead, go get Zenos and bring him to the monster - after killing it, you'll see the last intermediate dialogue.
You may also keep Zenos alive by using Heroes/Henchmen and just have them flagged to fight enemies while you stay back with Zenos.

quests/quest:gww:204375/sections/objecti.text: Kill the Iron Forgeman in the Forge Heart.
*BONUS* Kill The Unlike the previous objective, 'The' is capitalized here Iron Forgeman in Hard Mode.
See Zehnchu [Zaishen Challenge] for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:204375/sections/rewards.text: Complete the Base Objective for 30 Zaishen Copper Coins.
Complete the *BONUS* Objective for an additional 75 Zaishen Copper Coins.

quests/quest:gww:3199/sections/objective.text: Enter the arena and defeat all of the other combatants.
See Arena Master Portus for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:3199/sections/walkthrou.text: Starting from Breaker Hollow, walk south along the west wall onto a small hill and locate Arena Master Portus (point P on the map). There is usually a wandering group near the small hill consisting of one to two Creeping Carps, an Irukandji, and Scuttle Fish as well as a group of three to four Oni that will spawn at the top of the small hill just before meeting with Portus.
2 Warriors, 2 Monks, 1 Necromancer, 2 Assassins, 1 Ritualist, no monsters.
1 Irukandji, 1 Warrior, 1 Ranger, 2 Monks, 1 Necromancer, 1 Mesmer, 1 Elementalist.
1 Jade Torn Kirin, 2 Rangers, 2 Monks, 2 Mesmers, 1 Elementalist.

quests/quest:gww:3199/sections/notes-1/b.text: The professions of the criminals can be identified by their appearance.
The combatants turn hostile when they enter your aggro circle or when Portus reaches them.
The Criminals carry resurrection signets. Bringing a skill such as Frozen Soil will help.
This quest can be used to farm Luxon faction, cash, and experience for Survivor.
It works better if the alliance's battles map favor Kurzicks.
This run can be completed in 3-4 minutes with a meta hero team.

An efficient team can complete the quest in under three minutes (including travel time). With the Blessing of the Luxons active, you can earn 140-160 points, in addition to the 400 point reward for completing the quest. This translates to roughly 11,000 points per hour.

The quest can be completed in 2 minutes if all party members cast Recall on a single runner starting from Jade Flats. Since the enemies along the route to the arena do not possess snares, this allows the runner to shave a minute of time.
Sometimes the enemy party will not turn hostile at all or it may take a substantial amount of time.
If you are killed and returned to the resurrection shrine, the enemies sometimes will not attack, using only healing skills. The monks will still attempt to heal their teammates.

quests/quest:gww:10713/sections/objectiv.text: Travel to the Jade Quarry and speak to Kommandant Durheim.

quests/quest:gww:10713/sections/walkthro.text: Starting from House zu Heltzer, head southeast through Ferndale to reach Lutgardis Conservatory. Then proceed northeast through Melandru's Hope, and eventually you will reach your destination. Talk to Kommandant Durheim for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:18610/sections/objectiv.text: Travel to the Jade Quarry and speak to Erek.

quests/quest:gww:18610/sections/walkthro.text: Leaving from Cavalon, travel south by southwest through Archipelagos until you reach the Jade Flats (Luxon), then head into the next outpost.

quests/quest:gww:70229/sections/objectiv.text: Speak to Justiciar Naveed when you are ready to face the White Mantle.

quests/quest:gww:70229/sections/walkthro.text: You will be in an explorable version of Tarnished Haven with Justiciar Naveed.

Fairly large groups of White Mantle will come from the southern portal. A second group will come as soon as you finish off the first group, and so on. There are 7 waves. Don't be discouraged, as these Mantle will be fairly easy to kill. Focus your fire on the White Mantle Priests and stay clear of the Searing Heat cast by White Mantle Savants. When all the groups are dead, Lazarus the Dire will come forth. You do not need to fight him, just watch the confrontation between him and the justiciar.

quests/quest:gww:70229/sections/notes-1/.text: It is possible to go through the portal to Alcazia Tangle and explore the whole area without interference from the regular foes.

quests/quest:gww:25421/sections/objectiv.text: Find and kill the Kaguchi brothers.
See Headmaster Zhan for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:25421/sections/walkthro.text: Journeying from Tsumei Village, head to the western side of Panjiang Peninsula. The Kaguchi brothers can be found just north of Pei the Skull Blade's ship.

quests/quest:gww:12000/sections/objectiv.text: Gather a party in Ascalon City. Sir Tydus recommends bringing Alesia to heal you.
Go to Old Ascalon. Deliver the royal message to Ambassador Zain.

quests/quest:gww:12000/sections/rewards-.text: War Hammer (has the skin of a Foehammer)

quests/quest:gww:12000/sections/walkthro.text: Invite at least one player or henchman to your party before stepping through the portal into Old Ascalon. Head straight east toward a small Krytan camp ahead. Beware of the two Devourers that pop up from the ground next to the bridge if you get too close to them. If you're a warrior, you can easily pick up quests from Warmaster Grast who is on the route of this quest (just past the bridge).

quests/quest:gww:12000/sections/notes-1/.text: Forming any group anywhere in the game completes the first objective, despite what the the quest suggests.
This objective becomes active again if you leave your group at any point in the future. You must face Ambassador Zain in a group if you wish to proceed with the quest.
Prince Rurik will not appear for his dialogue with Ambassador Zain if any member of the party is a non-Prophecies character or has already completed the quest.

quests/quest:gww:25351/sections/objectiv.text: Travel to Frontier Gate and speak with Warmaster Riga.
Travel to the Eastern Frontier to aid King Adelbern against the Titans.

quests/quest:gww:25351/sections/walkthro.text: Because of the high level charr and low level henchmen, it is best to either go with other players or with heroes. Also, due to the small party size, the party must be well balanced.

The quest itself is straightforward. Walk out the gate and a short distance (through a few Charr groups) to find King Adelbern, one Adelbern's Priest and two Adelbern's Guards rushing towards a group of Charr. They are low level Charr and no threat, but after the elimination of that group the Armageddon Lords will start to arrive, one at a time. Each one will be accompanied with some regular Charr and some Charr lords. The groups increase in difficulty; at first there will be only one Charr lord, then two, then two including a healer and then three Charr lords. The final group will have two Armageddon Lords together.

In general, you need to watch the composition of the incoming enemies. If there are any Spark of the Titans, take them down as fast as you can; they have the potential to deal a large amount of damage to the party. Next on the list are the Charr Lord casters — Charr Shaman Lord, Charr Flame Lord, Charr Mind Lord, and Charr Ashen Lord. Turn your attention to any Charr Axe Lords and Charr Stalker Lords before tackling the Armageddon Lord. You can pretty much ignore the regular level 8 or 9 Charr, as they usually die to any AoE damage when you're attacking the Charr Lords.

Another strategy is to kill the Sparks, the Armageddon and their spawns, avoiding killing one or two Charr casters, who do considerably less damage. Since the next enemy wave won't approach until all the charr in the previous group are dead, by keeping them alive you can buy some time to heal and regenerate energy with little pressure before facing a new wave.

Always attempt to intercept the incoming groups well ahead of King Adelbern and always protect Adelbern's Priest. Losing the priest ally will most assuredly put too much pressure on the single monk in the party.
Tips
If possible, bring cold damage. Cold damage deals heavy damage against the Titans.
Bringing Winter is a better alternative as Adelbern and his guards use Fiery Dragon Swords.
Likewise, Area of Effect skills like traps are helpful as the groups are often close together and come from the same direction.

Elementalist equiped with Water spells are also extremely useful. Ice Spikes and Maelstrom can do cold damage and slow down the enemy advance while Mist Form and Swirling Aura can give your party additional healing, taking some pressure off of the primary healer
Both Ward Against Harm and Mantra of Flame are helpful in reducing damage.
Try to keep the NPCs alive as long as possible, as they greatly help.
Morale Boosts and Holy Blessing can be acquired from the statue of Lyssa west of Adelbern's group.
If you fail this quest, your entire party, no matter its size, will be sent to Frontier Gate intact as long as you did not bring henchmen that are not available in said outpost.
Rebel Yell helps with the Charr encountered during this quest.
It is possible to kill three of the Armageddon Lord groups without spawning King Adelbern's group by approaching the Titans from the south on the eastern side.
By flagging heroes, it is possible to kill all five Armageddon Lord groups without spawning King Adelbern's group. See the talk page for a map.
Because the Armageddon Lords are melee casters, it is advisable to bring a tank with good fire or elemental protection.

If you do not have any heroes and cannot find players to help you, it is possible to leave in hard mode so that you have level 20 henchmen and, except for the low level Charr, the enemies are not boosted very much.
Running from Yak's Bend for a party of 6, or from Temple of the Ages for a party of 8 is possible.

quests/quest:gww:25351/sections/notes-1/.text: Each group after the first starts to approach once all the original members of the previous group are killed, regardless of whether or not Risen Ashen Hulks, Fists of the Titans or Hands of the Titans are still alive.

If you kill all the titan groups (which will be updated if you kill the last Armageddon Lord) and King Adelbern dies, you will be sent back to Frontier Gate, but you'll only have to reach Adelbern again and speak with him, then you will be able to take the reward at Glint's Vision.
Even if one person hasn't talked to Warmaster Riga yet, as long as someone in your party did so, everyone who has the quest in their log can complete it.
If you approach the king from the north or west, he will run to the blue dot as soon as he spawns.
With this quest, a Charr lord or two might spawn inside one of the cliffs. Such a spawn obstructs weapons, but can still be killed with ranged skills.

Warning: In contrast to most other quests that require you to protect an NPC, Adelbern's death will lead to you immediately travelling back to your last visited outpost. Especially groups arriving from Yak's Bend or Temple of the Ages should be very careful with regards to Adelbern's survival.

quests/quest:gww:281225/sections/objecti.text: Travel to Frontier Gate and speak with Warmaster Riga.
Travel to the Eastern Frontier to aid King Adelbern against the Titans.

quests/quest:gww:281225/sections/walkthr.text: Ideally, come from the south, keeping east of Adelbern's trigger circle. Kill the eastern-most group first. Work your way counter-clockwise for groups 2 and 3. For the last of the northern groups, use only one hero to pull them closer to you by carefully flagging the hero, while keeping the rest of your party back with you. As soon as the hero gets attacked, pull them back to you. If the hero should die, use another hero to ressurect them. Finally, backtrack towards the 5th and last group to the crossroad. Careful pulling should also be used for enemies between you and the last group.
If possible, bring cold damage as it deals better damage against the Titans.
Bringing Winter is highly recommended as Adelbern and his guards use Fiery Dragon Swords.

It is possible to kill three of the five Armageddon Lord groups before King Adelbern spawns by coming from the south and attacking the easternmost groups first. Using heroes for pulling, all five groups can be killed.
A Soul Twisting Ritualist with protective spirits or a Protection Prayers Monk are necessary because of the Armageddon Lords' high damage output.
Buffs that mitigate elemental or fire damage, such as Ward Against Harm and Mantra of Flame, are recommended.
Avoid melee distance with Armageddon Lords if possible. If not, be sure to bring good defense against elemental or fire damage.
Avoid using builds that rely on long recharging enchantments.
Adelbern is great at soaking up damage, so using him to tank can be helpful.
Rebel Yell helps with fighting the Charr in this quest.

quests/quest:gww:281225/sections/notes-1.text: Each group after the first starts to approach once all the original members of the previous group are killed, regardless of whether or not Risen Ashen Hulks, Fists of the Titans or Arms of the Titans are still alive.

quests/quest:gww:70268/sections/objectiv.text: See Veth the Storyteller for your reward.

quests/quest:gww:70268/sections/walkthro.text: General tips
This quest automatically appears in your quest log when entering the dungeon.
Quest progress is saved even when exiting the dungeon. This allows you to modify your party's build(s) for each boss, if required.

Unlike most dungeons, Slavers' Exile is not linear, and you can kill the first four bosses in any order. The initial room leads directly to each sub-level, with Duncan's room opening once the others are complete.
You don't need to defeat all of the bosses in Hard Mode to get the Hard Mode page for the dungeon book, only Duncan.
If striving to complete all the sub-quests in one go, consider bringing a few Identification Kits. There is a Weaponsmith in the main area to whom you can sell your items.
Most of the Stone Summit have some type of resurrection skill, consider bringing Frozen Soil.
Justiciar Thommis' level

There are two bosses on this level, Justiciar Thommis, and Rand Stormweaver. It is recommended to do both during the same run, otherwise the exit will be blocked. The main difficulty is the large number of Dwarves that tend to aggro at the same time. Be prepared to do hit and run, or to manage large groups.
Selvetarm's level

Aside from large groups of Dwarves (see above), there are three additional difficulties here. (1) Some places have chained clerics and reavers popups, which may overwhelm groups already engaged in a fight. Pulling is recommended, as well as tactical retreats. (2) At the door right before the boss, there are popups. Each time you kill them, a larger groups spawns. There are a limited number of groups, but unprepared groups may suffer a wipe. Pulling is recommended to avoid the new group appearing on top of you. Also, these use life-stealing skills. Focus fire and general caster-shutdown is recommended against them. (3) Selvetarm and his group use Jagged Bones and Death Nova to produce a self-renewing supply of undead bombs. Using Verata skills to steal his minions will help, or some form of spike AoE damage such as splinter barrage.
Forgewight's level
Enemies primarily consist of large groups of fire elementals and large groups of Stone Summit.

A general strategy against this is to have a dedicated Tank/Aggro manager, a Protection or bonder monk, and a few AoE damagers. Cast protective spells on tank, have them hold the aggro, then do as much AoE damage as possible to thin out the group. A ranger with Frozen Soil is highly recommended against Stone Summit to prevent resurrection, and Gaze of Fury to remove spirits when needed.
Duncan the Black's level

The mobs in this area are composed entirely of Stone Summit and Restless Dead popups. The Restless Dead use Vampiric Touch and Vampiric Bite quite a bit, which can be countered with "Can't Touch This!". Refer to the other sections for skills and tactics to counter Summit dwarves.
Duncan the Black awaits in a large room full of Restless Dead popups. Sweeping the room to popup and killing all foes makes the following fight easier.

When approaching Duncan, several groups of Spirits will appear. Not only will these spirits damage, blind and disenchant you, several of Duncan's skills profit from having a spirit within earshot as well. These spirits will respawn when killed, but it is possible to move them away using Swap before engaging Duncan.

Duncan himself uses Duncan's Defense, which deals twice the damage he takes back to you. Don't damage him too quickly, or your healers will struggle to keep you alive. This can be circumvented by using life stealing or health loss instead of damage. Due to his large amount of health, Spoil Victor works great.
Once Duncan is dead, the spirits will disappear.

quests/quest:gww:70268/sections/notes-1/.text: You can leave the dungeon at any time between completing the rooms of the bosses. The game records any killed bosses as killed in the quest log. The log will not be reset.
This quest also rewards 5000 Norn reputation points for first time completion. 2500 Norn reputation are awarded upon repeat.

To gain access to Duncan's dungeon, all party members must kill the preceding four bosses Justiciar Thommis, Rand Stormweaver, Selvetarm and Forgewight as shown in The Last Hierophant quest. The 4 "defeat" lines must be crossed off leaving only "Destroy Duncan the Black" left undone. This situation is frequently abbreviated "4/5". Once you have completed the quest, you will need to retake it and kill the other bosses before you can face Duncan again.

quests/quest:gww:25500/sections/objectiv.text: Find Farmer Dirk's last remaining Prize-Winning Hog and chase it back to him.
Return to Farmer Dirk for your reward.
